label: German Expressionism
defn: A film of the Weimar Expressionist movement: painted, distorted décor, chiaroscuro and stylised acting expressing inner states (The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Nosferatu, Metropolis). Later Expressionist-influenced genre films go to their genre (A4 Horror).

label: French Impressionist Cinema
defn: A film of the 1919–1929 French avant-garde narrative school (Gance, Epstein, Dulac) using rhythmic montage and subjective optical effects to render feeling (J'accuse!, Napoleon, The Fall of the House of Usher).

label: Soviet Montage
defn: A Soviet silent film built on montage theory, meaning made by the collision of shots (Battleship Potemkin, Strike, Earth). Vertov's documentary Man with a Movie Camera sits in A19-3.

label: Poetic Realism
defn: A 1930s French film of fatalistic working-class romance in studio-built, mist-laden settings (Port of Shadows, L'Atalante, Daybreak).

label: Italian Neorealism
defn: A postwar Italian film shot on location with non-professional actors about poverty and reconstruction (Bicycle Thieves, Rome, Open City, Umberto D.).

label: Parallel Cinema
defn: An Indian art-cinema film of the realist, non-commercial alternative to the mainstream, from Ray and Ghatak onward (Pather Panchali, Charulata, The Cloud-Capped Star). Popular Hindi cinema goes to A18.

label: Polish Film School
defn: A Polish film of 1955–1961 reckoning with war and resistance (Ashes and Diamonds, Kanal, A Generation).

label: French New Wave
secs: 1=Forerunners & First Features (1956–1959) | 2=High Period (1960–1964) | 3=Late & Politicised Films (1965–1968)
defn: A film by the late-1950s/1960s Cahiers-generation directors breaking classical continuity: location shooting, jump cuts, cinephile reference (The 400 Blows, Breathless, Jules and Jim). The Resnais–Marker–Varda wing with literary modernist leanings goes to A1-9.

label: Left Bank
defn: A film of the Rive Gauche group (Resnais, Marker, Varda, Duras) joining literary modernism to fractured memory and time (Hiroshima Mon Amour, Last Year at Marienbad, Muriel).

label: British New Wave
defn: A British film of c.1959–1970 adapting kitchen-sink realism to working-class lives in the industrial North (Saturday Night and Sunday Morning, A Taste of Honey, Kes).

label: Japanese New Wave
defn: A Japanese film of the 1960s–70s nūberu bāgu breaking with studio humanism through sex, politics and formal rupture (Death by Hanging, Woman in the Dunes, The Insect Woman).

label: Czechoslovak New Wave
defn: A Czechoslovak film of 1963–1970 using absurdist humour, surreal fantasy or non-professional realism against official culture (Daisies, Closely Watched Trains, The Firemen's Ball).

label: Yugoslav Black Wave
defn: A Yugoslav film of the 1960s–early 1970s whose dark, sexually frank critique of socialist society drew censure (WR: Mysteries of the Organism, I Even Met Happy Gypsies, Early Works).

label: Portuguese New Cinema
defn: A film of the 1960s Novo Cinema in Portugal, modernist breaks with the Estado Novo studio tradition (The Green Years, Change of Life).

label: New German Cinema
defn: A West German film of the 1960s–early 1980s auteur renewal after the Oberhausen Manifesto (Aguirre, the Wrath of God, Fear Eats the Soul, Kings of the Road).

label: Cinema Novo
defn: A Brazilian film of the 1960s movement of "an idea in the head and a camera in the hand", poverty, violence and myth in the sertão (Black God, White Devil, Barren Lives, Entranced Earth).

label: Cinema Marginal
defn: A Brazilian underground film of the late 1960s, a trash-aesthetic, anarchic reply to Cinema Novo (The Red Light Bandit).

label: Third Cinema
defn: A militant anti-colonial film of the Latin American, African and Arab "third cinema" manifesto against Hollywood and auteur cinema (The Battle of Algiers, Memories of Underdevelopment, Blood of the Condor). Its militant documentaries sit in A19.

label: New American Cinema
defn: A New York independent film of the late-1950s/1960s New American Cinema Group, improvised and anti-Hollywood (Shadows, The Cool World). Its underground and diary films sit in A20-2 and A19-5.

label: New Hollywood
secs: 1=Counterculture & Youth Films | 2=Revisionist Crime & Gangster Films | 3=Paranoia, Horror & Suspense | 4=Character Studies & Ensemble Films | 5=Vietnam & Late Epics | 6=The Blockbuster Turn
defn: An American studio-era film of 1967–1980 made by the auteur generation that took over Hollywood, with downbeat endings, sex, violence and European influence (Bonnie and Clyde, Taxi Driver, Nashville, Jaws).

label: L.A. Rebellion
defn: A film by the Black filmmakers of UCLA's 1967–1990s L.A. School, neorealist and Third Cinema-informed (Killer of Sheep, Daughters of the Dust, Bush Mama).

label: No Wave Cinema
defn: A late-1970s/1980s Lower East Side underground film, punk, Super 8 or 16mm, deadpan (Stranger Than Paradise, Permanent Vacation, Born in Flames).

label: Australian New Wave
defn: An Australian film of the 1970s–early 1980s revival, landscape-haunted and period-set (Picnic at Hanging Rock, Wake in Fright, Breaker Morant).

label: Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema
defn: A Filipino film of the 1970s–early 1980s auteur renaissance under martial law (Manila in the Claws of Light, Insiang, Oro, Plata, Mata).

label: Cinema of Moral Anxiety
defn: A Polish film of 1976–1981 probing compromise and corruption in socialist life (Camera Buff, Man of Iron, Blind Chance).

label: Iranian New Wave
defn: An Iranian art film from the late 1960s onward, often child-centred, reflexive and near-documentary (Close-Up, Taste of Cherry, The White Balloon, A Separation).

label: Taiwan New Cinema
defn: A Taiwanese film of the 1980s–90s movement of long takes and historical memory (A City of Sadness, Yi Yi, A Brighter Summer Day).

label: Hong Kong New Wave
defn: A Hong Kong film of the late-1970s/1980s new wave and its second wave (Boat People, Rouge, Chungking Express).

label: Fifth Generation
defn: A mainland Chinese film by the 1982 Beijing Film Academy graduates, allegorical and visually lavish (Yellow Earth, Red Sorghum, Farewell My Concubine).

label: Sixth Generation
defn: A mainland Chinese film of the 1990s–2000s urban, semi-underground generation (Platform, Suzhou River, Still Life).

label: Cinéma du look
defn: A 1980s French film of glossy, youth-oriented, music-video visual style (Diva, Subway, Betty Blue).

label: New Queer Cinema
defn: An early-1990s independent queer film, defiant and formally transgressive in the AIDS era (Poison, My Own Private Idaho, The Living End).

label: New Argentine Cinema
defn: An Argentine film of the 1990s–2000s renewal, minimalist and observational (The Swamp, Pizza, Beer, and Cigarettes, Los Muertos).

label: Dogme 95
defn: A film certified under the Dogme 95 "vow of chastity": handheld, location sound, no added lighting or score (The Celebration, The Idiots, Julien Donkey-Boy).

label: Mumblecore
defn: A 2000s–2010s American micro-budget film of improvised talk among twenty-somethings (Funny Ha Ha, Drinking Buddies, Tiny Furniture).

label: Berlin School
defn: A German art film of the 1990s–2010s Berliner Schule, restrained and observational (Yella, Everyone Else, Toni Erdmann).

label: Romanian New Wave
defn: A Romanian film of the 2000s onward, long-take realist dramas of post-communist bureaucracy and morality (The Death of Mr. Lazarescu, 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Police, Adjective).

label: Greek Weird Wave
defn: A Greek film of the 2009–2010s crisis-era wave of deadpan, absurdist family and social allegory (Dogtooth, Attenberg, Alps).

label: Slow Cinema
secs: 1=European Modernist Precursors | 2=Later European Slow Cinema | 3=Taiwanese & Southeast Asian Slow Cinema | 4=Turkish Slow Cinema | 5=Iberian & Latin American Slow Cinema
defn: A narrative art film whose defining device is duration: very long takes, minimal action, contemplative observation (Jeanne Dielman, Sátántangó, Stalker, Uncle Boonmee). National movements with a slow strand (Taiwan New Cinema, Romanian New Wave) keep their own leaf.

label: Free Cinema
defn: The British documentary movement of 1956–1959 (Lindsay Anderson, Karel Reisz, Tony Richardson, Lorenza Mazzetti) whose six National Film Theatre programmes showed unscripted, personal films of working-class leisure and labour (O Dreamland, Every Day Except Christmas). Its directors went on to the British New Wave (A1-10).

label: Ukrainian Poetic Cinema
defn: The Kyiv (Dovzhenko Studio) school of the mid-1960s to late 1970s — Parajanov, Ilyenko, Osyka, Ivchenko, Mykolaichuk — making folkloric, painterly, ritual-saturated films of Ukrainian village and legend (Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors, The White Bird Marked with Black).

label: Korean New Wave
defn: The South Korean art cinema of c. 1987–1996 (Park Kwang-su, Jang Sun-woo, Lee Myung-se, Park Jong-won) that, after democratisation, turned realist and modernist means on division, labour and the Gwangju massacre (Chilsu and Mansu, A Petal, A Single Spark); it precedes the commercial Korean Wave of the 2000s.

label: Thai New Wave
defn: The revival of Thai cinema from 1997 by directors from advertising and music video — Pen-Ek Ratanaruang, Nonzee Nimibutr, Wisit Sasanatieng, the Pang brothers — mixing pastiche, colour stylisation and genre (Tears of the Black Tiger, 6ixtynin9, Monrak Transistor).

label: Nuevo Cine Mexicano
defn: The 1990s–2000s renewal of Mexican cinema (Arturo Ripstein's late films, María Novaro, Jorge Fons, Alfonso Cuarón, Alejandro González Iñárritu, Antonio Serrano) after the IMCINE reforms: urban, frank, internationally co-produced films (Danzón, Midaq Alley, Y tu mamá también).

label: Cinema of Transgression
defn: Nick Zedd's 1985 name for the New York Lower East Side Super-8 underground (Zedd, Richard Kern, Lydia Lunch, Tessa Hughes-Freeland) of deliberately shocking, punk, sexually and violently taboo films (Fingered, They Eat Scum).

label: Gangster Film
secs: 1=Classical Gangster Cycle | 2=Mafia & Mob Saga | 3=Crime-Boss Rise and Fall | 4=British Gangster Film | 5=European Underworld Film | 6=South Indian Gangster Film | 7=Triad & East Asian Gangster Film
defn: A film whose protagonist is a member or boss of a criminal organisation and whose story is the gang's rise, wars and fall (Little Caesar, Once Upon a Time in America, Gomorrah, Vada Chennai). Hindi-language underworld films go to A2-2 Mumbai Noir, Japanese ones to A2-3; a film that follows the police against the mob goes to A2-15/A2-16.

label: Mumbai Noir
defn: A Hindi-language film of the Bombay underworld (or its Shakespearean transpositions to the gangland of the Hindi heartland), shot in a realist, violent register (Satya, Maqbool, Omkara). South Indian gangster sagas stay in A2-1.

label: Yakuza Film
secs: 1=Early & Post-War Yakuza Films | 2=Borderless Action & Ninkyō Eiga (1959–1972) | 3=Jitsuroku Eiga (1973–1980s) | 4=V-Cinema & the Auteur Yakuza Film (1989–) | 5=Yakuza Films Made Abroad
defn: A film about the Japanese yakuza, from the ninkyo chivalry films through Fukasaku's jitsuroku and Kitano's deadpan cycle (Battles Without Honor and Humanity, Sonatine, Outrage).

label: Poliziottesco
defn: An Italian crime-action film of the 1970s cycle of violent cops, mobsters and kidnappers (Caliber 9, Rabid Dogs).

label: Hitman Film
defn: A film whose protagonist is a professional killer and whose drama is the contract, its code and its cost (The Mechanic, Ghost Dog, The American, The Killer). Stylised existential killers of the Melville line sit in A2-25 Neo-Noir.

label: Drug Film
secs: 1=Cartel & Trafficking Film (Narco Film) | 2=Dealer's-World Film | 3=Addiction Crime Film
defn: A crime film whose engine is the illegal drug trade or drug addiction: cartels and mules, the dealer's world, the junkie's crimes (Traffic, Maria Full of Grace, Pusher, Drugstore Cowboy).

label: Blaxploitation
defn: A 1970s American exploitation film made for Black urban audiences, with Black heroes against the Man, pimps and pushers (Shaft, Super Fly, Coffy), including its horror and Afrofuturist offshoots.

label: Hood Film
defn: An African-American (or Caribbean, Latino and Black British) film of street life, gangs and drugs in the inner-city neighbourhood (Boyz n the Hood, Menace II Society, Kidulthood).

label: Cine Quinqui
defn: A Spanish film of the late-1970s/80s cycle about juvenile delinquents of the urban periphery, often cast with real delinquents (Deprisa, Deprisa).

label: Pinky Violence
defn: A 1970s Toei exploitation film of female gangs and avenging women prisoners (Female Prisoner #701: Scorpion).

label: Heist Film
secs: 1=Classic Caper | 2=Ensemble Caper | 3=Robbery Gone Wrong | 4=Professional-Thief Film | 5=Heist Action Spectacle | 6=Heist Comedy
defn: A film built around planning and executing a robbery, told from the thieves' side (Rififi, Ocean's Eleven, Heat, Reservoir Dogs). A swindle with no break-in goes to A2-12; a standoff with hostages to A3-12.

label: Con-Artist Film
defn: A film whose engine is a confidence trick: grifters, swindlers and the marks they play, often with a twist that cons the viewer (Nine Queens, House of Games, The Grifters, Focus).

label: White-Collar Crime Film
defn: A film about crime committed by the respectable in suits: fraud, embezzlement, financial and corporate crime (Wall Street, Boiler Room, Arbitrage, Lord of War).

label: Gambling Film
defn: A crime film whose world is the gambling table and the debt it creates (Rounders, Croupier, Uncut Gems, Hard Eight).

label: Police Procedural
secs: 1=Homicide Investigation | 2=Rural & Small-Town Investigation | 3=Federal Investigation
defn: A film that follows police or federal investigators working a case step by step, its drama in the method of the inquiry (Stray Dog, The Night of the 12th, In the Heat of the Night, Mississippi Burning). A hunt for a serial killer goes to A3-6; a film about the cop's own conduct goes to A2-16.

label: Police Film
secs: 1=Maverick Cop | 2=Police Corruption | 3=Undercover Cop | 4=Street Unit & Tactical Police
defn: A film whose subject is the police officer rather than the case: the rule-breaking maverick, the corrupt cop, the undercover cop, the beat or tactical unit (Dirty Harry, Training Day, Infernal Affairs, Elite Squad).

label: Nordic Noir
defn: A Scandinavian crime film in the bleak, procedural, socially critical Nordic-noir manner (The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, Department Q, Insomnia 1997).

label: Private-Eye Film
defn: A film whose investigator is a private detective outside the noir canon: modern and comic private eyes and gentleman sleuths (Harper, Gone Baby Gone, Detective Byomkesh Bakshy!, Veronica Mars). Classic hardboiled eyes go to A2-24 and A2-25; closed-circle puzzles to A3-1.

label: Prison Film
secs: 1=Prison-Escape Film | 2=Inside-Life Prison Drama | 3=Prison Action Film | 4=Political & Wartime Prison Film
defn: A film set inside a prison whose drama is incarceration itself: escape, survival among inmates, guard and riot (The Shawshank Redemption, Escape from Alcatraz, A Prophet, A Man Escaped).

label: Legal Drama
defn: A film whose drama runs through the legal process: trial, appeal, jury and death row (The Third Murder, The Life of David Gale, The Juror).

label: True-Crime Film
secs: 1=Killer Portrait | 2=Abduction & Captivity | 3=Notorious Case | 4=Hustle & Swindle
defn: A dramatisation of a real crime case, centred on the criminal, the victim or the case itself rather than on a fictional investigation (In Cold Blood, 10 Rillington Place, Snowtown, Killers of the Flower Moon).

label: Social Problem Film
secs: 1=Juvenile Delinquency Film | 2=Street-Gang & Hooligan Film | 3=Slum & Favela Crime Film | 4=Desperation Crime Drama | 5=Vice Exposé
defn: A crime film that presents crime as the product of a social condition, youth, gangs, slum, poverty or vice, rather than as a genre puzzle (The Young and the Damned, City of God, Pickpocket, A Touch of Sin).

label: Lovers-on-the-Run Film
defn: A film of a criminal couple in flight from the law, the outlaw road movie of Bonnie and Clyde (You Only Live Once, Breathless 1983, True Romance, Ain't Them Bodies Saints).

label: Film Noir
secs: 1=American Noir: Wartime Phase (1940–1945) | 2=American Noir: Post-War Phase (1946–1949) | 3=American Noir: Late Phase (1950–1962) | 4=British Noir | 5=French Noir & Poetic-Realist Precursors | 6=Italian & Other European Noir | 7=Japanese Noir (Nikkatsu & Studio Noir) | 8=Latin American Noir (Argentina & Mexico)
defn: A crime film of the classical noir period (c.1940–1960), and its pre-war precursors and contemporaries abroad, with fatalistic, shadowed visual style and doomed protagonists (Double Indemnity, Out of the Past, The Asphalt Jungle, Touchez pas au grisbi). Post-classical noir goes to A2-25.

label: Neo-Noir
secs: 1=Neo-Noir Private Eye | 2=Femme-Fatale Neo-Noir | 3=Country Noir | 4=Professional-Criminal Neo-Noir | 5=Payback Neo-Noir | 6=Surreal & Dream Noir | 7=Korean Noir | 8=Chinese-Language Noir | 9=Neo-Noir Pastiche
defn: A post-classical crime film that revives noir's fatalism, moral ambiguity and stylisation (Chinatown, Blood Simple, Le Samouraï, Drive). Classical-period noir goes to A2-24.

label: Crime Comedy
defn: A crime film played for laughs: bungling crooks and mob farce (The Pope of Greenwich Village, Amateur, Caught Stealing). Comic heists stay in A2-11; most crime comedies are in A12 Comedy.

label: Whodunit
secs: 1=Classical Detective Mystery | 2=Closed-Circle Mystery | 3=Comic Whodunit | 4=Contemporary Murder Mystery | 5=Twist-Puzzle Mystery
defn: A mystery whose engine is the fair-play puzzle of which suspect committed the murder, solved by a detective (Murder on the Orient Express, Gosford Park, Knives Out). Inquiries by police squads go to A2-15.

label: Inverted Detective Story
defn: A crime story that shows the murder and the murderer first, its suspense in the cover-up and the investigator closing in (Drishyam, Match Point, A Hard Day, Dial M for Murder).

label: Mystery Film
secs: 1=Disappearance Mystery | 2=Buried-Past Mystery | 3=Esoteric Puzzle Mystery | 4=Art-Film Enigma
defn: A mystery whose enigma is not a murder puzzle but a disappearance, a buried past or a riddle, pursued by an ordinary person (Bunny Lake Is Missing, A Simple Favor, The Da Vinci Code, Blow-Up).

label: Krimi
secs: 1=Rialto Edgar Wallace Series (1959–1972) | 2=Dr. Mabuse Revival (1960–1964) | 3=Bryan Edgar Wallace & Other Krimis
defn: A West German Edgar Wallace (or Bryan Edgar Wallace) crime-mystery film of the 1959–1972 Rialto cycle (Face of the Frog).

label: Giallo
secs: 1=Mario Bava | 2=Dario Argento | 3=Lucio Fulci | 4=Sergio Martino | 5=Other Gialli of the Classic Cycle (1968–1982) | 6=Late Gialli & Neo-Giallo
defn: An Italian murder-mystery thriller of the 1960s–80s cycle: black-gloved killer, stylised set-piece murders, amateur sleuth (Blood and Black Lace, The Bird with the Crystal Plumage, Deep Red).

label: Serial-Killer Thriller
secs: 1=Manhunt Thriller | 2=Killer's-Eye Thriller | 3=Witness & Survivor Thriller
defn: A thriller whose engine is a serial or spree killer, followed by the hunter, the killer himself or the survivor (The Silence of the Lambs, Zodiac, The Chaser). Dramatised portraits of real killers go to A2-21.

label: Psychological Thriller
secs: 1=Unreliable Mind & Breakdown | 2=Doppelgänger & Double | 3=Amnesia & Lost Identity | 4=Obsession & Fixation | 5=Impostor & Assumed Identity | 6=Manipulation & Mind Game
defn: A thriller whose threat comes from the mind: a protagonist's unstable perception, a double, lost memory, obsession or a mind game played on them (Vertigo, Memento, Black Swan, Shutter Island). Threats from spouse, family or lodger go to A3-8.

label: Domestic Thriller
secs: 1=Marriage Thriller | 2=Intruder from Hell | 3=Stalker Thriller | 4=Family-Secret Thriller
defn: A thriller whose danger lives in the home and its intimacies: the murderous spouse, the intruder who moves in, the stalker, the poisoned family (Gaslight, Sleeping with the Enemy, The Hand That Rocks the Cradle, Single White Female). Desire-driven danger goes to A3-9..

label: Erotic Thriller
secs: 1=Femme-Fatale Erotic Thriller | 2=Obsessive-Affair Thriller | 3=Voyeur Thriller | 4=Art-House Erotic Thriller | 5=Sexual-Power Thriller
defn: A thriller in which sexual desire is the engine of danger and crime (Body Heat, Fatal Attraction, Basic Instinct, The Handmaiden).

label: Revenge Thriller
secs: 1=Korean Revenge Thriller | 2=Vigilante Film | 3=Rape-and-Revenge Film | 4=Vendetta Thriller | 5=Revenge Action Thriller
defn: A thriller whose engine is the protagonist's vengeance for a wrong (Death Wish, Oldboy, I Spit on Your Grave, Blue Ruin).

label: Kidnapping Thriller
secs: 1=Ransom Kidnapping | 2=Abduction & Search | 3=Captivity Thriller
defn: A thriller whose engine is an abduction: the ransom demand, the frantic search, or the captive's ordeal (High and Low, Ransom, Prisoners, Misery).

label: Hostage & Siege Thriller
secs: 1=Hostage Standoff | 2=Siege Film | 3=Hijacking & In-Transit Thriller
defn: A thriller of a standoff: hostages taken, a building besieged, a plane or train hijacked (The Negotiator, Toy Soldiers, Captain Phillips, The Taking of Pelham One Two Three).

label: Home-Invasion Thriller
defn: A thriller in which intruders break into a home and hold or hunt its occupants (Panic Room, Cold Creek Manor, Borgman).

label: Survival Thriller
secs: 1=Wilderness Survival | 2=Road & Pursuit Terror | 3=Sea & River Survival | 4=Trapped & Confined | 5=Escape from Unrest
defn: A thriller of staying alive against nature, a pursuer or a trap (Deliverance, Duel, Buried, Alive).

label: Death Game Film
defn: A film in which people are forced into a lethal game or contest with rules (Battle Royale, The Hunger Games, Cube, Escape Room), including the human hunt of The Most Dangerous Game.

label: Real-Time Thriller
defn: A thriller whose suspense depends on unfolding in (near) real time in a confined frame, a phone line, a screen or a race against the clock (Phone Booth, The Guilty, Run Lola Run, Profile).

label: Wrong-Man Thriller
defn: A Hitchcockian thriller of an innocent accused or mistaken for someone else, who must flee and prove his innocence (The 39 Steps, North by Northwest, The Fugitive, Tell No One).

label: Conspiracy Thriller
secs: 1=Paranoid Thriller | 2=Corporate & Whistleblower Thriller | 3=Investigative-Journalism Thriller | 4=Government Cover-Up
defn: A thriller in which the protagonist uncovers a hidden plot by the powerful, the state, corporations or secret societies (The Parallax View, All the President's Men, The Insider, Enemy of the State).

label: Political Thriller
secs: 1=Assassination Thriller | 2=Terrorism & Counter-Terror | 3=Military & Nuclear Crisis | 4=Dictatorship & Repression | 5=Power & Political Intrigue
defn: A thriller whose stakes are political power itself: assassination, terrorism, military crisis, dictatorship, intrigue (Z, The Day of the Jackal, The Lives of Others, Conclave).

label: Techno-Thriller
defn: A thriller whose engine is a technology: hacking, surveillance, AI, computer crime (The Net, Blackhat, Eagle Eye, Who Am I).

label: Spy Film
secs: 1=Wartime Espionage | 2=Cold War Espionage | 3=Spy-Action Franchise | 4=Covert-Operation Film | 5=Modern Intelligence Thriller | 6=Inter-Korean Espionage Film | 7=Eurospy (1964–1968)
defn: A film about espionage: agents, moles and covert operations for a state (Notorious, The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, Dr. No, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy).

label: Ghost Film
secs: 1=Classic, Literary & Fairy-Tale Ghost Stories | 2=Vengeful Spirits & Bogeys | 3=Ghost-Seers, Mediums & Séances | 4=Ghost Ships, Battlefields & Place-Bound Spirits
defn: A horror film whose threat is the spirit of a dead person acting on the living, outside a single haunted dwelling (The Phantom Carriage, The Sixth Sense, Mama, The Devil's Backbone). A ghost bound to one house goes to the Haunted House Film; a Japanese onryō to J-Horror.

label: Haunted House Film
secs: 1=Classic Haunted House Films | 2=Family Hauntings & Poltergeists | 3=Paranormal Investigators & Demonologists | 4=Haunted Hotels, Schools & Institutions | 5=Grief, Guilt & Social Hauntings
defn: A horror film whose threat is a dwelling or building itself, haunted by presences that menace whoever lives in or visits it (The Haunting, Poltergeist, The Conjuring, The Shining). A house haunted by a single cursed Japanese spirit goes to A4-9 J-Horror.

label: Curse Film
secs: 1=Curses Laid & Passed On | 2=Urban Legends & Summoned Entities | 3=Cursed Objects, Games & Apps | 4=Death's-Design Films
defn: A horror film whose engine is a curse or rule-bound supernatural pursuit that is laid, summoned or passed on, so that knowing the rules is survival (It Follows, Candyman, Ouija, Final Destination). The Japanese curse cycle (Ringu) goes to A4-9 J-Horror.

label: Possession & Exorcism Film
secs: 1=The Exorcist Cycle | 2=Exorcist Procedurals & Priest Films | 3=Domestic & Child Possession | 4=Jinn, Dybbuk & Non-Christian Possession
defn: A horror film whose threat is a demon or spirit inhabiting a human body, usually met by an exorcism (The Exorcist III, The Rite, The Possession, Under the Shadow). A demon that besieges a house rather than a body goes to A4-2 or A4-5.

label: Satanic Film
secs: 1=Antichrist & Devil's-Child Films | 2=Satanic Cults & Covens | 3=The Devil Incarnate & Faustian Bargains | 4=Demonic Outbreaks & Deadites | 5=Hell, Cenobites & Otherworld Demons | 6=Angels & Apocalyptic Prophecy
defn: A horror film whose source of fear is Satan, his worshippers or the demonic hosts of Hell (The Omen, The Devil Rides Out, Hereditary, Hellraiser, The Evil Dead). A single possessed body goes to A4-4; nuns and convents to A4-6.

label: Religious Horror
defn: A horror film whose fear grows from faith itself: convents, saints, zealotry and sacred ritual (The Nun, Saint Maud, Immaculate, Alucarda). Exorcism plots go to A4-4; Satanist cults to A4-5.

label: Witchcraft Horror
secs: 1=Witches & Covens | 2=Black Magic, Sorcery & Ritual
defn: A horror film whose threat is a witch, a coven or a practitioner of black magic (Suspiria, The Craft, The Lords of Salem, The Boxer's Omen). Rural pagan communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.

label: Folk Horror
secs: 1=British & Irish Folk Horror | 2=Pagan Cults & Harvest Communities | 3=Forest & Wilderness Folklore | 4=World Folk Horror
defn: A horror film whose dread comes from a rural landscape, its old beliefs and the community that keeps them (The Wicker Man, Witchfinder General, Midsommar, The Witch). A witch in a modern city goes to A4-7.

label: J-Horror
secs: 1=Onryō & Curse Cycle | 2=Techno-Urban Dread | 3=Hollywood Remakes of Asian Horror
defn: The Japanese horror wave from the late 1990s, built on vengeful onryō, technology as a channel for the dead and urban isolation, plus its Hollywood remakes (Ringu, Ju-on: The Grudge, Pulse, The Ring). Pre-modern Japanese ghost tales go to A4-10 Kaidan Film.

label: Kaidan Film
defn: A Japanese film of a pre-modern ghost or supernatural tale in the kaidan tradition (Ugetsu, Kwaidan, Onibaba, Kuroneko).

label: Korean Horror
defn: A South Korean supernatural horror film drawing on shamanism, han and family guilt (A Tale of Two Sisters, The Wailing, Exhuma, Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum). Korean zombie films go to A4-18.

label: Thai Horror
defn: A Thai supernatural horror film built on phi spirits, Buddhist karma and village belief (Nang Nak, Shutter, The Medium, Death Whisperer). Thai horror-comedy goes to A4-38.

label: Indonesian Horror
defn: An Indonesian supernatural horror film drawn from local folklore, black magic (ilmu hitam) and Islamic belief, from the Suzzanna era to the 2010s revival (Satan's Slaves, Impetigore, Mystics in Bali, KKN di Desa Penari).

label: Jiangshi Film
defn: A Hong Kong horror-comedy of hopping corpses and the Taoist priests who fight them (Mr. Vampire). Kept as the named cycle; European vampires go to A4-16.

label: Gothic Horror
secs: 1=Silent & Early Sound Gothic | 2=Universal Classic Monsters | 3=Corman–Poe Cycle | 4=Hammer Horror | 5=Italian Gothic | 6=Gothic Revival & Period Pastiche
defn: A period horror film in the Gothic tradition of castles, ancestral curses and literary monsters, from Universal and Hammer to modern revivals (Frankenstein, Horror of Dracula, Black Sunday, Crimson Peak). Dracula and vampire films go to A4-16; werewolves to A4-17.

label: Vampire Film
secs: 1=Dracula & Nosferatu Films | 2=Art-House & Erotic Vampire Films | 3=Vampire Comedies | 4=Teen & Romantic Vampire Films | 5=Vampire Action & Hunters | 6=Vampire Sieges & Plagues
defn: A film whose monster is a blood-drinking undead, from Dracula adaptations to vampire comedies and action franchises (Nosferatu, Let the Right One In, The Lost Boys, Underworld). Hopping corpses go to A4-14 Jiangshi Film.

label: Werewolf & Shapeshifter Film
defn: A horror film whose monster is a human who turns into a wolf or another beast (An American Werewolf in London, The Howling, Ginger Snaps, Cat People). Universal's The Wolf Man stays in A4-15.

label: Zombie Film
secs: 1=Voodoo & Sorcery Zombies | 2=Romero Cycle & Ghoul Sieges | 3=Italian & European Zombie Films | 4=Zombie Comedies | 5=Rage-Virus & Infected Films | 6=Zombie Action & Game Adaptations | 7=Revenant, Resurrection & Humanist Zombie Films
defn: A horror film whose threat is the reanimated or infected dead, from voodoo to rage virus (Night of the Living Dead, 28 Days Later, Shaun of the Dead, Train to Busan). Lab reanimation played for gore-comedy goes to A4-37 Splatstick.

label: Creature Feature
secs: 1=Amphibious & Sea Monsters | 2=Subterranean & Cave Creatures | 3=Folkloric & Demonic Monsters | 4=Little Monsters | 5=Prehistoric Beasts & Cryptids
defn: A horror film whose threat is an invented monster that is neither a real animal nor an alien (Creature from the Black Lagoon, Tremors, Gremlins, The Descent). Real animals go to A4-21 Natural Horror; aliens to A4-22; giant city-smashers to A5-6 Kaiju.

label: Killer Toy Film
defn: A horror film whose threat is a doll, puppet, toy or animatronic come alive (Child's Play, Puppet Master, Annabelle, Five Nights at Freddy's). An AI android doll goes to A4-22.

label: Natural Horror
secs: 1=Shark & Sea-Beast Attacks | 2=Crocodilians & Giant Snakes | 3=Swarms, Bugs & Atomic Giants | 4=Mammal & Bird Attacks | 5=Eco-Horror & Nature's Revenge
defn: A horror film whose threat is real animals or nature turned predator, including enlarged or mutated real species (Jaws 2, The Birds, Cujo, Them!, Long Weekend). Invented monsters go to A4-19.

label: Science Fiction Horror
secs: 1=Alien Horror | 2=Body Snatchers & Alien Infiltration | 3=Space & Research-Station Horror | 4=Mad Science & Lab-Made Monsters | 5=Contagion & Outbreak Horror | 6=Machine & Technology Horror
defn: A horror film whose threat comes from a science-fictional premise: aliens, space, experiments, contagion or machines (Alien, The Thing, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, The Fly). Bodily transformation as the point goes to A4-23 Body Horror; cosmic unknowability to A4-24.

label: Body Horror
secs: 1=Cronenbergian & Venereal Horror | 2=Transformation & Metamorphosis | 3=Surgical, Beauty & Bodily-Modification Horror | 4=Infection & Parasite Horror
defn: A horror film whose fear is the transformation, invasion or mutilation of the human body itself (Videodrome, Tetsuo: The Iron Man, The Substance, Titane). A creature born in a lab goes to A4-22.

label: Lovecraftian Horror
defn: A horror film of cosmic dread before entities or realities beyond human comprehension (In the Mouth of Madness, Color Out of Space, The Void, The Mist).

label: Psychological Horror
secs: 1=Madness & Breakdown | 2=Grief, Trauma & the Family | 3=Doubles & Fractured Identity | 4=Purgatory, Loops & Unreality | 5=Social-Thriller Horror & Allegory | 6=Obsession, Performance & Art | 7=Confinement, Traps & Captivity
defn: A horror film whose terror lies in the mind: breakdown, trauma, doubled identity or unreal worlds, with any monster kept ambiguous (Repulsion, Jacob's Ladder, Get Out, The Babadook). A killer stalking victims goes to A4-28 Slasher Film.

label: Psycho-Biddy
defn: A horror-thriller cycle built on an ageing woman as a deranged menace (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte, Strait-Jacket).

label: Home Invasion Film
secs: 1=Siege & Intruder Thrillers | 2=Masked-Stranger Horror | 3=Reverse Home Invasion
defn: A horror or thriller film whose engine is intruders breaking into a home and besieging those inside (Funny Games, The Strangers, You're Next, Don't Breathe).

label: Slasher Film
secs: 1=Proto-Slashers & Psycho-Killer Films | 2=Halloween & Friday the 13th Franchises | 3=Golden-Age Stalk-and-Slash | 4=Supernatural Slashers | 5=Post-Scream Revival Slashers | 6=Slasher Comedies, Meta & Time-Loop Slashers | 7=Retro & New-Wave Slashers | 8=Public-Domain Parody Slashers
defn: A horror film in which a stalking killer murders a group of victims one by one, often till a final girl remains (Halloween, Friday the 13th, A Nightmare on Elm Street, Scream). Rural killer clans go to A4-29; holiday-themed killers to A4-30.

label: Backwoods Horror
secs: 1=Texas Chain Saw Cycle | 2=Cannibal & Mutant Clans | 3=Outback & Roadside Predators | 4=Swamp & Forest Stalkers
defn: A horror film in which travellers stray into the countryside and are hunted by rural killers or inbred clans (The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, The Hills Have Eyes, Wrong Turn, Wolf Creek). Pagan rural communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.

label: Holiday Horror
secs: 1=Christmas Horror | 2=Other Holidays & Halloween Night
defn: A horror film whose killer or curse is built around a named holiday and its rituals (Silent Night, Deadly Night, My Bloody Valentine, Krampus, Trick 'r Treat). The Halloween franchise stays in A4-28.

label: Splatter Film
defn: A horror film whose primary attraction is graphic gore and the spectacle of the opened body (Blood Feast, Guinea Pig 2: Flower of Flesh and Blood, Nekromantik, Ichi the Killer). Prolonged captivity and torture go to A4-33.

label: New French Extremity
defn: The French-language extreme horror cycle of the 2000s, transgressive in violence and sexuality (High Tension, Inside, Martyrs, Frontier(s)).

label: Torture Porn
defn: A horror film whose engine is captivity and the prolonged torture of victims (Saw, Hostel, The Collector, Would You Rather).

label: Cannibal Film
defn: A horror film whose threat is people who eat people, including the Italian jungle cycle (Cannibal Holocaust, Cannibal Ferox, Raw, Ravenous). Rural killer families go to A4-29.

label: Found-Footage Horror
secs: 1=Lost Tapes & Expedition Footage | 2=Ghost-Hunt, News-Crew & Investigation Footage | 3=Home-Video Hauntings | 4=Faux Broadcasts & Mock Documentaries | 5=Screenlife & Livestream Horror | 6=Found-Footage Anthologies
defn: A horror film presented as recovered recordings made by the characters (The Blair Witch Project, REC, Paranormal Activity, Lake Mungo). Sources are the form; the threat may be any.

label: Anthology Horror
defn: A horror film made of separate stories, usually joined by a frame (Dead of Night, The House That Dripped Blood, Creepshow 2, Southbound). Found-footage anthologies stay in A4-35.

label: Splatstick
defn: A horror comedy whose humour is excessive gore staged as slapstick (Evil Dead II, Bad Taste, Re-Animator, Deathgasm). Zombie splatstick such as Braindead stays in A4-18.

label: Comedy Horror
secs: 1=Monster Rallies & Horror Spoofs | 2=Ghost & Supernatural Comedies | 3=Indian & Asian Horror-Comedies | 4=Creature Comedies | 5=Camp, Cult & Troma | 6=Dark Satire & Social Horror-Comedy | 7=Meta & Mockumentary Horror-Comedy
defn: A film in which horror's monsters, killers or hauntings drive a comic engine (Ghostbusters, Beetlejuice, Stree, The Cabin in the Woods, Ready or Not). Gore-as-slapstick goes to A4-37; pure parody of horror films to A12.

label: Fantaterror
secs: 1=Paul Naschy & the Daninsky Cycle | 2=Amando de Ossorio & the Blind Dead | 3=Other Fantaterror (Serrador, Aranda, Franco, Klimovsky)
defn: The Spanish horror boom of c. 1968–1980 — Paul Naschy's Waldemar Daninsky werewolf films, Amando de Ossorio's Blind Dead, Narciso Ibáñez Serrador, Vicente Aranda, León Klimovsky — mixing gothic monsters, Templar ghouls and late-Franco-era sexual and Catholic dread (Tombs of the Blind Dead, The House That Screamed).

label: Ramsay Brothers Horror
defn: The Hindi low-budget horror cycle of the Ramsay family (1972–1990s): haunted havelis, cursed temples, monster-men and songs, the B-movie strand of Bollywood horror (Purana Mandir, Veerana).

label: Hard Science Fiction
secs: 1=Orbit, Moon & Laboratory | 2=Mars Missions | 3=Deep-Space Voyages
defn: A science fiction film whose drama rests on plausible physics, biology and engineering, usually in spaceflight (2001: A Space Odyssey, The Martian, Interstellar, The Andromeda Strain). Space adventure with empires and aliens goes to A5-2.

label: Space Opera
secs: 1=Star Wars Saga | 2=Star Trek Films | 3=Planetary Romance & Pulp Space Opera | 4=Space Westerns & Frontier Adventures | 5=Family Space Adventures
defn: A science fiction adventure of interstellar empires, wars and heroes on a grand scale (Star Wars, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, Dune, Avatar). Plausible spaceflight goes to A5-1.

label: Military Science Fiction
defn: A science fiction film centred on soldiers, armies and future warfare (Starship Troopers, Battle Los Angeles, Universal Soldier, Ender's Game).

label: Alien Invasion
defn: A science fiction film in which extraterrestrials attack or occupy Earth (The War of the Worlds, Independence Day, They Live, Attack the Block). Peaceful contact goes to A5-5; alien horror to A4-22.

label: First Contact & Alien Visitor
secs: 1=First Contact & Messages | 2=Alien Visitors & Refugees | 3=Alien-Friend Family Films | 4=Abductions & UFO Encounters
defn: A science fiction film about humanity meeting extraterrestrials who are not simply invaders: messages, visitors, friends and abductors (Arrival, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Starman, Fire in the Sky).

label: Kaiju
secs: 1=Shōwa Era (1954–1975) | 2=Heisei Era (1984–1999) | 3=Millennium Era (1999–2004) | 4=Reiwa Era (2016–) | 5=Hollywood Giant Monsters & the MonsterVerse | 6=Kaiju beyond Japan and Hollywood
defn: A film of giant monsters that rampage through cities or fight each other, from Toho's Godzilla to its imitators (Godzilla, Gamera, King Kong, The Host). Ordinary-sized monsters go to A4-19.

label: Tokusatsu
secs: 1=Toho, Daiei & Toei Special-Effects Films | 2=Henshin Heroes (Ultra, Rider, Sentai & Power Rangers)
defn: A live-action special-effects superhero film in the Japanese tradition of costumed transforming heroes, including adaptations (Shin Ultraman, Shin Kamen Rider, Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie).

label: Time Travel Film
secs: 1=Time Machines & Time Tourism | 2=Changing the Past & Paradox | 3=Time Loops | 4=Time-Travel Comedies | 5=Messages Across Time & Time-Slip Romance
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is movement through time or a broken flow of time (Back to the Future, 12 Monkeys, Primer, Edge of Tomorrow).

label: Parallel Universe Film
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is alternate worlds or versions of reality existing side by side (Another Earth, Coherence, Mr. Nobody, The One).

label: Simulated Reality
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is a manufactured reality: virtual worlds, game spaces, dream and memory technology (Inception, Total Recall, eXistenZ, Ready Player One). The Matrix films stay in A5-11 Cyberpunk.

label: Cyberpunk
defn: A science fiction film of high-tech, low-life futures: corporations, cyborgs, hackers and networked cities (Blade Runner, The Matrix, RoboCop, Tetsuo II: Body Hammer).

label: Artificial Intelligence & Robots
secs: 1=Rogue AI & Machine Uprisings | 2=Androids & Synthetic Persons | 3=Robot Companions & Family Films | 4=Giant Robots & Transformers | 5=Mind Uploading & Digital Afterlives
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is thinking machines: rogue computers, androids, robot companions and giant robots (The Terminator, Ex Machina, Short Circuit, Transformers). A killer AI as horror goes to A4-22.

label: Biopunk
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is biotechnology: cloning, genetic engineering and chemical enhancement of humans and animals (The Boys from Brazil, Okja, Limitless, Mickey 17). Lab monsters as horror go to A4-22.

label: Scientific Romance
defn: A Verne- and Wells-type science adventure of submarines, inventions and fabulous journeys, and its retro-futurist pastiches (20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, Things to Come, Invention for Destruction).

label: Size-Change Film
defn: A science fiction film whose premise is people shrunk or enlarged (The Incredible Shrinking Man, Fantastic Voyage, Honey, I Shrunk the Kids, Downsizing).

label: Psionics
defn: A science fiction or horror film whose premise is psychic powers such as telekinesis, telepathy or teleportation (Scanners, Carrie, Jumper, Midnight Special).

label: Dystopian Film
secs: 1=Totalitarian & Surveillance States | 2=Lethal Games & Blood Sports | 3=Young-Adult Dystopias | 4=Control of Age, Birth & Life | 5=Class Enclosures & Vertical Societies | 6=Lawless Cities & Future Crime | 7=Absurdist & Satirical Dystopias
defn: A science fiction film set in a future society organised as oppression (1984, Brazil, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay, Snowpiercer). A world after collapse goes to A5-19.

label: Post-Apocalyptic Film
secs: 1=Nuclear War & Aftermath | 2=Wasteland Road & Raider Films | 3=Last Survivors | 4=Planet of the Apes Cycle | 5=Collapse & Survival | 6=Post-Apocalyptic Comedy & Cult
defn: A science fiction film set during or after the collapse of civilisation (Threads, Mad Max: Fury Road, The Road, Planet of the Apes). The catastrophe itself as spectacle goes to A5-20.

label: Disaster Film
secs: 1=Earthquakes, Volcanoes & Floods | 2=Cosmic Impacts & End of the World | 3=Transport, Structure & Industrial Disasters | 4=Pandemic Outbreaks | 5=Storms & Climate Catastrophes
defn: A film whose spectacle is a large-scale catastrophe and the struggle to survive it (The Towering Inferno, Twister, Armageddon, Contagion). Life after the collapse goes to A5-19.

label: Soft Science Fiction
defn: A science fiction film whose speculative conceit serves human, social or philosophical questions rather than technology or spectacle (Solaris, The Man from Earth, The Fountain, Hard to Be a God).

label: Science Fiction Comedy
defn: A film whose comic engine is a science-fictional premise, often aliens among ordinary people (The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Kin-dza-dza!, Earth Girls Are Easy, Iron Sky).

label: Afrofuturist Film
defn: Science fiction of the Afrofuturist movement (the term is Mark Dery's, 1993): Black diasporic and African speculative futures, cosmic myth and technoculture (Space Is the Place, The Brother from Another Planet, Neptune Frost).

label: High Fantasy
defn: A feature set wholly in an invented secondary world with its own peoples, history and magic, built around an epic quest or war (The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, Willow, The Dark Crystal, Wicked). A pulp-barbarian hero of muscle and steel goes to A6-2; a child who crosses into the world from ours goes to A6-4.

label: Sword and Sorcery
secs: 1=1980s Sword-and-Sorcery Boom (incl. Italian barbarian films) | 2=Later Sword and Sorcery (1990s–)
defn: A fantasy adventure of a lone warrior or mercenary band fighting sorcerers and monsters in a barbaric pre-modern world, with personal rather than world-saving stakes (Conan the Barbarian, The Beastmaster, Deathstalker, Red Sonja). An epic secondary-world war goes to A6-1.

label: Arthurian Film
defn: A film retelling the Matter of Britain: King Arthur, the Round Table, Camelot, the Grail or its knights, in any register from epic to parody (Excalibur, Perceval le Gallois, The Green Knight, Kaamelott: First Installment). Robin Hood and other outlaw legends go to A6-18.

label: Portal Fantasy
defn: A fantasy in which a protagonist from our world crosses through a door, book, dream, game or screen into another realm and must find the way back (The Wizard of Oz, Labyrinth, The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Pleasantville). A film set wholly in the other world goes to A6-1.

label: Dark Fantasy
defn: A fantasy whose wonders are menacing and whose tone is grim, cruel or uncanny, without being built to frighten in the manner of horror (Pan's Labyrinth, The City of Lost Children, Tideland, Border). A dark retelling of a named fairy tale goes to A6-12; a film built for fear goes to A4.

label: Contemporary Fantasy
defn: A fantasy in which a hidden society of wizards, demigods or magical beings exists alongside the modern world and a young hero is initiated into it, usually through a school or secret order (Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief, Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children). Adult supernatural action in a modern city goes to A6-7.

label: Urban Fantasy
defn: A fantasy action film in which vampires, immortals, demons, witches or sorcerers wage hidden wars in a present-day city (Night Watch, Highlander, Big Trouble in Little China, Bright). A youth-initiation story of a hidden wizarding school goes to A6-6; a film built to frighten goes to A4.

label: Romantic Fantasy
defn: A fantasy whose central engine is a love story across a supernatural barrier: immortality, a curse, an angel, a djinn or an enchanted village (Ladyhawke, Brigadoon, Winter's Tale, Three Thousand Years of Longing). A fairy-tale romance retold from a named tale goes to A6-12; a romance with only a light magical device goes to A13.

label: Fantasy Comedy
secs: 1=Body-Swap & Age-Change Comedy | 2=Ghost & Afterlife Comedy | 3=Angels, Devils & Genies | 4=Witch Comedy | 5=Enchanted Object, Creature & Tall-Tale Comedy
defn: A comedy whose engine is a single magical premise dropped into ordinary life: a body swap, a ghost, a genie, a witch or an enchanted object (Big, Heaven Can Wait, The Witches of Eastwick, Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian). Magic told with deadpan seriousness goes to A6-10; a comedy aimed chiefly at children goes to A17-1.

label: Magical Realism
secs: 1=Marvellous in the Everyday | 2=Afterlife & Heavenly Messengers
defn: A film that treats the marvellous as an unremarked part of an otherwise realistic world, or stages the afterlife and heavenly messengers with the same matter-of-factness (Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands, Big Fish, Wings of Desire, After Life). A comedy built on a magic gimmick goes to A6-9.

label: Mythological Fantasy
secs: 1=Classical Myth & Peplum Fantasy | 2=Indian & East Asian Mythological Fantasy (shenmo, puranic) | 3=Folk Legend & World Mythology | 4=Heaven, Hell & the Devil
defn: A fantasy that dramatises a named mythology, epic, religious cosmology or folk legend, with gods, demigods, demons and heroes of that tradition (Jason and the Argonauts, Journey to the West: Conquering the Demons, Yeelen, The Seventh Seal). A fairy tale goes to A6-12; a historical epic without gods goes to A8.

label: Fairy-Tale Film
secs: 1=European Fairy-Tale Film (Märchenfilm & pohádka) | 2=Auteur & Poetic Fairy Tales | 3=Hollywood Live-Action Fairy Tales & Remakes | 4=Revisionist & Dark Retellings | 5=Fairy-Tale Romance & Parody | 6=Soviet Skazka Films (Ptushko & Rou)
defn: A film that adapts, retells or parodies a named fairy tale or literary tale (Grimm, Perrault, Andersen, Arabian Nights, Collodi) or invents one in its form (Beauty and the Beast 1946, The Singing Ringing Tree, Snow White and the Huntsman, The Princess Bride). A myth or epic goes to A6-11.

label: Marvel Cinematic Universe
secs: 1=The Infinity Saga (Phases One–Three) | 2=The Multiverse Saga (Phases Four–Six)
defn: A feature produced by Marvel Studios as part of its shared continuity of Marvel Comics heroes (Iron Man, The Avengers, Black Panther, Thunderbolts*). Marvel characters filmed by other studios outside that continuity go to A6-15.

label: DC Comics Film
secs: 1=Superman Film Series | 2=Batman Film Series | 3=DC Extended Universe | 4=Other DC Adaptations & the DC Universe
defn: A live-action feature adapting DC Comics characters, in any of the studio's successive continuities (Superman 1978, Batman 1989, The Dark Knight, Wonder Woman). Deconstructions such as Watchmen go to A6-17.

label: Marvel Comics Film outside the MCU
secs: 1=X-Men Film Series | 2=Spider-Man & Sony's Spider-Man Universe | 3=Other Licensed Marvel Films
defn: A live-action feature adapting Marvel Comics characters made by a licensee studio outside the Marvel Studios continuity (X-Men, Spider-Man 2002, Blade, Venom). A Marvel Studios feature goes to A6-13.

label: Standalone Superhero Film
secs: 1=Pulp & Comic-Strip Heroes | 2=Independent-Comics & Manga Adaptations | 3=Screen-Original Superheroes | 4=Children's Superhero Comedy | 5=Superhero Cinema outside Hollywood
defn: A superhero film outside the Marvel and DC franchises: a pulp or comic-strip avenger, an independent-comics or manga hero, a hero created for the screen, or a national industry's own superhero (The Rocketeer, Hellboy, Darkman, Krrish). Parody and deconstruction go to A6-17.

label: Superhero Parody & Deconstruction
defn: A film that mocks the superhero form or takes its premise apart: what powers, costumes and vigilantism would really mean (Watchmen, Kick-Ass, Unbreakable, Mystery Men). A straight franchise entry with jokes goes to its franchise leaf.

label: Swashbuckler
defn: A costume adventure of sword-fighting heroes, outlaws and avengers in a pre-modern Europe or its colonies, built on duels, rescues and daring escapes (The Adventures of Robin Hood, The Mark of Zorro, The Three Musketeers 1973, Scaramouche). Sea-rovers go to A6-19.

label: Pirate Film
defn: An adventure of pirates, buccaneers or smugglers at sea or on their islands, often with buried treasure (Captain Blood, Treasure Island 1950, Cutthroat Island, Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl). Land-bound duellists go to A6-18.

label: Treasure-Hunt Adventure
defn: A pulp adventure in which an archaeologist, prospector or rogue follows clues, maps and traps to a lost artefact or hoard (Raiders of the Lost Ark, Romancing the Stone, National Treasure, The Mummy 1999). A whole hidden world of survivals goes to A6-21; a video-game hero such as Lara Croft goes to A7-16.

label: Lost World
defn: An adventure in which explorers find a hidden land where prehistoric creatures, vanished peoples or a utopia survive (Journey to the Center of the Earth 1959, Lost Horizon, Congo, Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend). An artefact hunt goes to A6-20.

label: Jungle Adventure
defn: An adventure set in jungle, savannah or colonial frontier, built on the hero's survival among wild animals, rivers and peoples, including Tarzan, Mowgli and the imperial adventure of the British Empire film (Tarzan and His Mate, Gunga Din, The African Queen, Jungle Cruise). A hunt for a single artefact goes to A6-20.

label: Nautical Adventure
defn: An adventure at sea or on a desert island in which the ocean, a whale, a raft or a wreck is the antagonist, including the Robinsonade (Moby Dick, Kon-Tiki, Life of Pi, Swiss Family Robinson). Pirates go to A6-19; naval combat goes to A9.

label: Prehistoric Fiction
defn: An adventure set among early humans in the Stone Age, built on the struggle for fire, food and survival (Quest for Fire, 10,000 BC, Alpha).

label: Expedition Adventure
defn: An adventure of a journey or expedition against distance and nature, by balloon, plane, horse or on foot, in the tradition of the voyages extraordinaires (Around the World in 80 Days 1956, The Aeronauts, Hidalgo, Letter Never Sent). A voyage at sea goes to A6-23.

label: Bergfilm (Mountain Film)
defn: The German mountain film of the 1920s–30s (Arnold Fanck, Leni Riefenstahl, Luis Trenker): real Alpine climbing and skiing photographed on location, elemental storms and avalanches, romantic rivalry and heroic summits (The Holy Mountain, The White Hell of Pitz Palu, The Blue Light).

label: Action-Hero Film
secs: 1=Silent Stunt & Serial Action | 2=One-Man Army | 3=Fugitive, Drifter & Street-Level Action | 4=Ensemble & Legacy Action
defn: An action film built around a single indestructible hero who takes on an army, a gang or a town alone, from silent stunt serials to the muscle cinema of the 1980s and its ensemble revivals (Commando, Rambo: First Blood Part II, Road House, The Expendables). A hero trapped in one besieged place goes to A7-2; a revenge mission goes to A7-3.

label: Die Hard Scenario
defn: An action thriller in which a lone hero is trapped in one sealed location (a tower, plane, ship, train, school or White House) taken by terrorists or criminals (Die Hard, Speed, Under Siege, Olympus Has Fallen). A hero who roams freely goes to A7-1; a pure hostage-negotiation thriller goes to A3.

label: Vigilante Film
defn: An action film in which a wronged individual takes the law into their own hands to punish criminals or rescue a kidnapped relative (Taken, The Equalizer, Nobody, The Man from Nowhere). A professional killer for hire goes to A7-6.

label: Military Action Film
defn: An action film of special forces, commandos, fighter pilots or tactical units on missions, rescues and counter-terror strikes outside a declared war narrative (Missing in Action, Top Gun, Extraction, Kandahar). A film about a historical war goes to A9.

label: Car Chase Film
defn: An action film whose set pieces are vehicle chases, street races, getaways and stunt driving (The Fast and the Furious, The Transporter, Wheelman, Premium Rush). A heist plot without the driving goes to A2.

label: Hitman Film
defn: An action film centred on a professional contract killer or assassin, the job, the code and the double-cross (Léon: The Professional, The Mechanic, Assassins, Polar). A woman assassin film in the girls-with-guns mould goes to A7-7; a stylised gun-ballet killer goes to A7-8.

label: Girls with Guns
defn: An action film whose fighting hero is a woman or girl (assassin, cop, avenger or princess), the cycle named in Hong Kong and global since (Yes, Madam!, La Femme Nikita, The Villainess, Kill Boksoon). A male professional killer goes to A7-6.

label: Gun Fu
defn: An action film whose gunfights are choreographed like martial arts: close-quarter shooting, acrobatics and a fight ballet (John Wick, Desperado, Shoot 'Em Up, Crank). The Hong Kong source tradition goes to A7-9.

label: Heroic Bloodshed
defn: The Hong Kong gangster-action cycle of brotherhood, loyalty and operatic gunplay launched by John Woo, and its direct successors (A Better Tomorrow, The Killer, Hard Boiled, Exiled). Its stylised global offspring go to A7-8.

label: Hong Kong Action Cinema
defn: A modern-dress Hong Kong action film of stunt-driven police, adventure and crime set pieces (Police Story, Project A, Wheels on Meals, Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In). Period kung fu goes to A7-11; swordplay to A7-12; gangster gunplay to A7-9.

label: Kung Fu Film
secs: 1=Bruce Lee Films | 2=Shaw Brothers & Shaolin Films | 3=Kung Fu Comedy | 4=Folk-Hero Kung Fu (Wong Fei-hung, Ip Man) | 5=Bruceploitation
defn: A martial arts film of Chinese unarmed and weapon styles, usually set in the late imperial or Republican past, built on training, schools and revenge (Enter the Dragon, The 36th Chamber of Shaolin, Drunken Master, Ip Man). Swordsmen of the jianghu go to A7-12.

label: Wuxia
secs: 1=New-School Wuxia (1966–1984: King Hu, Chang Cheh, Chu Yuan) | 2=Hong Kong New Wave Wuxia (1985–1999) | 3=Wuxia Blockbusters (2000–)
defn: A Chinese martial-chivalry film of wandering swordsmen and swordswomen in the jianghu underworld, with lightness-skill and codes of honour (Come Drink with Me, A Touch of Zen, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Hero). Hand-to-hand kung fu goes to A7-11.

label: Martial Arts Film
secs: 1=Japanese Budō Film | 2=Karate Kid & Dojo Film | 3=Tournament & Fight-Circuit Film | 4=Martial-Arts Star Vehicles | 5=Muay Thai & Thai Action | 6=Silat & Indonesian Action | 7=Other Asian Martial Arts Cinema
defn: A martial arts film of Japanese, Korean, Southeast Asian or Western fighting styles (judo, karate, kickboxing, muay thai, silat) built on training, tournaments and hand-to-hand set pieces (The Karate Kid, Bloodsport, Ong-Bak: The Thai Warrior, The Raid: Redemption). Chinese kung fu goes to A7-11; ninjas to A7-14.

label: Ninja Film
secs: 1=Japanese Ninja Films | 2=Hong Kong Ninja Films | 3=Cannon & Western Ninja Boom (1981–)
defn: A martial arts film whose fighters are ninja, from the 1980s ninja boom to its revivals (Ninja III: The Domination, American Ninja, Ninja Assassin, Snake Eyes).

label: Buddy Cop Film
secs: 1=Mismatched-Partner Action | 2=Buddy-Cop Comedy & Spoof | 3=Buddy-Cop Film beyond Hollywood
defn: An action film or action comedy built on two mismatched police partners (or a cop and an unlikely partner) forced to work a case together (48 Hrs., Lethal Weapon, Rush Hour, Hot Fuzz). A comedy without police work goes to A12.

label: Video Game Adaptation
defn: A live-action feature adapted from a video game franchise, whatever its genre (Mortal Kombat, Lara Croft: Tomb Raider, Warcraft, A Minecraft Movie). A film merely set inside a game goes to its genre.

label: Exploitation Action Film
defn: A low-budget action film sold on excess (gore, nudity, absurd stunts), from grindhouse and direct-to-video cult items to deliberate grindhouse homages (Samurai Cop, Hard Ticket to Hawaii, Riki-Oh: The Story of Ricky, Hobo with a Shotgun).

label: Lucha Film
defn: The Mexican luchador film (1952–1980s): masked professional wrestlers — El Santo, Blue Demon, Mil Máscaras, the Wrestling Women — fighting vampires, mummies, mad scientists and Martians in action-horror-science-fiction serials (Santo vs. the Vampire Women).

label: Historical Epic
secs: 1=Foundation & National Sagas | 2=Multigenerational & Revolutionary Sagas | 3=South & East Asian Historical Epics | 4=Pre-Contact & Ancient-World Epics
defn: A large-scale, long-form spectacle that sweeps a nation, dynasty or family through decades of real history, with the historical upheaval itself as the subject (Intolerance, Gone with the Wind, 1900, Ponniyin Selvan: Part I). Ancient Mediterranean spectacles go to A8-2; epics built around a battle campaign go to A9-1.

label: Sword-and-Sandal Film
secs: 1=Silent Epics (1913–1927) | 2=Hollywood & British Epics of the Studio and Widescreen Era (1932–1966) | 3=Italian Peplum (1954–1965) | 4=Art-House & Erotic Antiquity | 5=Revival Epics (2000–)
defn: A spectacle set in Greco-Roman or biblical antiquity, built on gladiators, legions, mythic heroes or Old Testament stories (Ben-Hur, Spartacus, The Ten Commandments, 300). Lives of Jesus and the saints go to A11-4 Religious Biopic.

label: Medieval Film
defn: A film set in the European or Near Eastern Middle Ages whose world of knights, sagas, crusades and feudal law is the subject rather than a single battle campaign (The Northman, The Last Duel, Flesh+Blood, Arn: The Knight Templar). Battle-centred medieval epics go to A9-1.

label: Royal Court Drama
defn: A period drama of intrigue inside a royal or imperial court, where succession, favour and palace politics drive the story and no single royal life is traced (The Lion in Winter, Queen Margot, Curse of the Golden Flower, The King's Warden). A film tracing a monarch's life goes to A11-1 Royal Biopic.

label: Jidaigeki
secs: 1=Prewar Jidaigeki (1925–1945) | 2=Postwar Golden Age (1950–1959) | 3=1960s Jidaigeki | 4=Late & Contemporary Jidaigeki (1970–)
defn: A Japanese period drama set before the Meiji Restoration in which manners, clan duty and social hierarchy, not sword combat, carry the story (Sansho the Bailiff, Rashomon, Ran, The Twilight Samurai). A film driven by swordplay goes to A8-6 Chanbara.

label: Chanbara
secs: 1=Classic Ronin & Samurai Swordplay | 2=Zatoichi Series | 3=Lone Wolf and Cub & Revenge Manga Films | 4=Modern Chanbara Revival
defn: A Japanese swordplay film in which sword combat by samurai or ronin is the engine of the drama (Yojimbo, Seven Samurai, The Tale of Zatoichi, 13 Assassins). Swordless period dramas go to A8-5 Jidaigeki.

label: Colonial & Slavery Film
secs: 1=Slavery & Abolition | 2=Colonial Rule & Anti-Colonial Revolt
defn: A period film whose subject is chattel slavery or colonial rule and resistance to it, told from the plantation, the mission or the colony (Burn!, The Last Supper, 12 Years a Slave, The Camp at Thiaroye). Battle-centred colonial wars go to A9-1.

label: Heritage Film
secs: 1=Austen Adaptations | 2=Georgian & Victorian Novel Adaptations | 3=Edwardian & Merchant Ivory Films | 4=Interwar Country-House Films
defn: A British (or British-set) period film of gentility, country houses and pre-war manners, usually from a classic English novel, valued for its nostalgic re-creation of the national past (A Room with a View, Pride & Prejudice, Howards End, Downton Abbey). Continental and American literary costume films go to A8-9.

label: Costume Drama
secs: 1=French Novel Adaptations | 2=Russian, Baltic & Central European | 3=Southern European & Latin | 4=Scandinavian & Nordic | 5=American Gilded & Jazz Age | 6=Original Period Romances | 7=Twentieth-Century Period Pieces
defn: A period drama, usually adapted from a classic novel or play, whose dress, manners and social codes of a past society are the dramatic material (Les Misérables, The Leopard, Anna Karenina, Portrait of a Lady on Fire). British gentility films go to A8-8 Heritage Film.

label: Shakespeare Film
defn: A screen adaptation of a Shakespeare play, in period or transposed dress, with the play's text and structure carrying it (Hamlet, Chimes at Midnight, Henry V, The Tragedy of Macbeth). Free transpositions into another culture such as Throne of Blood stay with their tradition.

label: Political Drama
secs: 1=Fascist & Nazi Era | 2=Stalinist & Soviet-Bloc Era | 3=Latin American Dictatorships | 4=Other Twentieth-Century Political Histories | 5=Nineteenth-Century Revolutions & Repression
defn: A period drama of private lives under a named political regime, where dictatorship, purge, occupation or revolution is the pressure that shapes the story (Mephisto, Burnt by the Sun, No, A Taxi Driver). Dramatised single events go to A8-13 Docudrama; lives of politicians go to A11-2.

label: Social Problem Film
secs: 1=Labour, Poverty & Rural Life | 2=Emigration & Immigration | 3=Women's Lives & Reproductive Rights | 4=Race & Civil Rights | 5=Queer History | 6=Witch Trials & Religious Persecution
defn: A period drama that dramatises a social injustice of its era, such as labour, emigration, women's rights, race, sexuality or persecution, through fictional representative lives (Germinal, Vera Drake, The Help, The Crucible). Real activists' lives go to A11-2.

label: Docudrama
secs: 1=Disasters, Rescues & Expeditions | 2=Political Crises & Scandals | 3=Massacres, Riots & Terror | 4=Legal Cases & Miscarriages of Justice | 5=Journalism & Whistleblowing | 6=Humanitarian Crises & Genocide
defn: A dramatised reconstruction of one documented real event, crisis or case, where the event rather than a person's life is the subject (A Night to Remember, Apollo 13, United 93, The Post). A film tracing a person's life goes to A11.

label: Sageuk Film
defn: The Korean historical film (sageuk), set chiefly in the Goryeo and Joseon courts and countryside: palace intrigue, royal doubles, scholars, painters and kisaeng (The King and the Clown, Masquerade, Untold Scandal).

label: War Epic
secs: 1=Ancient & Medieval Battles | 2=Early Modern, Napoleonic & Colonial Wars | 3=American Revolution & Civil War | 4=Revolutions & Civil Wars of the Early 20th Century
defn: A large-scale battle spectacle of a pre-twentieth-century war or an early-twentieth-century revolution, with the campaign as the narrative spine (Alexander Nevsky, Braveheart, Zulu, Glory). WWI and later go to their own leaves.

label: World War I Film
defn: A film of the First World War, its trenches, air war and immediate aftermath (All Quiet on the Western Front, Paths of Glory, Gallipoli, 1917).

label: World War II Combat Film
secs: 1=Western Front & Mediterranean | 2=Air & Naval War | 3=Commando & Men-on-a-Mission Films | 4=Eastern Front | 5=Nordic & Baltic Fronts
defn: A combat film of the Second World War in Europe and the Mediterranean, centred on soldiers, aircrews or sailors in action (Saving Private Ryan, Das Boot, The Guns of Navarone, Come and See is A9-5). Pacific theatre goes to A9-4.

label: Pacific War Film
defn: A film of the Pacific and Asian theatres of the Second World War, including the Second Sino-Japanese War (The Burmese Harp, The Human Condition, Letters from Iwo Jima, The Thin Red Line). POW camps go to A9-7.

label: Partisan & Resistance Film
secs: 1=Yugoslav Partisan Film | 2=Soviet & East European Partisans | 3=Western European Resistance
defn: A film of irregular fighters and resistance networks against occupation in the Second World War, with the Yugoslav partisan film as its named canon (The Battle of Neretva, Walter Defends Sarajevo, The Ascent, Army of Shadows). Old leaf Partisan Film merged here with resistance films.

label: Holocaust Film
secs: 1=Camps | 2=Ghettos, Round-Ups & Deportation | 3=Hiding, Rescue & Survival | 4=Perpetrators & Aftermath
defn: A fiction film of the Nazi persecution and murder of European Jews: camps, ghettos, deportations, hiding and the reckoning afterwards (Schindler's List, The Pianist, Son of Saul, The Zone of Interest).

label: Prisoner-of-War Film
defn: A war film set among captured soldiers in a POW camp, built on survival, collaboration or escape (Stalag 17, The Great Escape, The Bridge on the River Kwai, Rescue Dawn).

label: Home Front Film
secs: 1=World-War Home Fronts | 2=Children in War | 3=Civilians in Later Wars
defn: A war film centred on civilians, families and children living through a war away from or overrun by the front (Mrs. Miniver, Forbidden Games, Two Women, Empire of the Sun).

label: Atomic Bomb Film
defn: A Japanese film of the atomic bombings and the hibakusha who survived them (Black Rain).

label: Vietnam War Film
defn: A film of the Vietnam War, American or Vietnamese, in combat or in its training camps (Platoon, Full Metal Jacket, Wild Field, Da 5 Bloods). Veterans' homecoming goes to A9-13.

label: Modern War Film
secs: 1=Korean War & Cold War | 2=Decolonisation & African Wars | 3=Balkan & Caucasus Wars | 4=Middle Eastern Wars | 5=Insurgencies, Civil Wars & the Troubles | 6=Russo-Ukrainian War | 7=Soviet–Afghan & South Asian Wars
defn: A film of a post-1945 war other than Vietnam and the War on Terror: Korea, decolonisation, the Balkans, the Middle East, insurgencies and Ukraine (Tae Guk Gi, No Man's Land, Lebanon, Beasts of No Nation).

label: War on Terror Film
defn: A film of the Gulf, Iraq and Afghanistan wars and counter-terror operations after 1990, often built on a single real mission (The Hurt Locker, Black Hawk Down, Jarhead, Warfare).

label: Returning Veteran Film
defn: A film of a war's aftermath for those who fought or occupied: homecoming, trauma, mine-clearing and reckoning (The Best Years of Our Lives, Birdy, Land of Mine, Beanpole). Weakly attested label; the field also says homecoming film.

label: Anti-War Film
secs: 1=Allegory & Protest | 2=War Satire & Comedy
defn: A film whose primary mode is protest against war itself, by allegory or by satire, rather than depiction of one campaign (Johnny Got His Gun, Shame, Three Kings, Jojo Rabbit).

label: Silent Western
defn: A western of the silent era, from William S. Hart to John Ford's first epics (Hell's Hinges, The Iron Horse, The Wind).

label: Classical Western
secs: 1=Cavalry & Epic Westerns | 2=Lawman & Town-Tamer Westerns | 3=Range, Ranch & Homestead Westerns | 4=Psychological & Revenge Westerns | 5=Mexico-Border & Mercenary Westerns
defn: A Hollywood sound western of the studio era and its later classical survivors, built on the frontier code of lawmen, cattlemen, cavalry and gunfighters (Stagecoach, The Searchers, Rio Bravo, Winchester '73). Westerns that interrogate the myth go to A10-6.

label: Singing Cowboy Western
defn: A B-western musical vehicle for a singing cowboy star (Under Western Stars, Melody Ranch).

label: Comedy Western
defn: A western played for comedy or parody of the frontier code (Go West, Destry Rides Again, Cat Ballou, Shanghai Noon).

label: Musical Western
defn: A stage or screen musical set on the frontier (Calamity Jane, Oklahoma!, Seven Brides for Seven Brothers).

label: Revisionist Western
secs: 1=Anti-Myth & Elegiac Westerns | 2=Outlaw Demythologised | 3=Native American, Black & Frontier Violence | 4=Frontier Women, Settlers & Survival
defn: A western that questions the frontier myth, its violence, heroes, racial and gender order (The Wild Bunch, McCabe & Mrs. Miller, Unforgiven, Meek's Cutoff).

label: Acid Western
defn: A countercultural, hallucinatory western of the late 1960s and its descendants (The Shooting, El Topo, Dead Man).

label: Spaghetti Western
secs: 1=Sergio Leone | 2=Sergio Corbucci | 3=Zapata Westerns (Sollima, Damiani & the political spaghetti) | 4=Other Spaghetti Westerns | 5=Comic Spaghetti & the Trinity Cycle
defn: An Italian-produced western of the 1960s–70s cycle, with its operatic violence and its Trinity comic offshoot (A Fistful of Dollars, Django, The Great Silence, They Call Me Trinity).

label: Ostern
secs: 1=DEFA Indianerfilme (1966–1985) | 2=Soviet Red Westerns (Easterns)
defn: An Eastern Bloc western, East German Indianerfilm or Soviet "red western" (The Sons of Great Bear, Apaches, Nobody Wanted to Die).

label: Meat Pie Western
defn: An Australian western of bushrangers and the outback frontier (The Story of the Kelly Gang, Ned Kelly, The Proposition).

label: Transnational Western
defn: A western whose codes are transposed to another nation's landscape and history, from Manchuria to Patagonia (The Good, the Bad, the Weird, Marlina the Murderer in Four Acts, The Settlers, Bacurau). Italian and Eastern Bloc cycles have their own leaves. Weakly attested umbrella label.

label: Neo-Western
defn: A film set in the contemporary American West in which the western's codes of land, law and violence persist (Hud, No Country for Old Men, Hell or High Water, Wind River).

label: Karl May Western
defn: The West German (Rialto/CCC) cycle of 1962–1968 adapting Karl May's Winnetou and Old Shatterhand novels, shot in Yugoslavia: noble Apache chief, German blood-brother hero, Martin Böttcher scores (Treasure of Silver Lake, Apache Gold). It preceded and fed the Spaghetti Western boom.

label: Royal Biopic
secs: 1=English Monarchs to the Stuarts | 2=Georgian to Windsor Britain | 3=Continental European Courts | 4=Asian & Central Asian Rulers
defn: A film tracing the life or reign of a monarch, consort or royal favourite (The Private Life of Henry VIII, Sissi, The King's Speech, Spencer). Court intrigue without a single life goes to A8-4.

label: Political Biopic
secs: 1=Heads of State & Statesmen | 2=Revolutionaries & National Liberators | 3=Civil-Rights Leaders & Activists | 4=Journalists, Whistleblowers & Dissidents
defn: A film tracing the life or career of a statesman, revolutionary, activist or dissident (Gandhi, Malcolm X, Lincoln, Milk). A single political crisis goes to A8-13 Docudrama.

label: Military Biopic
defn: A film tracing the life of a soldier, general or war hero, where the person rather than one battle is the subject (Sergeant York, Lawrence of Arabia, El Cid, Napoleon). Battle-centred true stories go to A9.

label: Religious Biopic
defn: A film of the life of Jesus, a prophet, saint, reformer or religious leader (The Gospel According to St. Matthew, The Passion of the Christ, Kundun, The Message). Old Testament spectacles go to A8-2.

label: Explorer & Adventurer Biopic
defn: A film of an explorer, mountaineer or solitary adventurer, where the journey into the unknown is the life (Dersu Uzala, Into the Wild, The Lost City of Z, Tenzing).

label: Science & Medicine Biopic
secs: 1=Scientists, Mathematicians & Thinkers | 2=Physicians & Medical Pioneers | 3=Inventors, Engineers & Architects | 4=Space Flight
defn: A film of a scientist, physician, inventor or astronaut, built on the discovery and its cost (A Beautiful Mind, The Imitation Game, Oppenheimer, First Man).

label: Business Biopic
defn: A film of an entrepreneur, tycoon or company founding, built on the rise and the deal (The Social Network, The Aviator, The Founder, BlackBerry). Fraudsters go to A11-13.

label: Artist Biopic
secs: 1=Painters & Sculptors | 2=Photographers | 3=Fashion, Modelling & Dance
defn: A film of a painter, sculptor, photographer, fashion designer or dancer, built around the making of the work (Rembrandt, Frida, Mr. Turner, Saint Laurent).

label: Writer Biopic
secs: 1=Pre-Modern & Romantic-Era Writers | 2=Nineteenth-Century Writers | 3=Twentieth-Century Writers & Thinkers | 4=Children's & Fantasy Authors
defn: A film of a novelist, poet, playwright or thinker, built around the writing and the life that fed it (Becoming Jane, Capote, Bright Star, Tolkien). Adaptations of a writer's own memoir of ordinary life go to A11-14.

label: Musical Biopic
secs: 1=Classical Composers & Performers | 2=Jazz, Blues, Soul & R&B | 3=Rock & Pop | 4=Country & Folk | 5=Hip Hop | 6=Chanson, Latin & World Popular Music
defn: A film of a composer, singer, band or performer, with the music performed as part of the story (Amadeus, Ray, Walk the Line, Bohemian Rhapsody).

label: Show Business Biopic
secs: 1=Stage, Vaudeville & Circus | 2=Hollywood Stars & Filmmakers | 3=Television & Comedy | 4=World Film Industries
defn: A film of a stage, film or television entertainer, filmmaker or impresario, built on the business of performing (Chaplin, Ed Wood, Judy, Man on the Moon).

label: Sports Biopic
secs: 1=Boxing, Wrestling & Combat Sports | 2=Team Sports | 3=Individual & Endurance Sports
defn: A film of an athlete, coach or team, built on a career rather than a single match (Ali, Foxcatcher, I, Tonya, The Iron Claw).

label: Crime Biopic
secs: 1=Gangsters & Drug Lords | 2=Outlaws, Robbers & Con Artists | 3=Killers & True-Crime Cases | 4=Terrorists & Armed Militants
defn: A film of a real gangster, outlaw, swindler, killer or militant, built on the criminal career (GoodFellas, Catch Me If You Can, Monster, Carlos).

label: Autobiographical & Memoir Film
secs: 1=Childhood, Family & Self-Discovery | 2=Addiction & Mental Illness | 3=Illness & Disability | 4=Trauma, Abuse & Survival | 5=Teachers & Mentors | 6=Couples & Love Stories
defn: A film adapted from a memoir or tracing the true life of a private person, known for what they lived through rather than a public field (My Left Foot, Angela's Ashes, Girl, Interrupted, Lion). Weakly attested umbrella label.

label: Silent Clown Comedy
defn: A silent-era comedy (to c. 1930, plus Chaplin's late silents) built on the pantomime and stunt gags of a clown persona or on silent visual farce (The General, Safety Last!, The Kid, The Doll). A sound-era gag film in the same spirit goes to A12-3 Slapstick.

label: Comedian Comedy
secs: 1=Double Acts & Comedy Teams | 2=Hollywood Star-Comedian Vehicles | 3=National Comic Personas | 4=Sketch-Character Spin-Offs | 5=Man-Child Comedy
defn: A film built as a vehicle for a comedian's or comedy team's established persona, where the routines of the performer matter more than the plot (Duck Soup, The Bank Dick, The Gendarme of Saint-Tropez, Wayne's World, Billy Madison). If the film has a stronger premise engine (body swap, heist, parody) it goes there; a silent clown film goes to A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy.

label: Slapstick
defn: A sound-era comedy whose main engine is physical and visual gag work: pratfalls, chases, destruction and choreographed mishap (Playtime, The Return of the Pink Panther, It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World, Bean), including the stunt-prank films of the Jackass line. A silent film goes to A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy.

label: Screwball Comedy
secs: 1=Classic Hollywood Screwball (1933–1945) | 2=European Screwball of the 1930s | 3=Late Studio-Era Screwball (1946–1960s) | 4=Neo-Screwball (1970–) | 5=Screwball Romantic Comedies
defn: A fast, dialogue-driven comedy of the 1930s–40s Hollywood type (and its later pastiches) in which a madcap heroine or eccentric pair upends social decorum, often across class lines (Bringing Up Baby, My Man Godfrey, The Lady Eve, Mr. Deeds Goes to Town). A divorce-and-reunion plot goes to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; a modern romantic comedy to A13.

label: Comedy of Remarriage
defn: A screwball-era comedy whose plot is a married or divorced couple driven apart and brought back together (Stanley Cavell's canon: The Awful Truth, His Girl Friday, The Philadelphia Story, My Favorite Wife). Other screwball plots go to A12-4 Screwball Comedy.

label: Comedy of Manners
secs: 1=Classical High Comedy | 2=Contemporary Comedy of Manners | 3=Urban Neurotic Comedy | 4=Conversational Moral Comedy
defn: A comedy whose engine is the conversation, codes and hypocrisies of a social milieu, from Wilde and Lubitsch high comedy to modern urban talk comedies (The Importance of Being Earnest, The Women, Metropolitan, Hannah and Her Sisters, Pauline at the Beach). A plot driven by door-slamming mechanics goes to A12-7 Farce; open social attack to A12-15 Social Satire.

label: Farce
secs: 1=Bedroom Farce | 2=Boulevard Comedy | 3=Chamber & Dinner-Party Farce | 4=Comedy of Errors & Mistaken Identity | 5=Cross-Dressing Farce
defn: A comedy driven by an accelerating mechanism of deception, mistaken identity, disguise and near-discovery, usually in a confined set (Noises Off..., The Dinner Game, Some Like It Hot, Housefull, Perfect Strangers). Talk-driven social comedy goes to A12-6 Comedy of Manners; bodily slapstick to A12-3 Slapstick.

label: Picaresque Comedy
defn: A comedy that follows a roguish or innocent hero through an episodic string of adventures across a society, often a period or literary one (Tom Jones, The Decameron, A Dog's Will, Forrest Gump, Poor Things). A settled ensemble portrait goes to A12-57 Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama.

label: Ealing Comedy
defn: A comedy from the post-war Ealing Studios cycle (1947–57) of ironic, understated British comedies about little people and institutions (Kind Hearts and Coronets, The Lavender Hill Mob, The Ladykillers).

label: Commedia all'italiana
defn: An Italian comedy of the 1958–1980 cycle that laughs bitterly at national vices, sex, family and poverty (Big Deal on Madonna Street, Divorce Italian Style, The Easy Life, We All Loved Each Other So Much).

label: Comédia à portuguesa
defn: A Portuguese popular comedy of the 1930s–40s Lisbon cycle, built on neighbourhood types, fado and city-country contrast (The Courtyard of the Ballads, O Leão da Estrela, Aldeia da Roupa Branca).

label: Bourekas Film
defn: An Israeli popular comedy of the 1960s–70s cycle built on Ashkenazi–Mizrahi ethnic stereotypes and mix-ups (Sallah Shabati, Snooker).

label: Mo lei tau
defn: Hong Kong nonsense comedy of Stephen Chow's type, mixing absurd non-sequitur, pop-culture spoof and cartoon violence (The God of Cookery, Kung Fu Hustle). A Hong Kong martial-arts action comedy goes to A12-49 Action Comedy.

label: Political Satire
secs: 1=Satire of Dictators & Regimes | 2=Campaign & Government Satire | 3=War Satire | 4=Religious Satire
