defn: A comedy whose target is political power: rulers, regimes, campaigns, wars and churches (The Great Dictator, Dr. Strangelove, The Death of Stalin, Wag the Dog, Dogma). Biblical or historical burlesque goes to A12-23 Parody & Spoof. Satire of class, lifestyle or media goes to A12-15 / A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire.

label: Social Satire
secs: 1=Class Satire | 2=Suburban & Lifestyle Satire | 3=Race Satire | 4=Satire of Tradition & Custom | 5=Corporate & Advertising Satire
defn: A comedy whose target is a social order rather than a government: class, suburbia, consumer life, race, custom or the corporation (Life Is a Long Quiet River, American Beauty, Triangle of Sadness, Thank You for Smoking, Dear White People). Satire of media and show business goes to A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire.

label: Media & Show-Business Satire
secs: 1=Hollywood Satire | 2=Television & News Satire | 3=Celebrity & Influencer Satire | 4=Fashion & Art-World Satire
defn: A satire whose target is the image industries: Hollywood, television news, celebrity and influencer culture, fashion and the art market (The Player, Network, The King of Comedy, Ingrid Goes West, Official Competition). A non-satirical backstage comedy goes to A12-32 Workplace Comedy; a fake documentary to A12-24 Mockumentary.

label: Black Comedy
secs: 1=Death & Funeral Comedy | 2=Murder Comedy | 3=Misanthropic & Taboo Comedy | 4=Revenge & Feud Comedy | 5=Escalating-Nightmare Comedy
defn: A comedy that extracts laughter from death, murder, cruelty, taboo and misfortune, without a political or social target as its main point (Arsenic and Old Lace, Harold and Maude, Happiness, Wild Tales, The Banshees of Inisherin). Satire of institutions goes to A12-14 / A12-15 Social Satire; crime plots played for laughs to the crime-comedy leaves.

label: Camp & Trash Comedy
defn: A deliberately tasteless, low-budget comedy of outrageous excess, drag and bad taste celebrated as style — the John Waters line and its kin (Pink Flamingos, Female Trouble, Polyester, Pepi, Luci, Bom). Black comedy without the trash aesthetic goes to A12-17 Black Comedy.

label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
secs: 1=Absurdist Comedy | 2=Surreal Fable | 3=Metafictional Comedy
defn: A comedy built on illogic: absurd premises played straight, dream logic, magical-realist fable or self-reflexive play with the film itself (Deerskin, Songs from the Second Floor, Arizona Dream, Adaptation.). Minimalist straight-faced comedy goes to A12-20 Deadpan.

label: Deadpan Comedy
defn: A minimalist comedy of expressionless performance, static framing and laconic timing (Drifting Clouds, Mystery Train, Divine Intervention, Whisky). Whimsical, designed indie quirk goes to A12-21 Quirky Indie Comedy.

label: Quirky Indie Comedy
defn: An American-indie comedy of whimsical eccentrics, handmade design and wry melancholy, the 'quirky' sensibility of the 2000s (Napoleon Dynamite, Moonrise Kingdom, Lars and the Real Girl, Safety Not Guaranteed).

label: Cringe Comedy
defn: A comedy whose laughter comes from social embarrassment and excruciating awkwardness sustained past comfort (The Foot Fist Way, Shiva Baby, Young Adult, Friendship).

label: Parody & Spoof
secs: 1=Genre Spoof | 2=Film & Franchise Spoof | 3=Mock-Epic & Historical Burlesque | 4=Persona & Milieu Spoof | 5=Television Parody
defn: A comedy that imitates the conventions of a genre, a specific film or franchise, a historical epic or a public persona in order to mock them (Airplane!, Young Frankenstein, Scary Movie, Monty Python and the Holy Grail, Zoolander). Spy spoofs go to A12-50 Spy Comedy; fake documentaries to A12-24 Mockumentary.

label: Mockumentary
defn: A fiction comedy formatted as a documentary, or a staged 'real' encounter with a fictional character (This Is Spinal Tap, Best in Show, Borat, Zelig).

label: Sketch Film
defn: A comedy made of separate sketches or self-contained episodes, by one troupe or several directors (Monty Python's And Now for Something Completely Different, The Kentucky Fried Movie, Coffee and Cigarettes, Movie 43, Le Plaisir).

label: Stand-Up Comedy Film
secs: 1=Theatrical Concert Films | 2=Stand-Up Specials | 3=Musical Comedy Specials | 4=Monologue & Stage-Show Films
defn: A recorded performance of stand-up or solo comic monologue, released theatrically, on television or streaming (Richard Pryor: Live in Concert, Eddie Murphy: Raw, Hannah Gadsby: Nanette, Bo Burnham: Inside).

label: Fish-out-of-Water Comedy
secs: 1=Country & City Comedy | 2=Culture-Clash & Immigrant Comedy | 3=Class-Swap & Sudden-Fortune Comedy
defn: A comedy whose engine is a character transplanted into a world whose codes they do not know: country and city, nation and culture, or class (Crocodile Dundee, Welcome to the Sticks, Trading Places, Legally Blonde, Local Hero). A transplant by magic goes to A12-28 Fantasy Comedy.

label: Fantasy Comedy
secs: 1=Body-Swap & Transformation Comedy | 2=Wish, Curse & Magic-Object Comedy | 3=Ghost, Angel & Afterlife Comedy | 4=Time-Loop & Time-Travel Comedy | 5=Talking-Animal Comedy
defn: A comedy built on a single supernatural or magical premise whose consequences drive the gags (Groundhog Day, Freaky Friday, Liar Liar, Blithe Spirit, Doctor Dolittle). A technological premise goes to A12-29 Science Fiction Comedy; fantasy adventure to A6.

label: Science Fiction Comedy
defn: A comedy built on a science-fiction premise (aliens, clones, inventions, apocalypse) whose consequences drive the gags rather than action (Coneheads, Multiplicity, Sleeper, Paul, This Is the End). Sci-fi action comedies go to A12-49 Action Comedy.

label: Buddy Comedy
secs: 1=Odd-Couple Comedy | 2=Bromance | 3=Female Buddy Comedy | 4=Bachelor-Party Comedy
defn: A comedy whose engine is a pair or small group of friends or ill-matched partners and their friction (The Odd Couple, Twins, I Love You, Man, Romy and Michele's High School Reunion, The Hangover). A buddy pair of cops goes to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film.

label: Road & Vacation Comedy
secs: 1=Road-Trip Comedy | 2=Vacation & Holiday-Resort Comedy
defn: A comedy structured by a journey or a holiday away from home, its gags arising from the trip itself (National Lampoon's European Vacation, French Fried Vacation, Flirting with Disaster, Kikujiro).

label: Workplace Comedy
secs: 1=Office Comedy | 2=Service-Industry Comedy | 3=Newsroom & Broadcast Comedy | 4=Teacher & School-Staff Comedy | 5=Medical Comedy | 6=Show-Business & Backstage Comedy
defn: A comedy set in and driven by a workplace and its hierarchy, routines and colleagues (9 to 5, Office Space, Waiting..., Broadcast News, Day for Night). Satire of the corporation as such goes to A12-15 Social Satire; the military to A12-33 Military Comedy.

label: Military Comedy
defn: A comedy of soldiers and military institutions: barracks and boot-camp service comedy, or farce set amid war (Stripes, Private Benjamin, Sgt. Bilko, La Grande Vadrouille). Satire of war itself goes to A12-14 Political Satire.

label: Sports Comedy
defn: A comedy built on a sport or competition and the underdog struggle to win it (Caddyshack, Beerfest, The Big Year, The Cup).

label: Family Comedy
secs: 1=Parenting Comedy | 2=Kid-Centred Comedy | 3=In-Law Comedy | 4=Family-Gathering Comedy | 5=Homeowner Comedy | 6=Live-Action Cartoon Comedy
defn: A comedy whose engine is family life itself: parenting chaos, troublesome kids, in-laws, family gatherings and homes (Mr. Mom, Cheaper by the Dozen, Meet the Parents, Problem Child, The Flintstones). Family comedy-drama goes to A12-52 Family Comedy-Drama; children's films to A17.

label: Wedding Comedy
defn: A comedy organised around a wedding and its preparations, guests and disasters (Father of the Bride, Bridesmaids, Monsoon Wedding, The Wedding Ringer). A comedy whose aim is the couple's love goes to A13.

label: Teen Comedy
secs: 1=High-School Comedy | 2=School-Prank Comedy | 3=Summer-Camp Comedy | 4=Party & One-Crazy-Night Comedy
defn: A comedy of adolescent social life: high-school hierarchies, school pranks, summer camp and the one wild night (Ferris Bueller's Day Off, Clueless, Mean Girls, Superbad). Teenage sexual initiation goes to A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; reflective adolescence to A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama.

label: Teen Sex Comedy
defn: A teen comedy whose plot is the quest to lose virginity or to score (Porky's, Lemon Popsicle, American Pie, Blockers).

label: College & Fraternity Comedy
defn: A comedy of campus life, fraternities and anarchic students versus the dean (National Lampoon's Animal House, Revenge of the Nerds, Old School, Neighbors).

label: Sex Comedy
defn: An adult comedy whose engine is sexual desire, temptation and frankness, including its gross-out extreme (The Seven Year Itch, The 40-Year-Old Virgin, Deuce Bigalow: Male Gigolo, No Hard Feelings). Teenagers' quest goes to A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; adultery mechanics to A12-7 Farce.

label: Stoner Film
defn: A comedy built around cannabis or other drug use and the stoned perspective (Up in Smoke, Dude, Where's My Car?, Harold & Kumar, Pineapple Express).

label: Slacker Comedy
defn: A comedy of aimless young adults hanging out, talking and avoiding work, including the low-budget mumblecore strand (Slacker, Clerks, Mallrats, Withnail and I).

label: Caper Comedy
secs: 1=Heist Comedy | 2=Con-Artist Comedy | 3=Prison Comedy
defn: A comedy organised around a planned theft, swindle or escape, the plan and its unravelling being the engine (A Fish Called Wanda, The Sting, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Stir Crazy). Amateurs stumbling into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy.

label: Gangster Comedy
secs: 1=Mob & Mafia Comedy | 2=Gangland Ensemble Comedy | 3=Hitman Comedy
defn: A comedy set among professional criminals — the mob, gangland crews and hitmen (Analyze This, Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, Snatch, In Bruges). Civilians drawn into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; hitman action vehicles to A12-49 Action Comedy.

label: Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy
secs: 1=Kidnapping & Hostage Comedy | 2=Get-Rich-Quick Crime Comedy | 3=Body & Cover-Up Comedy | 4=Wrong-Place Civilians
defn: A crime comedy in which ordinary people botch a kidnapping, robbery, killing or cover-up, the escalating mess being the engine (Ruthless People, Raising Arizona, Horrible Bosses, Delhi Belly). Planned professional jobs go to A12-43 Caper Comedy.

label: Comedy Mystery
defn: A comic whodunit or detective comedy in which a mystery is investigated for laughs (Clue, Fletch, The Big Lebowski, See How They Run).

label: Cop Comedy
defn: A comedy of bungling police, cadets and security guards as an institution, without the action-buddy formula (Police Academy, Super Troopers, Torrente, Paul Blart: Mall Cop).

label: Buddy Cop Film
defn: An action comedy pairing two mismatched partners, at least one a cop, on a case (Beverly Hills Cop, Taxi, The Nice Guys, Let's Be Cops).

label: Action Comedy
secs: 1=Adventure & Chase Action Comedy | 2=Assassin Action Comedy | 3=Martial-Arts Action Comedy | 4=Sci-Fi Action Comedy
defn: A comedy whose set pieces are action — chases, fights, shoot-outs, martial arts or sci-fi spectacle — played for laughs (Armour of God, Men in Black, The Hitman's Bodyguard, The Lost City). Cop pairs go to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; spies to A12-50 Spy Comedy.

label: Spy Comedy
secs: 1=Spy Spoof | 2=Action Spy Comedy | 3=Spy Thrillers Played for Laughs
defn: A comedy built on espionage, either spoofing the spy genre or using spy action for comedy (Austin Powers, OSS 117, Johnny English, Charlie's Angels, The Spy Who Dumped Me).

label: Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=Childhood | 2=Adolescence | 3=Young Adulthood
defn: A comedy-drama about growing up, from childhood through the first steps of adulthood (Amarcord, Juno, Frances Ha, Boy, Ghost World). Purely comic teen films go to A12-37 Teen Comedy.

label: Family Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=Family Reunion & Holiday Dramedy | 2=Parent & Adult-Child Dramedy | 3=Sibling Dramedy | 4=Dysfunctional-Family Dramedy
defn: A comedy-drama of a family's tensions and attachments, usually dysfunctional (The Royal Tenenbaums, Parenthood, The Farewell, This Is Where I Leave You). Comic family chaos goes to A12-35 Family Comedy.

label: Marital Comedy-Drama
defn: A comedy-drama of a marriage under strain — affairs, divorce, therapy, the long haul (Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice, Heartburn, This Is 40, Hope Springs). Courtship goes to A13; remarriage plots to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage.

label: Midlife Crisis Comedy
secs: 1=Midlife Crisis | 2=Old-Age & Retirement Comedy
defn: A comedy or comedy-drama about middle and later life: the midlife crisis, retirement, ageing and late awakening (City Slickers, Sideways, About Schmidt, Grumpy Old Men, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel).

label: Tragicomedy
defn: A comedy-drama facing illness, grief, addiction or death, whose humour coexists with real loss (Steel Magnolias, 50/50, The Barbarian Invasions, The Bucket List).

label: Ensemble Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=Reunion & Friendship Ensemble | 2=Community Underdog Comedy
defn: A comedy-drama of a group of friends or a community whose interlocking stories carry the film, including the reunion film and the community underdog comedy (The Big Chill, Diner, Short Cuts, The Full Monty, Calendar Girls).

label: Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=City & Neighbourhood | 2=Village & Small-Town Comedy | 3=Artists & Writers
defn: A gently comic comedy-drama observing everyday life in a neighbourhood, town or creative milieu, with little plot engine (Marius, Smoke, Happy-Go-Lucky, Cutting It Short, The Horse's Mouth).

label: LGBTQ Comedy
defn: A comedy or comedy-drama whose premise is queer identity — coming out, drag, queer family or a gay wedding (The Wedding Banquet, But I'm a Cheerleader, Breakfast on Pluto, Loose Cannons). Cross-dressing as disguise goes to A12-7 Farce.

label: Commedia sexy all'italiana
defn: The Italian erotic comedy cycle of c. 1970–1985: schoolteachers, nurses, policewomen and maids (Edwige Fenech, Gloria Guida, Lino Banfi, Alvaro Vitali) in bawdy, voyeuristic farces descended from the commedia all'italiana and the decamerotici (Malizia, L'insegnante).

label: Carry On Film
defn: The British Carry On series (Peter Rogers and Gerald Thomas, 1958–1978, revived 1992): seaside-postcard innuendo, a stock company (Sid James, Kenneth Williams, Hattie Jacques, Barbara Windsor) and genre and institution parodies (Carry On Nurse, Carry On Up the Khyber).

label: Chanchada
defn: The Brazilian popular musical comedy of the 1930s–1950s, above all Atlântida's carnival films with Oscarito and Grande Otelo: samba numbers, burlesque and parodies of Hollywood (Carnaval Atlântida, Nem Sansão Nem Dalila). Its erotic successor is A15-6 Pornochanchada.

label: Star-Crossed Romance
secs: 1=Romeo and Juliet Stories | 2=Class-Crossed Love | 3=Interfaith, Interethnic & Interracial Love | 4=Love Against Custom & State
defn: A love story whose engine is an outside force forbidding the match: feuding families, class or caste, religion or ethnicity, custom, state or law (Romeo + Juliet, Bombay, Jungle Fever, Cold War). A comic treatment of the same obstacle goes to the romantic-comedy leaves; a wartime separation goes to A13-6.

label: Romantic Melodrama & Weepie
secs: 1=Woman's Film & Sacrificial Melodrama | 2=Illness & Dying-Lover Weepies | 3=Grief & Widowhood Romances | 4=Amnesia & Memory-Loss Romances | 5=Sentimental Small-Town Romances
defn: A love story built to move the audience to tears through suffering, sacrifice, illness, death or loss (Now, Voyager, Love Story, The Fault in Our Stars, The Notebook). The tearjerker and the woman's film; an obsessive, self-destroying love goes to A13-3.

label: Amour Fou & Obsessive Love
secs: 1=Self-Destructive Devotion | 2=Possessive & Jealous Love | 3=Outlaw Lovers
defn: A love story whose engine is the lovers' own excessive, possessive or self-destroying passion rather than an outside obstacle (Devdas, Leaving Las Vegas, Loulou, Kabir Singh). Where sex itself is the subject the title goes to A15-1.

label: Adultery & Love Triangle
secs: 1=Brief Affairs & Unconsummated Love | 2=Adultery & Marital Betrayal | 3=Love Triangles | 4=Temptation & Fidelity Tales
defn: A love story driven by a third party: an affair, a betrayal of marriage, two rivals for one heart, or a temptation resisted (Brief Encounter, In the Mood for Love, Closer, My Night at Maud's). A comic triangle goes to the romantic-comedy leaves.

label: Relationship Drama
secs: 1=Chance Encounters | 2=A Couple over the Years | 3=Long-Distance & Epistolary Love | 4=Breakups & Marital Crisis | 5=Late-Life & May–December Love
defn: A love story with no outside obstacle whose subject is one couple's relationship itself: its chance beginning, its course over years, separation by distance, breakdown, or love late in life (Before Sunrise, Past Lives, Blue Valentine, Like Crazy). An affair or triangle goes to A13-4; a weepie of illness to A13-2.

label: Wartime Romance
defn: A love story whose engine is war: lovers met, parted or endangered by a war that stays in the background of the romance (Casablanca, Waterloo Bridge, The English Patient, Dear John). A film about the fighting goes to A9.

label: Period Romance
secs: 1=Literary Classic Adaptations | 2=Original Period Love Stories
defn: A love story set in a reconstructed past, where period manners, dress and social codes shape the courtship: classic novel adaptations and original period love stories (Wuthering Heights, Titanic, Far and Away, Lady Chatterley's Lover). Heritage romance; a wartime love story goes to A13-6.

label: Teen Romance
secs: 1=First Love & Summer Romance | 2=High-School Romance | 3=Teen Romantic Comedy | 4=New-Adult & Bad-Boy Romance
defn: A love story whose lovers are adolescents or just past adolescence, built on first love, school and youth (Say Anything..., The Spectacular Now, To All the Boys I've Loved Before, After). Queer teen love goes to A13-9; a teen weepie of illness to A13-2.

label: LGBTQ+ Romance
secs: 1=Gay Male Romance | 2=Lesbian & Sapphic Romance | 3=Queer First Love & Coming Out | 4=Queer Romantic Comedy
defn: A love story between lovers of the same sex or across gender identity, where queer desire is the romance (Brokeback Mountain, Carol, Call Me by Your Name, Fire Island). A queer movement film of the early 1990s goes to A1.

label: Pink Neorealism
defn: Italian 1950s romantic comedy that keeps neorealism's poor settings and non-star manner but turns them to sentimental courtship (Two Cents Worth of Hope). Neorealismo rosa.

label: Romantic Comedy of Manners
secs: 1=Continental Sophisticated Comedy | 2=Urban Neurotic Comedy | 3=Shakespearean & Austen Comedy | 4=Ensemble Roundelay
defn: A witty, talk-driven romantic comedy whose engine is the social and sexual manners of a milieu, usually urban, sophisticated or literary (Ninotchka, Smiles of a Summer Night, Annie Hall, Bridget Jones's Diary). A farcical screwball goes to A13-10.

label: Sex Comedy
secs: 1=Hollywood Sex Comedy | 2=Gross-Out Romantic Comedy | 3=Hook-Up & Dating Comedy
defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is sex and the rules of dating: seduction, sexual mores, hook-ups and the failures of the dating market (Pillow Talk, There's Something About Mary, Knocked Up, How to Be Single). A teen sex comedy goes to A12.

label: Meet-Cute Romantic Comedy
secs: 1=Destiny & Near-Miss | 2=Epistolary & Pen-Pal | 3=Holiday-Abroad Romance
defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is the contrived or fated first meeting and the near misses that follow, including courtship by letter and the romance of a trip (Sleepless in Seattle, Serendipity, You've Got Mail, French Kiss). The friends who were already there go to A13-17.

label: Enemies to Lovers
secs: 1=Bickering Rivals | 2=Opposites Attract
defn: A romantic comedy whose couple begins in hostility, rivalry or total mismatch and fights its way to love (The Quiet Man, The Ugly Truth, Hum Tum, Anyone But You). Battle-of-the-sexes and opposites-attract comedy; rivals at work go to A13-19.

label: Fake Relationship
secs: 1=Fake Dating & Marriages of Convenience | 2=Bets & Wagers | 3=Disguise & Mistaken Identity | 4=Matchmakers & Cyrano Schemes
defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a pretence: a fake engagement or marriage of convenience, a bet, a disguise or mistaken identity, or a matchmaker's scheme (Green Card, The Proposal, How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, Hitch). A teen bet comedy goes to A13-8.

label: Friends to Lovers
secs: 1=Friends Becoming Lovers | 2=Friends with Benefits
defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a friendship that turns, slowly or suddenly, into love, including the friends-with-benefits arrangement (When Harry Met Sally..., Love, Rosie, Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na, Friends with Benefits). A dramatic version spanning years goes to A13-5.

label: Cinderella Story
secs: 1=Cinderella & Makeover | 2=Royal & Political Romance | 3=Celebrity & Commoner Romance
defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a match across wealth or rank in which one lover is raised into the other's world: makeover, royalty, celebrity (Pretty Woman, Roman Holiday, Notting Hill, Maid in Manhattan). A forbidding, tragic class divide goes to A13-1.

label: Workplace Romantic Comedy
defn: A romantic comedy whose couple meets and spars through a shared job, office or profession (Desk Set, Office Romance, Working Girl, Two Weeks Notice). Career-woman comedy; workplace enemies with no job plot go to A13-15.

label: Wedding Comedy
secs: 1=Brides, Grooms & Wedding Planning | 2=Wedding Guests & Crashers | 3=Meet-the-Family & Arranged Marriage
defn: A romantic comedy organised around a wedding: brides and planners, guests and crashers, or the clash of two families and arranged matches (Four Weddings and a Funeral, My Best Friend's Wedding, My Big Fat Greek Wedding, Band Baaja Baaraat). A wedding as one scene only does not count.

label: Holiday Romantic Comedy
defn: A romantic comedy built on a calendar holiday that sets its deadline and mood: Christmas, New Year, Valentine's Day (The Irony of Fate, Valentine's Day, Holidate). Christmas only as backdrop does not count.

label: Romantic Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=Deadpan & Eccentric Lovers | 2=Damaged & Healing Lovers | 3=Single Parents & Second Chances | 4=Age-Gap & Late-Life Love Comedy | 5=Homecoming & Small-Town Romance
defn: A romantic comedy played half-seriously, whose obstacle lies in the lovers' own eccentricity, damage, family burdens or age (Moonstruck, As Good as It Gets, Silver Linings Playbook, Something's Gotta Give). A purely dramatic treatment goes to A13-5.

label: Romantic Fantasy
secs: 1=Ghost & Afterlife Romance | 2=Time-Travel & Time-Slip Romance | 3=Paranormal & Creature Romance | 4=Science-Fiction & AI Romance | 5=Magic, Curse & Body-Switch Romance | 6=Time-Loop & Parallel-Life Romance
defn: A love story, dramatic or comic, whose engine is a fantastic or speculative device: ghosts and afterlife, time travel, supernatural creatures, machines, magic or a time loop (Ghost, Somewhere in Time, Twilight, Her, Palm Springs). Where the device dominates and love is secondary the title goes to A5 or A6.

label: Telefoni Bianchi
defn: The Italian sentimental and sophisticated comedies of c. 1932–1943 ('white telephone' films), set among department stores, hotels and Art Deco apartments, after Hollywood and Hungarian models (Mario Camerini, Vittorio De Sica, Mario Soldati): What Scoundrels Men Are!, Il signor Max.

label: Book Musical
secs: 1=Hollywood Studio Musicals | 2=Broadway Adaptations | 3=Family & Fantasy Musicals | 4=Teen & High-School Musicals | 5=Contemporary Screen Originals | 6=European & World Film Musicals | 7=Astaire–Rogers RKO Musicals (1933–1939)
defn: A musical film whose songs and dances arise inside the story and carry plot and character, written for the screen or adapted from the stage (Top Hat, Meet Me in St. Louis, West Side Story, La La Land). Numbers staged as performances go to A14-4; an all-sung film to A14-5.

label: Operetta Film
defn: A musical film in the operetta tradition, light romantic plots in a mythical Ruritania or old Europe told through sung waltzes and duets (The Love Parade, Love Me Tonight, Naughty Marietta, Ulduz).

label: Revue Film
defn: A plotless or nearly plotless film made of separate musical and comic numbers, the screen form of the stage revue (King of Jazz, Ziegfeld Follies).

label: Backstage Musical
secs: 1=Broadway & Revue Backstage | 2=Hollywood & Stardom | 3=Cabaret, Nightclub & Showgirl
defn: A musical film about putting on a show, whose numbers are staged as performances within the story (42nd Street, Singin' in the Rain, The Band Wagon, Cabaret). Integrated numbers go to A14-1; a musician's story without numbers goes to A14-13.

label: Opera Film & Sung-Through Musical
secs: 1=Filmed & Adapted Opera | 2=Sung-Through Screen Musicals | 3=Traditional Music-Theatre Forms
defn: A film entirely or almost entirely sung: a filmed or adapted opera, a sung-through screen musical, or a traditional sung music-theatre form (The Tales of Hoffmann, The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, Chunhyang, Annette). A rock opera goes to A14-6.

label: Rock Opera & Rock Musical
defn: A musical film set to rock music, a sung rock narrative or stage rock musical (Tommy, Jesus Christ Superstar, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Hedwig and the Angry Inch). A musical built on existing hits goes to A14-7.

label: Jukebox Musical
defn: A musical film whose numbers are previously released popular songs, often one artist's catalogue (Mamma Mia!, Across the Universe, Moulin Rouge!, Sunshine on Leith). A biopic of the artist goes to A11.

label: Pop Star Vehicle
defn: A fiction film built to showcase a singer or band playing a version of themselves through their songs (Jailhouse Rock, A Hard Day's Night, Purple Rain, Spice World). A concert record goes to A19.

label: Filmed Stage Musical
secs: 1=Pro-Shot Theatre Recordings | 2=Live Television Musicals
defn: A recording of a stage musical as performed in the theatre, or broadcast live, rather than re-made for the camera (Hamilton, Cats (1998), Grease Live!). Weakly attested label (trade: pro-shot); a screen adaptation goes to A14-1.

label: Visual Album
defn: A feature-length film made to accompany a music album, its songs strung into an impressionistic narrative (Lemonade, Dirty Computer, Black Is King).

label: Dance Film
secs: 1=Ballet & Concert Dance | 2=Flamenco Dance Film | 3=Ballroom & Social Dance | 4=Disco & Teen Dance | 5=Street & Hip-Hop Dance | 6=Striptease & Burlesque Dance
defn: A fiction film whose story is carried by dance and dancers, its climaxes danced performances or competitions (The Red Shoes, Saturday Night Fever, Dirty Dancing, Step Up). A sung musical goes to A14-1.

label: Rumberas Film
defn: Mexican golden-age cabaret melodrama starring a rumba dancer, the rumbera (Victims of Sin).

label: Music Film
secs: 1=Jazz & Blues Lives | 2=Bands & Rock Dreams | 3=Hip-Hop, DJ & Electronic | 4=Singers & Stardom | 5=Choirs, Classical Music & Teachers | 6=Music & Family | 7=Competitions & Battles of the Bands
defn: A fiction film about musicians and music-making whose music is performed in the story but which is not a musical: bands, singers, players, teachers, contests (Whiplash, Once, 8 Mile, Pitch Perfect). A biopic of a real musician goes to A11; a documentary to A19.

label: Comedia Ranchera
defn: The Mexican ranch musical of the Golden Age (1936–1950s): singing charros (Tito Guízar, Jorge Negrete, Pedro Infante), haciendas, serenades, cockfights and rival suitors (Allá en el Rancho Grande, ¡Ay Jalisco, no te rajes!, Dos tipos de cuidado).

label: Huangmei Opera Film
defn: The sung costume romance in Huangmei-opera style, launched in Hong Kong by Li Han-hsiang at Shaw Brothers (1958–1960s) after the mainland Heavenly Match: legendary lovers, cross-dressing heroines, palace and garden sets (The Kingdom and the Beauty, The Love Eterne).

label: Erotic Drama
secs: 1=Sexual Awakening | 2=Obsession & Transgression | 3=Sadomasochism & Power Games | 4=Unsimulated-Sex Art Film | 5=Erotic Romance Bestsellers
defn: A narrative film whose subject is sexual desire, practice or obsession, shown explicitly as the core of the drama (Last Tango in Paris, In the Realm of the Senses, Secretary, Fifty Shades of Grey). A love story with sex scenes goes to A13; a suspense plot to A15-2.

label: Erotic Thriller
defn: A thriller whose suspense is driven by sexual desire, seduction or perversity (The Housemaid, Eyes Wide Shut, A Snake of June). A mainstream erotic thriller led by crime goes to A3.

label: Softcore Film
secs: 1=Emmanuelle & French Softcore | 2=European Erotic Auteurs (Franco, Borowczyk, Metzger) | 3=American Softcore
defn: A film of simulated sex made for erotic display, often in the European erotic tradition (Immoral Tales, Vampyros Lesbos, Delta of Venus).

label: Sexploitation
secs: 1=Sex-Hygiene Roadshow Film | 2=Nudie-Cuties & Roughies | 3=Russ Meyer | 4=Nunsploitation | 5=Naziploitation | 6=Women-in-Prison Film
defn: A low-budget independent film made to exploit sex and nudity, from roadshow sex-hygiene films to Russ Meyer and nunsploitation (Mom and Dad, Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!, Ilsa, the Wicked Warden).

label: Pink Film
secs: 1=First Wave (1962–1971) | 2=Nikkatsu Roman Porno (1971–1988) | 3=Pink Shitennō (Four Heavenly Kings, 1985–2000) | 4=Seven Lucky Gods of Pink (1994–) | 5=Roman Porno Reboot (2016–2017)
defn: Japanese theatrical softcore cinema (pinku eiga) of the independent studios and Nikkatsu's Roman Porno line. Kept as an attested canon although no title in the present corpus belongs here.

label: Pornochanchada
defn: Brazilian erotic comedy and drama of the 1970s–80s made around São Paulo's Boca do Lixo (A Dama do Lotação).

label: Hong Kong Category III Film
secs: 1=Erotic Category III | 2=True-Crime & Shock Category III
defn: A Hong Kong film of the adults-only Category III rating cycle (1988 onward, peaking in the early 1990s): sex-and-violence exploitation, erotic costume romps (Sex and Zen) and lurid true-crime shockers (The Untold Story, Ebola Syndrome). Defined by the named Hong Kong cycle rather than one plot type.

label: Shomingeki (Shoshimin-eiga)
defn: A Japanese studio drama of ordinary lower-middle-class urban life: salarymen, households, marriages arranged and parents left behind, told at the scale of the home (Tokyo Story, Late Spring, I Was Born, But...). Non-Japanese family dramas go to A16-3 or A16-4.

label: Family Saga
defn: A drama that follows one family across generations or decades, the passing of time and inheritance of fortune being the engine (The Magnificent Ambersons, Giant, Fanny and Alexander, The Best of Youth). A drama confined to one crisis in one generation goes to A16-3 or A16-4.

label: Family Drama
secs: 1=Sibling Dramas | 2=Family Gatherings & Reunions | 3=Inheritance, Feuds & Family Fortunes | 4=Bereaved Families | 5=Foster, Adoptive & Found Families
defn: A drama whose engine is the family as a group rather than one parent–child pair: siblings, the family gathered for a holiday or funeral, the inheritance, the household after a death, the chosen or foster family (Still Walking, Rachel Getting Married, Shoplifters, Ordinary People). One parent and child at the centre goes to A16-4; a couple to A16-5.

label: Parent–Child Drama
secs: 1=Fathers & Sons | 2=Fathers & Daughters | 3=Mothers & Children | 4=Ageing Parents & Adult Children
defn: A drama centred on one parent and child — the father–son or mother–daughter bond strained, broken or repaired (The Return, Aftersun, Autumn Sonata, Mommy, On Golden Pond). A drama of the whole family goes to A16-3; Japanese shomingeki to A16-1.

label: Domestic Drama
secs: 1=Marriage in Crisis | 2=Adultery | 3=Divorce & Custody
defn: A drama of the married couple at home — the marriage worn down, betrayed or dissolved (Scenes from a Marriage, Revolutionary Road, Kramer vs. Kramer, Marriage Story). A romance that ends in marriage goes to A13; the wider family to A16-3.

label: Melodrama
secs: 1=Maternal Melodrama | 2=Woman's Film | 3=Family Melodrama | 4=Illness Tearjerkers
defn: A drama in the melodramatic mode — heightened emotion, sacrifice and fate carried by music and mise-en-scène, usually centred on a suffering woman or family (Stella Dallas, All That Heaven Allows, Imitation of Life, All About My Mother). Realist family dramas go to A16-3 to A16-5.

label: Psychological Drama
secs: 1=Grief & Mourning | 2=Breakdown & Mental Illness | 3=Trauma, Abuse & Guilt | 4=Obsession & Desire
defn: A drama whose engine is one person's inner state — grief, breakdown, trauma or obsession — rendered from inside (Three Colors: Blue, Through a Glass Darkly, Manchester by the Sea, Death in Venice). Where suspense drives it, see A3; where the crisis is existential rather than psychological, A16-8.

label: Existentialist Film
secs: 1=Modernist Alienation | 2=Ennui of the Affluent | 3=Double Lives & Masks | 4=Rise-and-Fall Lives | 5=Midlife & Old Age
defn: An art-film character study whose engine is a crisis of meaning — alienation, ennui, a life weighed up or a self disguised (La Dolce Vita, The Silence, Lost in Translation, The Passenger, Citizen Kane). A clinical inner state goes to A16-7; a quiet everyday portrait to A16-9.

label: Slice of Life
secs: 1=Everyday Lives | 2=Drifters & Loners
defn: A drama with no plot engine beyond daily life observed — routines, small encounters and drifting days (Paterson, Perfect Days, Wanda, Wendy and Lucy). A crisis of meaning goes to A16-8; a journey to A16-36.

label: Chamber Drama (Kammerspiel)
defn: A drama confined to a few characters in one space or one conversation, the dialogue being the action (My Dinner with Andre, Tape, The Sunset Limited, Locke). A filmed stage production goes to A16-12 when it is about performers.

label: Hyperlink Cinema
defn: An ensemble drama of several separate storylines linked by chance, place or a shared event (Magnolia, 21 Grams, Babel, Crash). A single family's ensemble goes to A16-3.

label: Artist Film (Künstlerroman)
secs: 1=Filmmakers & the Film World | 2=Actors & Performers | 3=Musicians | 4=Writers & Painters
defn: A drama of a fictional artist or performer whose art or career is the engine — the actor, filmmaker, musician, writer or painter at work and in crisis (8½, All About Eve, Tár, La belle noiseuse). Real artists' lives go to A11; musicals to A14.

label: Coming-of-Age Film
secs: 1=Childhood at Home | 2=City Childhoods | 3=Village & Country Childhoods | 4=Summers Away | 5=Childhood under War & Dictatorship | 6=Boarding-School Childhoods
defn: A drama of a child's or young adolescent's passage toward understanding, told from the child's side (The Spirit of the Beehive, My Life as a Dog, Stand by Me, Boyhood). High-school teen life goes to A16-14; delinquency to A16-15.

label: Teen Film
secs: 1=High School & Friendship | 2=First Love & Sexual Awakening
defn: A drama of teenage life in its own institutions — high school, cliques, first love and sexual awakening (The Breakfast Club, Lady Bird, Eighth Grade, Murmur of the Heart). Rebellion and crisis go to A16-15; teen comedies to A12; teen romance to A13.

label: Juvenile Delinquency Film
secs: 1=Street Gangs | 2=Rebels & Runaways | 3=Youth Subcultures | 4=Teens in Crisis
defn: A drama of youth in revolt or in danger — gangs, rebels, subcultures and teenagers in crisis (Rebel Without a Cause, The Outsiders, This Is England, Thirteen); includes the Japanese taiyōzoku cycle (Crazed Fruit). Crime-driven youth gangs go to A2.

label: Campus Film
defn: A drama set in a college or university, or among its just-graduated (Starter for 10, Higher Learning, St. Elmo's Fire). High school goes to A16-14; campus comedy to A12.

label: Teacher Film
defn: A drama whose engine is a teacher and a class — the inspirational, embattled or failing educator (To Sir, with Love, Dead Poets Society, The Class, The Teachers' Lounge). Pupils' own stories go to A16-13 or A16-14.

label: LGBTQ Film
secs: 1=Coming Out | 2=Queer Love & Community | 3=Trans & Intersex Lives
defn: A drama whose engine is queer identity — coming out, queer love and community, or trans life (Beautiful Thing, Moonlight, The Boys in the Band, A Fantastic Woman). A queer love story foregrounding romance goes to A13; the 1990s movement to A1.

label: Social Realism
secs: 1=Working Lives & Labour | 2=Unemployment & Precarity | 3=Street Life & Slums | 4=Rural & Peasant Life
defn: A drama of ordinary working or poor people shown in their material conditions — labour, unemployment, the street, the village (Salt of the Earth, Rosetta, I, Daniel Blake, Salaam Bombay!). A drama built around one named social issue goes to A16-22; Italian neorealism and kitchen-sink realism as movements to A1.

label: Banlieue Film
defn: A French drama of the multi-ethnic housing estates of the urban periphery, youth and police at its centre (La Haine, Girlhood, Les Misérables). Non-French urban dramas go to A16-19.

label: Immigrant Film
secs: 1=Arrival & New Lives | 2=Second Generation | 3=Crossings & Refugees
defn: A drama whose engine is migration — the crossing, the arrival in a new country, or the second generation between cultures (El Norte, Minari, My Beautiful Laundrette, Io Capitano). Migration as backdrop to a crime goes to A2.

label: Social Problem Film
secs: 1=Alcoholism | 2=Drug Addiction | 3=Gambling | 4=Race & Caste | 5=Youth Violence & Reform Schools | 6=Sexual Violence & Reproductive Rights | 7=Patriarchy & Women's Rights | 8=Prostitution & Trafficking
defn: A drama built to expose one named social ill — addiction, racism, sexual violence, the oppression of women, prostitution (The Lost Weekend, Gentleman's Agreement, Requiem for a Dream, Moolaadé). Diffuse working-class hardship goes to A16-19; the courtroom to A16-25.

label: Political Drama
secs: 1=Power & Office | 2=Activism & Revolution | 3=Life under Repression | 4=Conflict & Extremism
defn: A drama whose engine is political power — winning and abusing office, resisting it, or living under it (Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Candidate, Yol, Leviathan). Political thrillers go to A3; war to A9.

label: Journalism Film
defn: A drama of reporters and the press, the getting or abusing of a story being the engine (Ace in the Hole, Good Night, and Good Luck., She Said). Newspaper thrillers go to A3.

label: Legal Drama
secs: 1=Criminal Trials | 2=Political & War-Crimes Trials | 3=Courts-Martial | 4=Wrongful Conviction & Death Penalty | 5=Lawyers & Civil Suits
defn: A drama of the law in action — the trial, the lawyer's case, the wrongful conviction (12 Angry Men, To Kill a Mockingbird, Anatomy of a Murder, Anatomy of a Fall). A whodunit with a courtroom climax goes to A3.

label: Medical Drama
secs: 1=Doctors, Nurses & Carers | 2=Terminal Illness | 3=Disability | 4=Dementia
defn: A drama whose engine is illness, disability or medicine — the dying patient, the disabled life, dementia, the doctor's work (Ikiru, The Father, Scent of a Woman, Bringing Out the Dead). Mental illness as inner state goes to A16-7.

label: Religious Drama
secs: 1=Priests & Pastors | 2=Nuns & Convents | 3=Believers & Seekers
defn: A drama whose engine is faith — the priest's or nun's vocation, doubt, conversion or fanaticism (Diary of a Country Priest, Winter Light, Ida, First Reformed). Evangelical industry films go to A16-28; biblical epics to A8.

label: Christian Film
defn: A film made by or for the evangelical Christian film industry, whose plot affirms faith (Fireproof, God's Not Dead, The Shack); includes the early race-film religious dramas (The Blood of Jesus). Art-house faith dramas go to A16-27.

label: Sports Film
secs: 1=Ice & Snow Sports | 2=Cricket, Rugby & Other Field Games | 3=Golf, Tennis & Table Tennis | 4=Running, Swimming & Rowing | 5=Gymnastics & Cheerleading | 6=Surfing, Skating & BMX | 7=Horse Racing & Cycling | 8=Pool, Bowling & Board Games | 9=Wrestling & Martial Combat
defn: A drama whose engine is athletic contest outside the sports given their own leaves — ice and snow, field games, golf and racket sports, athletics, gymnastics, boards, racing animals and bicycles, cue games and combat sports (Chariots of Fire, The Hustler, Miracle, Lagaan). Boxing, baseball, American football, basketball, football and motor racing have leaves A16-30 to A16-35.

label: Boxing Film
defn: A sports drama of the prizefighter and the ring, including cage fighting (Rocky, Fat City, Million Dollar Baby, Creed).

label: Baseball Film
defn: A sports drama of baseball (The Pride of the Yankees, The Natural, Bull Durham, Moneyball).

label: American Football Film
defn: A sports drama of American (gridiron) football (Rudy, Remember the Titans, Friday Night Lights, Any Given Sunday).

label: Basketball Film
defn: A sports drama of basketball (Hoosiers, He Got Game, Coach Carter, Love & Basketball).

label: Association Football Film
defn: A sports drama of association football (Victory, Bend It Like Beckham, Goal! The Dream Begins, Next Goal Wins).

label: Auto Racing Film
defn: A sports drama of motor racing (Grand Prix, Le Mans, Rush, Ford v Ferrari).

label: Road Movie
secs: 1=Family Road Trips | 2=On the Run | 3=Motorcycle Journeys | 4=Pilgrimages & Long Walks | 5=Quests of Search & Memory | 6=Drifters & Nomads
defn: A drama whose engine is the journey itself — leaving home, the open road and what it changes (Wild Strawberries, Thelma & Louise, The Straight Story, Nomadland). A journey driven by the bond of two friends goes to A16-37; migrant crossings to A16-21.

label: Buddy Film
secs: 1=Male Buddies | 2=Female Buddies | 3=Mismatched Pairs | 4=Gangs of Friends
defn: A film whose engine is the friendship of two (or a small band of) companions, here mostly on a trip together (Planes, Trains & Automobiles, Rain Man, Y tu mamá también, The Trip). Cop-buddy action goes to A7; pure road comedy also to A12.

label: Animal Film
secs: 1=Dogs | 2=Horses | 3=Wild & Farm Animals
defn: A drama whose engine is the bond between people and an animal, or an animal's own odyssey (Lassie Come Home, The Black Stallion, Au hasard Balthazar, Hachi: A Dog's Tale). Animated talking-animal films go to C12; wildlife documentary to A19.

label: Pre-Code Hollywood Film
secs: 1=Fallen Women & Kept Women | 2=Gold Diggers & Working Girls | 3=Social-Conscience & Forgotten-Man Films
defn: The Hollywood dramas of c. 1929–1934, between the coming of sound and strict enforcement of the Production Code, that treated sex, adultery, prostitution, crime and Depression misery with a frankness later forbidden (Baby Face, Red-Headed Woman, Heroes for Sale). Pre-Code gangster, horror and musical films stay in their genres.

label: Brat Pack Film
defn: The mid-1980s American youth films starring the 'Brat Pack' (Emilio Estevez, Molly Ringwald, Judd Nelson, Ally Sheedy, Andrew McCarthy, Rob Lowe, Demi Moore, Anthony Michael Hall), above all John Hughes's teen films and Joel Schumacher's post-college ensemble (The Breakfast Club, St. Elmo's Fire).

label: Heimatfilm
secs: 1=Classic Heimatfilm (1947–1960s) | 2=Anti-Heimatfilm (1968–1970s)
defn: The German and Austrian homeland film, dominant c. 1947–1960s: Alpine, Black Forest and heath landscapes, foresters, dirndls, folk song and reconciled village communities (Black Forest Girl, Grün ist die Heide), and the critical Neuer or Anti-Heimatfilm of the late 1960s–70s that inverted it.

label: Rubble Film (Trümmerfilm)
defn: The German films of 1946–1949 shot among the bombed ruins, about guilt, returning soldiers, black markets and survival in the immediate post-war (The Murderers Are Among Us, In Those Days).

label: Children's Fantasy Film
secs: 1=Musical & Magical-Nanny Fantasy | 2=Storybook & Roald Dahl Adaptations | 3=Creature & Magic-Friend Fantasy | 4=Halloween & Spooky Family Fantasy
defn: A fantasy made first for children, in which magic, a magical nanny, a creature friend or a spooky night enters a child's world (Mary Poppins, Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory, Pete's Dragon, The Witches). A wizarding-school saga goes to A6-6; a Disney Channel television film to A17-6.

label: Animal Adventure Film
secs: 1=Dog Films | 2=Talking-Animal & CGI-Hybrid Films | 3=Wild-Animal & Horse Stories
defn: A family film whose hero is an animal: a dog, horse, whale or talking creature, live or computer-generated (Homeward Bound: The Incredible Journey, Babe, Free Willy, Paddington). An animated feature goes to C12.

label: Children's Adventure Film
secs: 1=Gang & Treasure Adventures | 2=Kid Spies & Kid Capers
defn: A family adventure in which a gang of children or a child hero goes treasure-hunting, on the run, or undercover as a kid spy (The Goonies, Holes, Spy Kids: Armageddon, Agent Cody Banks). A child alone at home at Christmas goes to A17-9.

label: Children's Drama
secs: 1=Classic Children's Novel Adaptations | 2=Contemporary & World Children's Drama
defn: A serious film for and about children: a classic children's novel or a contemporary story of a child facing illness, difference, grief or loneliness (The Secret Garden 1993, A Little Princess, Like Stars on Earth, Wonder). A coming-of-age drama for adults goes to A16.

label: Family Comedy
secs: 1=Kid-Lit & School Comedies | 2=Kid-in-Charge & Slapstick Mischief | 3=Family-Man Comedies | 4=Live-Action Cartoon, Comic & Puppet Films | 5=Television, Toy & Web Spin-off Films
defn: A comedy made for the whole family whose engine is a child's mischief, school life, a parent's mishaps or a cartoon brought to the screen (Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Dennis the Menace, The Game Plan, The Muppets Take Manhattan). A comedy built on magic goes to A6-9 or A17-1; a comedy for adults to A12.

label: Disney Channel Original Movie
secs: 1=Tween Musicals | 2=Magic & Monster DCOMs | 3=Tween Comedy & Sports DCOMs
defn: A made-for-television feature of the Disney Channel tradition for tweens and teens: musicals, magic-and-monster comedies and school or sports stories (High School Musical, Halloweentown, Descendants, Cadet Kelly). A theatrical family comedy goes to A17-5.

label: Christmas Carol Adaptation
defn: A film adapting Dickens's A Christmas Carol: a miser visited by ghosts of Christmas past, present and future, straight or updated (A Christmas Carol 1951, Scrooge, Scrooged, The Muppet Christmas Carol).

label: Christmas Fantasy Film
secs: 1=Santa Claus Films | 2=Angels & Christmas Miracles | 3=Christmas Action & Horror
defn: A Christmas film whose engine is the holiday's magic: Santa Claus and his workshop, an angel or Christmas miracle, or Santa turned action hero (Miracle on 34th Street, It's a Wonderful Life, Elf, The Santa Clause). Dickens's ghosts go to A17-7.

label: Christmas Family Comedy
secs: 1=Kids at Christmas & Home Alone | 2=Family-Gathering Christmas Comedy | 3=Adult & Raunchy Christmas Comedy | 4=Christmas Specials & Musical Revues | 5=Christmas Comedy beyond Hollywood
defn: A comedy whose engine is the Christmas season itself: a child left home alone, the family gathering, the office party, the pageant (Home Alone, A Christmas Story, National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation, Bad Santa). A Christmas love story goes to A17-10.

label: Christmas Romantic Comedy
secs: 1=Classic Hollywood Christmas Romance | 2=Royal & Fairy-Tale Christmas Romance | 3=Contemporary Holiday Rom-Com
defn: A romantic comedy timed to and powered by the Christmas season: a holiday meet-cute, a fake date home for Christmas, a snowed-in prince (The Shop Around the Corner, The Holiday, A Christmas Prince, Happiest Season). A non-seasonal rom-com goes to A13.

label: Bollywood Masala
secs: 1=Angry Young Man Era (1973–1980s) | 2=Romantic & Family Spectacle (1990s–2000s) | 3=Star Action Masala (1995–)
defn: A Hindi popular film in the masala mode: action, romance, comedy, family melodrama and song-and-dance combined around a star (Sholay, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Dabangg, Jawan). A big-budget multilingual South Indian release goes to A18-4.

label: Tamil Masala
secs: 1=Superstar Vehicles (Rajinikanth) | 2=Vijay & Ajith Mass Films | 3=Shankar Vigilante Spectacles | 4=Lokesh Cinematic Universe | 5=New Tamil Mass Cinema
defn: A Tamil-language popular film in the masala mode built around a mass hero, punch dialogues, songs and social messages (Baasha, Sivaji, Ghilli, Vikram). A pan-Indian multilingual epic goes to A18-4.

label: Telugu Masala
defn: A Telugu-language popular film in the masala mode: a mass hero, family sentiment, comedy and action set pieces (Pokiri, Magadheera, Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo, Dasara). A pan-Indian multilingual epic goes to A18-4.

label: Pan-Indian Film
defn: A South Indian big-budget spectacle made and released simultaneously in several Indian languages for a national market (Baahubali: The Beginning, K.G.F: Chapter 1, RRR, Pushpa: The Rise - Part 1).

label: Malayalam Mass Film
defn: A Malayalam-language star action film in the mass mode, from political-gangster sagas to ensemble fight films (Lucifer, King of Kotha, RDX: Robert Dony Xavier, Rifle Club).

label: Dhallywood & Lollywood Masala
defn: A masala film from the Bengali, Bangladeshi, Pakistani or Sri Lankan popular industries (Toofan, Taandob, The Legend of Maula Jatt, Teefa In Trouble).

label: Nollywood
secs: 1=Home-Video Era (1992–2000s) | 2=New Nollywood (2009–)
defn: A Nigerian popular feature of the Lagos-centred industry, from video-era melodrama to New Nollywood comedies and crime films (Osuofia in London, The Wedding Party, King of Boys, The Black Book).

label: Yeşilçam
secs: 1=Yeşilçam Melodrama | 2=Yeşilçam Comedy (Eğilmez, Sunal) | 3=Historical Adventure (Malkoçoğlu, Tarkan, Kara Murat) | 4=Turksploitation Remakes
defn: A Turkish popular film of the Istanbul studio era (c. 1950–1990): melodramas, school comedies and historical adventures (The Chaos Class, Tosun Pasha, My Dear Brother, The Girl with the Red Scarf).

label: Wakaliwood
defn: An ultra-low-budget action film from Wakaliga, Kampala, made by Ramon Film Productions with homemade effects and a live 'video joker' narration (Who Killed Captain Alex?, Bad Black, Crazy World).

label: Ozploitation
defn: The Australian low-budget exploitation boom of c. 1971–1990 under the 10BA tax concession: ocker sex comedies, bikie films, outback horror, kung-fu and car-crash action (Stone, Alvin Purple, Patrick, Turkey Shoot, Dead End Drive-In).

label: Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité
secs: 1=Institutions | 2=Campaigns & Public Life | 3=Families & Private Lives | 4=Work & Labour | 5=Communities & Places
defn: A documentary made by observing events as they happen, with lightweight sync-sound cameras, no narration and minimal intervention (Primary, Titicut Follies, Salesman, Grey Gardens). A first-person or reflexive film goes to A19-5; a film staging or re-enacting goes to A19-7.

label: Ethnographic Film
defn: A documentary that records and interprets a culture or way of life, from Flaherty to sensory ethnography (Nanook of the North, Dead Birds, Leviathan, Manakamana).

label: City Symphony
defn: A feature-length silent-era documentary portraying a city's day as a rhythmic montage (Berlin: Symphony of a Metropolis, Man with a Movie Camera). City-symphony shorts sit in A21-12.

label: Essay Film
secs: 1=Essays on Images & Cinema | 2=History, Politics & Society | 3=Place & Travel | 4=Identity & the Body
defn: A documentary that argues or meditates in a personal voice, usually through first-person narration over assembled images (Sans Soleil, F for Fake, The Gleaners & I, I Am Not Your Negro). When the subject is the filmmaker's own life the film goes to A19-5.

label: Diary Film
defn: A first-person documentary whose subject is the filmmaker's own life and family, often diaristic or home-movie based (Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania, Sherman's March, Tarnation, Stories We Tell).

label: Compilation Film
defn: A documentary built mainly from pre-existing archival footage, edited without new interviews (The Atomic Cafe, Apollo 11, They Shall Not Grow Old, State Funeral). Artist appropriation of footage goes to A20-4.

label: Docufiction
defn: A film that blends documentary and fiction: staged or re-enacted scenes with real people, or fiction shot as documentary (Louisiana Story, Caesar Must Die, Four Daughters, The Arbor). Includes mockumentary features.

label: Propaganda Film
secs: 1=Nazi Propaganda Film | 2=Soviet Agitprop Documentary | 3=American New Deal & Wartime Propaganda | 4=Popular Front & Anti-Fascist Documentary
defn: A documentary made by or for a state or cause to persuade a mass audience (Triumph of the Will, Why We Fight, The Negro Soldier). Wartime sponsored shorts go to A21-14.

label: Political Documentary
secs: 1=Polemic & First-Person Advocacy | 2=Environment, Food & Animals | 3=Labour & Class | 4=Civil Rights, Race & Disability | 5=Women's & LGBTQ Movements | 6=Elections, Politicians & Protest
defn: A documentary that takes a side on a public issue or follows a political movement, campaign or politician (Roger & Me, Harlan County U.S.A., An Inconvenient Truth, 13th). Exposés of hidden wrongdoing go to A19-10.

label: Investigative Documentary
secs: 1=Corporate & Financial Wrongdoing | 2=State Power & Corruption | 3=Cults, Religion & Belief | 4=Disasters & Accidents | 5=Media, Technology & the Internet
defn: A documentary that uncovers concealed wrongdoing through journalistic investigation (Inside Job, Citizenfour, Going Clear, Collective). A criminal case goes to A19-11.

label: True Crime Documentary
secs: 1=Murder & Violent Crime | 2=Trials & Wrongful Convictions | 3=Fraud, Scams & Hoaxes | 4=Abuse, Cults & Exploitation
defn: A documentary reconstructing a specific crime, its investigation or trial (The Thin Blue Line, Paradise Lost, Capturing the Friedmans, The Tinder Swindler).

label: War Documentary
defn: A documentary filmed in or about a war or armed conflict, often from the front line (Restrepo, For Sama, 20 Days in Mariupol, Hearts and Minds). Archival war compilations go to A19-6; wartime state films to A19-8.

label: Historical Documentary
defn: A documentary reconstructing a past event or period through testimony and research (Shoah, The Act of Killing, Freedom Riders, The Fog of War).

label: Biographical Documentary
secs: 1=Entertainers & Celebrities | 2=Public Figures, Writers & Thinkers | 3=Ordinary Lives & Eccentrics | 4=Subcultures & Communities
defn: A documentary portrait of one person, or of a small group or subculture, other than a musician, artist, filmmaker or athlete (Won't You Be My Neighbor?, RBG, Gates of Heaven, Paris Is Burning).

label: Art Documentary
defn: A documentary about a visual artist, designer, architect, dancer or fashion house and their work (Crumb, Pina, Finding Vivian Maier, Exit Through the Gift Shop).

label: Making-of & Film History Documentary
secs: 1=Making-of & Behind-the-Scenes | 2=Filmmaker & Actor Portraits | 3=Film History & Criticism
defn: A documentary about cinema or television itself: the making of a production, a filmmaker or actor portrait, or a history of films (Hearts of Darkness, Burden of Dreams, Jodorowsky's Dune, The Celluloid Closet).

label: Rockumentary
secs: 1=Musician Portraits | 2=Star Self-Portraits & Tour Documentaries | 3=Bands & Recording Sessions | 4=Scenes, Genres & Roots Music
defn: A documentary about musicians or music, built on interviews, archive and backstage footage rather than a complete performance (Dont Look Back, Amy, Searching for Sugar Man, Buena Vista Social Club). A film of a performance goes to A19-18.

label: Concert Film
secs: 1=Festival Films | 2=Rock, Soul & Jazz Concerts | 3=Pop Arena & K-Pop Tour Films | 4=Stage & Studio Performances
defn: A film whose substance is a recorded live performance, concert, tour show or festival (Monterey Pop, The Last Waltz, Stop Making Sense, Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour).

label: Sports Documentary
defn: A documentary about an athlete, team, match or competition (When We Were Kings, Senna, Hoop Dreams, The King of Kong). Official Olympic films go to A19-20.

label: Olympic Film
secs: 1=Interwar Olympic Films | 2=Postwar & Auteur Olympic Films (1948–1984) | 3=Later Olympic Films (1985–)
defn: An official or authorised feature film of an Olympic Games (Olympia, Tokyo Olympiad, Visions of Eight, 16 Days of Glory).

label: Travelogue Film
defn: A documentary organised as a journey through places, recording what the traveller sees (This Is Cinerama, Calcutta, ¡Vivan las antípodas!).

label: Mountaineering & Expedition Film
defn: A documentary of an expedition or feat of endurance in mountains, ice, ocean or wilderness (Kon-Tiki, Touching the Void, Free Solo, The Rescue).

label: Nature Documentary
defn: A documentary about animals, plants or the natural world (The Silent World, March of the Penguins, Microcosmos, My Octopus Teacher).

label: Mondo Film
defn: A shock documentary of real or staged death, cruelty and taboo customs (Faces of Death, Orozco the Embalmer).

label: Surrealist Film
defn: A film built on Surrealist dream logic, irrational juxtaposition and the disruption of bourgeois order (L'Age d'Or, The Exterminating Angel, The Holy Mountain, Eraserhead). Surrealist shorts sit in A21-15.

label: Underground Film
defn: A low-budget, self-distributed avant-garde feature made outside the industry, often transgressive or camp (Flaming Creatures, Chelsea Girls, Pink Narcissus, Trash Humpers).

label: Structural Film
defn: An experimental film whose shape is a predetermined system: fixed camera, duration, repetition or rule (Wavelength, Zorns Lemma, Empire, 13 Lakes).

label: Found-Footage Film
defn: An experimental feature made by re-editing appropriated film material (Decasia, Star Spangled to Death, The Clock). Archival documentary goes to A19-6.

label: Non-Narrative Film
defn: A feature without plot or characters, built as an audiovisual tone poem of images and music (Koyaanisqatsi, Baraka, Samsara).

label: Psychedelic Film
defn: An experimental feature that simulates altered states through strobing colour, sound and disorientation (Head, Enter the Void, Lux Æterna).

label: Art Film
defn: A narrative feature whose avant-garde form (tableau, recitation, fragmentation, anti-illusion) is its defining element (The Color of Pomegranates, India Song, Russian Ark, Holy Motors). Duration-based art films go to A1-39 Slow Cinema.

label: Lettrist & Situationist Cinema
defn: The Paris avant-garde of Isidore Isou's Lettrists (1951–1952) and Guy Debord's Situationist International: 'discrepant' and anti-films that separate sound from image, scratch and blank the film strip, and détourn found images against the spectacle (Venom and Eternity, Howlings in Favour of de Sade, The Society of the Spectacle).

label: Actuality Film
defn: A pre-1910 single-shot or few-shot nonfiction film recording a real scene (Workers Leaving the Factory, The Arrival of a Train, Roundhay Garden Scene).

label: Newsreel
defn: A short topical news film for theatrical release (Hindenburg Disaster Newsreel Footage, Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapse, Faces of November).

label: Trick Film
defn: An early short built on camera tricks (stop substitution, multiple exposure) for magical effect (A Trip to the Moon, The India Rubber Head, Dream of a Rarebit Fiend).

label: One-Reeler
defn: A silent narrative short of one reel or less, the story film of the nickelodeon era (The Great Train Robbery, A Corner in Wheat, The Musketeers of Pig Alley). Silent comedy shorts go to A21-5.

label: Slapstick Short
defn: A silent or early-sound comedy short of physical gags, typically a one- or two-reeler (The Immigrant, One Week, The Music Box).

label: Musical Short
defn: A short whose substance is a song or musical number: early sound musical shorts, soundies and long-form music videos (Black and Tan, Jammin' the Blues, Runaway, Anima).

label: Drama Short Film
secs: 1=Social Realist Shorts | 2=Childhood & Coming of Age | 3=Relationships & Family | 4=Art-House & Literary Shorts | 5=Crime & Thriller Shorts | 6=War Shorts
defn: A live-action fiction short whose engine is drama rather than comedy or genre (The Lunch Date, Wasp, The Present, The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar).

label: Comedy Short Film
defn: A sound-era live-action comedy short (Bottle Rocket, Six Shooter, Coffee and Cigarettes, An Irish Goodbye). Silent and early-sound slapstick goes to A21-5.

label: Horror Short Film
defn: A live-action horror short (Lights Out, Saw, Tarantella, Frankenweenie).

label: Science Fiction & Fantasy Short Film
defn: A live-action science-fiction or fantasy short (La Jetée, The Red Balloon, Electronic Labyrinth THX 1138 4EB, Rakka).

label: Tie-In Short Film
secs: 1=Studio Tie-Ins & One-Shots | 2=Fan Films | 3=Branded & Commissioned Shorts
defn: A short made to extend or promote an existing property or brand: studio one-shots, fan films, fake trailers, commissioned branded shorts (Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter, Team Thor, Power Rangers, Castello Cavalcanti).

label: Documentary Short
secs: 1=Portrait & Social Shorts | 2=Political & Activist Shorts | 3=City Symphonies & Poetic Shorts | 4=Essay & Memory Shorts | 5=Music & Performance Shorts | 6=Sport Shorts
defn: A nonfiction short of the sound era not made as sponsored or scientific film (Night and Fog, Land Without Bread, The House Is Black, Period. End of Sentence.).

label: Scientific Film
defn: A short that films natural or laboratory phenomena for science, often through microcinematography (The Sea Horse, The Vampire, The Love Life of the Octopus).

label: Sponsored Film
secs: 1=Government & Wartime Films | 2=Industrial & Corporate Films | 3=Educational Films
defn: A short commissioned by a government, company or institution to inform, instruct or promote (The Plow That Broke the Plains, Listen to Britain, Duck and Cover, Glass).

label: Avant-Garde Short
secs: 1=Dada & Cinéma Pur | 2=Surrealist & Trance Films | 3=Lyrical Film | 4=Structural Film Shorts | 5=Found-Footage & Collage Shorts | 6=Video & Expanded Works
defn: A short experimental film working with form, perception or the film material rather than story (Meshes of the Afternoon, Ballet Mécanique, Mothlight, Serene Velocity).

label: Prestige Drama
secs: 1=Third Golden Age: Cable Prestige (1999–2012) | 2=Peak TV & Streaming Era (2013–)
defn: A long-arc auteur drama whose engine is a morally compromised protagonist or a family/institution observed with novelistic ambition, made under the post-2000 cable "quality TV" banner (Mad Men, Six Feet Under, Billions, The Leftovers). A prestige crime saga goes to B7; a prestige family-business saga with succession at its centre goes to B1-3.

label: Family Saga
defn: A serial that follows one family (or a few linked families) across generations or decades, so that historical time is the plot (Roots, Heimat, Pachinko, When Life Gives You Tangerines). A family drama set in one present moment goes to B1-3; a dynasty soap of wealth and scheming goes to B12-5.

label: Family Drama
secs: 1=Ensemble Family Dramas | 2=Small-Town & Rural Family Dramas | 3=Wealthy-Family & Succession Dramas | 4=Marriage & Divorce Dramas | 5=Weekend & Daily Family Serials
defn: A series whose engine is the everyday bonds, conflicts and crises of one household or kin group in roughly its own present (Parenthood, This Is Us, The Waltons, Succession). A family followed across generations goes to B1-2; a family-revenge melodrama of the prime-time kind goes to B12-5.

label: Slice-of-Life Drama
secs: 1=Friendship & Young-Adult Ensembles | 2=Healing Dramas | 3=Urban Women's Dramas | 4=Later-Life & Community Dramas
defn: A low-plot drama of ordinary lives, friendships and recoveries in which the texture of daily living, not an event, carries the series (thirtysomething, My Mister, Ode to Joy, Dear My Friends). Social-problem realism goes to B1-5; a romance-driven series goes to B1-9.

label: Social Realist Drama
secs: 1=Working-Class & Community Realism | 2=Trauma & Social-Issue Dramas | 3=Faith & Religious-Community Dramas | 4=Migrant & Stateless Dramas
defn: A drama that renders a social condition (class, work, abuse, faith, migration) with documentary-leaning realism and makes that condition the subject (Boys from the Blackstuff, This Is England '86, I May Destroy You, Unorthodox). A dramatisation of a real public case goes to B1-26.

label: LGBTQ Drama
defn: A series whose central lives, community and conflicts are those of gay, lesbian, bisexual or trans characters (Queer as Folk, The L Word, POSE, It's a Sin). A teen coming-out romance stays in B1-7; East and Southeast Asian BL/GL series go to B5.

label: Teen Drama
secs: 1=Teen Soaps | 2=Teen Social-Issue Dramas | 3=School & Teacher Dramas | 4=Performing-Arts School Dramas | 5=School-Violence & Delinquent Dramas | 6=Teen Romance Dramas
defn: A drama centred on adolescents of secondary-school age and their school, friendships, first loves and coming of age (Beverly Hills, 90210, Degrassi, Skins, Euphoria). College and exam-coaching students go to B1-8; children's series for under-twelves go to B10.

label: Campus Drama
defn: A drama of university students or exam aspirants in which the college or coaching institution is the world of the series (Felicity, Kota Factory, Aspirants, Hellcats). Secondary-school life goes to B1-7.

label: Romantic Drama
secs: 1=Contemporary Romantic Dramas | 2=Literary & Young-Adult Romance | 3=Small-Town Romance | 4=Affair & Infidelity Dramas | 5=Erotic Drama Series
defn: A series whose main engine is a love story or the course of a relationship, played for feeling rather than laughs (Normal People, Virgin River, The Affair, Little Birds). A romantic comedy series goes to B8; a period romance in costume goes to B1-20; erotic film goes to A15.

label: Medical Drama
secs: 1=Hospital Ensemble Dramas | 2=Star-Doctor Dramas | 3=Emergency & Trauma Medicine | 4=Country, Island & Travelling Doctors | 5=Nurses, Midwives & Allied Professions | 6=Period Medical Dramas
defn: A series set among doctors, nurses and patients in which treating illness and the life of the hospital or practice drive the episodes (ER, Grey's Anatomy, House, Doctor X). A medical-crime investigation goes to B7.

label: Legal Drama
secs: 1=Law-Firm Dramas | 2=Defence & Courtroom-Case Dramas | 3=Prosecutor Dramas | 4=Judge, Court & Jury Dramas | 5=Legal Dramedies | 6=Legal Thrillers
defn: A series in which lawyers, prosecutors, judges or juries and their cases are the engine (L.A. Law, The Good Wife, Suits, Extraordinary Attorney Woo). A police procedural goes to B7; a courtroom docudrama goes to B1-26.

label: Political Drama
secs: 1=Executive & Head-of-State Dramas | 2=Parliamentary & Party Dramas | 3=City & Campaign Politics | 4=Diplomatic & Security-State Dramas
defn: A series about the getting and use of political power by presidents, ministers, legislators and their staffs (The West Wing, Borgen, House of Cards, The Diplomat). An espionage thriller goes to B7; a dramatised real scandal goes to B1-26.

label: Workplace Drama
secs: 1=Newsroom & Media Dramas | 2=First-Responder Dramas | 3=Office & Business Dramas | 4=Kitchen, Hotel & Trade Dramas | 5=Show-Business Dramas | 6=Therapy & Caring-Profession Dramas
defn: A series whose engine is the work and rivalries of one non-medical, non-legal profession or company (The Newsroom, Chicago Fire, Misaeng: Incomplete Life, The Bear). Hospitals go to B1-10, law to B1-11, the military to B1-16; a workplace sitcom goes to B8.

label: Musical Drama Series
defn: A drama whose world is the making of music or dance performance, with performances carrying story and feeling (Nashville, Smash, Daisy Jones & the Six, The Singing Detective). A performing-arts high school goes to B1-7; a music competition show goes to B13.

label: Sports Drama
secs: 1=Team-Sport Dramas | 2=Combat-Sport Dramas | 3=Individual & Racing-Sport Dramas | 4=Mind-Sport & Esports Dramas
defn: A series in which training for and competing in a sport or game is the spine of the story (Friday Night Lights, Cobra Kai, Racket Boys, Hikaru no Go). Sports anime goes to C7; live sport goes to B16.

label: Military Drama
defn: A series about serving soldiers, sailors or special forces and their units in peacetime or present-day deployments, where service life is the engine (SEAL Team, The Unit, Sea Patrol, D.P.). A historical war goes to B1-17.

label: War Drama
secs: 1=Second World War Dramas | 2=First World War & Earlier Wars | 3=Partisan & Resistance Dramas | 4=Post-1945 & Modern Wars | 5=Home-Front & War-Nursing Dramas
defn: A series set inside a historical war, on the front or behind it, in which the war itself drives the story (Band of Brothers, Das Boot, Generation War, Tour of Duty). Present-day service life goes to B1-16; war film goes to A9.

label: Television Western
secs: 1=Classic Episodic Westerns | 2=Frontier & Pioneer Dramas | 3=Western Miniseries & Epics | 4=Revisionist Westerns | 5=Neo-Westerns
defn: A series set on the American (or a comparable) frontier whose codes of gun, horse, land and law shape the story (Gunsmoke, Bonanza, Deadwood, Yellowstone). Western film goes to A10.

label: Historical Drama
secs: 1=Ancient-World & Sword-and-Sandal Epics | 2=Biblical & Religious Epics | 3=Medieval & Renaissance Dramas | 4=Royal-Court Dramas | 5=Colonial, Revolutionary & Slavery-Era Dramas | 6=National & Imperial Epics
defn: A series that dramatises the great events and rulers of a pre-twentieth-century age, its wars, courts and faiths (I, Claudius, The Tudors, Vikings, The Crown). Ottoman historical dizi go to B12-6; Chinese and Korean court drama go to B4 and B2; a novel adaptation in period dress goes to B1-20.

label: Costume Drama
secs: 1=Austen & Regency Dramas | 2=Victorian Novel Adaptations | 3=Continental Classic Adaptations | 4=Gothic & Sensation Dramas | 5=Classic Girls' & School Stories | 6=Costume Romances
defn: A series adapted from (or modelled on) a pre-1900 novel, whose period manners, marriages and class are the drama (Pride and Prejudice, Bleak House, Anne of Green Gables, Bridgerton). Real rulers and battles go to B1-19; Edwardian country-house and shop sagas go to B1-21.

label: Heritage Drama
secs: 1=Country-House Dramas | 2=Shop, Hotel & Enterprise Dramas | 3=Rural & Village Heritage Dramas | 4=Empire & Raj Dramas
defn: A series that lovingly recreates late-Victorian to interwar British (and kindred) society through a great house, shop or village and the classes inside it (Upstairs, Downstairs, Downton Abbey, Mr Selfridge, The Jewel in the Crown). Novel adaptations of the 19th century go to B1-20.

label: Period Drama
secs: 1=Interwar Dramas | 2=1940s Dramas | 3=Postwar & 1950s Dramas | 4=1960s & 1970s Dramas | 5=1980s & 1990s Dramas
defn: A series set in a recent past of the twentieth century (roughly 1918–1999) whose era, its manners and its changes are the drama (Pan Am, The Queen's Gambit, Cable Girls, Blossoms Shanghai). A series set within a war goes to B1-17; a multi-generation chronicle goes to B1-2.

label: Swashbuckler
defn: An episodic or serial adventure of swordplay, outlaw heroes, musketeers and pirates in a romanticised past (The Adventures of Robin Hood, Zorro, The Musketeers, Black Sails). Grounded medieval epics go to B1-19; martial-arts adventure goes to A7.

label: Action-Adventure
secs: 1=Literary Adventure & Voyages | 2=Treasure-Hunt & Tomb-Raiding Adventures | 3=Action-Hero Series | 4=Martial-Arts & Street-Fighting Series
defn: A series built on quests, voyages, treasure hunts or a weekly hero-in-action format (Knight Rider, MacGyver, The Lost Tomb, Michael Strogoff). Swordplay romances go to B1-23; spy and crime action go to B7; superpowered heroes go to B9.

label: Disaster Miniseries
defn: A miniseries whose story is an earthquake, eruption, impact or shipwreck and the struggle to survive it (10.5, Category 7: The End of the World, La Palma, Titanic). A dramatisation of a specific real disaster told as public record goes to B1-26.

label: Docudrama
secs: 1=Reenactment Docudramas | 2=Disaster & Catastrophe Docudramas | 3=Political & Public-Scandal Docudramas | 4=Injustice & Social-Case Docudramas | 5=Terror, War & Siege Docudramas | 6=Corporate & Public-Health Scandals | 7=Exploration, Science & Space Docudramas
defn: A drama that reconstructs a real event, case or institution with documentary fidelity, often naming the real people (Chernobyl, When They See Us, Mr Bates vs The Post Office, Dopesick). A dramatised life story goes to B1-27; a documentary series goes to B11.

label: Biographical Miniseries
secs: 1=Political & Royal Lives | 2=Music Biopics | 3=Show-Business & Fashion Lives | 4=Sports Lives | 5=Science, Enterprise & Faith Lives
defn: A miniseries or series that tells the life (or a defining stretch of it) of a real modern person (Fosse/Verdon, Elvis, Genius, The Kennedys). A pre-modern ruler goes to B1-19; biographical film goes to A11.

label: Literary Adaptation
defn: A limited series adapted from a modern literary novel or story, set in its author's present, where the book's voice shapes the drama (Olive Kitteridge, My Brilliant Friend, Patrick Melrose, The Slap). Pre-1900 novels go to B1-20; a literary romance goes to B1-9.

label: Anthology Drama
secs: 1=Live & Single-Play Anthologies | 2=Suspense & Crime Anthologies | 3=Omnibus & Linked-Story Anthologies | 4=Themed Modern Anthologies
defn: A series of self-contained plays or stories with new casts and stories per episode or season (Play for Today, Playhouse 90, Alfred Hitchcock Presents, Modern Love). Horror anthologies of the uncanny go to B9 when the supernatural is the engine.

label: Golden Age Anthology Drama
secs: 1=Live Anthologies | 2=Filmed Anthologies
defn: A sponsor-titled American anthology drama of the first Golden Age of Television (c. 1947–1961): a new self-contained teleplay each week, broadcast live from New York or Hollywood (Kraft Television Theatre, Studio One, The Philco Television Playhouse, Playhouse 90) or, later in the decade, filmed in Hollywood (General Electric Theater, Schlitz Playhouse). Later anthologies stay in B1-29 Anthology Drama.

label: Romantic Comedy (rom-com)
secs: 1=Contract, Fake-Relationship & Marriage-First Rom-Coms | 2=Cohabitation & Neighbour Rom-Coms | 3=Cross-Dressing, Makeover & Disguise Rom-Coms | 4=Showbiz & Celebrity Rom-Coms | 5=Thirty-Something & Second-Chance Rom-Coms | 6=Small-Town & Healing Rom-Coms | 7=Spy, Crime & Political Rom-Coms
defn: A Korean romance series whose engine is comic: mismatched leads, a contrived premise that forces them together, and a happy ending (Coffee Prince, Because This Is My First Life, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha). A romance set mainly at work goes to B2-2; a rich-heir and poor-heroine romance goes to B2-3; a supernatural premise goes to B2-12.

label: Office Romance
secs: 1=Boss & Secretary Romances | 2=Company & Office Ensembles | 3=Kitchen, Shop & Trade Romances | 4=Broadcasting, Publishing & Creative-Industry Romances
defn: A Korean romance series set inside a workplace, where the job, hierarchy and colleagues drive the love story (What's Wrong with Secretary Kim, Business Proposal, Pasta, Romance Is a Bonus Book). A series about a profession first and foremost (hospital, court) goes to B2-9 or B2-10.

label: Chaebol Romance
secs: 1=Cinderella ("Candy") Romances | 2=Reverse-Cinderella & Heiress Romances | 3=Royal & Constitutional-Monarchy Romances
defn: A Korean romance built on the class gap between a chaebol (conglomerate) heir or heiress and a poor partner, the "Candy" Cinderella formula (Boys over Flowers, Lovers in Paris, The Heirs, Queen of Tears). Chaebol family intrigue with birth secrets and revenge goes to B2-5 Makjang.

label: Korean Melodrama
secs: 1=Classic & Trendy Dramas (to 1999) | 2=Hallyu Tearjerkers: Fate, First Love & Illness | 3=Adult & Affair Melodramas | 4=Realist & Healing Romance Dramas | 5=Music & Arts Melodramas
defn: A Korean romance played for tears or emotional realism rather than laughs: fated or doomed love, illness, love triangles, adultery, or the quiet realism of adult relationships (Winter Sonata, Autumn in My Heart, Something in the Rain, Secret Love Affair). Melodrama of birth secrets, affairs and outrageous plotting goes to B2-5 Makjang.

label: Makjang Drama
secs: 1=Birth-Secret & Family-Feud Makjang | 2=Adultery & Marriage Makjang | 3=Revenge & Chaebol-Intrigue Makjang
defn: A Korean serial built on deliberately outrageous plotting: birth secrets, adultery, amnesia, chaebol family feuds and revenge escalating beyond plausibility (The Penthouse: War in Life, The World of the Married, East of Eden, Money Flower). A weekend family drama without the excess goes to B2-7.

label: Revenge Drama
defn: A Korean series whose spine is a protagonist's long-planned vengeance, usually wrapped in a romance or melodrama (Green Rose, Don't Look Back: The Legend of Orpheus, Goodbye Mr. Black, Call It Love). Revenge inside an outrageous family serial goes to B2-5 Makjang.

label: Family Drama (gajok deurama)
defn: A Korean series centred on an extended family across generations, typically the long-running weekend family drama or the evening daily drama (My Golden Life, Young Lady and Gentleman, Homemade Love Story). Family serials driven by birth secrets and revenge go to B2-5 Makjang.

label: Sageuk (historical drama)
secs: 1=Jeong-geuk & Dynastic Epics | 2=Fusion Sageuk: Adventure, Mystery & Comedy | 3=Sageuk Romance | 4=Fantasy, Time-Slip & Horror Sageuk | 5=Modern-Era Period Dramas (1890s-1990s)
defn: A Korean historical drama set in the Joseon, Goryeo or Three Kingdoms periods, or a modern-era period drama of the Korean Empire, the colonial era and the later twentieth century (Jewel in the Palace, Jumong, Moon Embracing the Sun, Mr. Sunshine). A present-day romance with a brief slip into the past goes to B2-12.

label: Medical Drama
defn: A Korean series set among doctors and hospitals, whose cases and careers drive the story even when a romance runs alongside (Descendants of the Sun, Emergency Couple, Doctor Slump). A psychiatric healing melodrama goes to B2-4.

label: Legal Drama
defn: A Korean series set among lawyers, prosecutors and judges, with cases framing the plot (I Hear Your Voice, Suspicious Partner, While You Were Sleeping). A Joseon-era lawyer goes to B2-8 Sageuk.

label: Thriller & Mystery Drama
defn: A Korean series driven by a crime, a mystery or a threat, usually entwined with a love story (The Smile Has Left Your Eyes, When the Phone Rings, The Trunk). A revenge plan as spine goes to B2-6; a police procedural without romance belongs in B7.

label: Fantasy Romance
secs: 1=Time-Slip, Time-Loop & Reincarnation | 2=Mythical & Immortal Beings | 3=Body-Swap, Possession & Transmigration | 4=Ghosts, Reapers & the Afterlife | 5=Superpowers & Science-Fiction Devices | 6=Webtoon, Drama & Fictional-World Romances
defn: A Korean romance series whose premise is supernatural or speculative: time slips, immortal beings (goblin, gumiho, grim reaper), body swaps, ghosts, superpowers or a fictional world (Guardian: The Lonely and Great God, My Love from the Star, Lovely Runner, W). A historical drama with fantasy elements goes to B2-8 section 4.

label: School & Youth Drama
secs: 1=High-School Dramas | 2=Campus & Twenty-Something Dramas | 3=Idol & Music Youth Dramas | 4=Sports Youth Dramas
defn: A Korean series about teenagers or people in their early twenties, set in high school, university, idol training or sport, where growing up is the subject (Playful Kiss, Cheese in the Trap, Weightlifting Fairy Kim Bok-joo, Twenty-Five Twenty-One). A rich-heir high-school romance goes to B2-3.

label: Asadora (Renzoku Terebi Shōsetsu)
