defn: An NHK morning serial: some 150 fifteen-minute episodes over six months following a heroine's life, often across decades (Oshin, Amachan, Massan). A family drama in other slots goes to B3-9.

label: Taiga Drama
defn: NHK's year-long Sunday historical epic, one historical figure or era per year (Atsu Hime, Taira no Kiyomori, What Will You Do, Ieyasu?). Other period dramas belong in A8 or B1.

label: Trendy Drama & Getsuku
secs: 1=Bubble-Era Trendy Dramas (to 1995) | 2=Getsuku Peak (1996-2009) | 3=Later Getsuku & Prime-Time Romances (2010-)
defn: A Japanese prime-time romance in the trendy-drama tradition: urban young professionals in love, star casts and theme songs, most famously Fuji TV's Monday 9 pm "getsuku" slot (Tokyo Love Story, Long Vacation, Beautiful Life, Rich Man, Poor Woman). A late-night or streaming romance goes to B3-4 or B3-5.

label: Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama
secs: 1=Pure-Love & Tearjerker Dramas | 2=Furin (Adultery) & Forbidden-Love Dramas | 3=Obsessive & Dark Romances
defn: A Japanese romance played for tears or for dark adult emotion: pure love against illness or death (jun'ai), forbidden or adulterous love (furin), obsessive love (Crying Out Love, in the Center of the World, Silent, Hirugao, Last Friends). A prime-time trendy romance goes to B3-3.

label: Romantic Comedy (ren'ai komedi)
secs: 1=Contract & Fake-Marriage Rom-Coms | 2=Konkatsu & Single-Life Rom-Coms | 3=Cohabitation & Housekeeper Rom-Coms | 4=Makeover, Otaku & Oddball Rom-Coms | 5=Rich-Man & Cinderella Rom-Coms | 6=Teens' Love & Late-Night Romances
defn: A Japanese romance series whose engine is comic: a contrived arrangement, a marriage hunt, a cohabitation or an oddball heroine, often adapted from josei or TL manga (Tokyo Tarareba Girls, Princess Jellyfish, Densha Otoko, Busu no Hitomi ni Koishiteru). An office love story goes to B3-6; a school romance goes to B3-7.

label: Office Romance (shanai ren'ai)
defn: A Japanese romance set inside a company or workplace, between boss and subordinate or colleagues (Hotaru no Hikari, Oh My Boss! Love Not Included, Kissing the Ring Finger). A drama about the work itself goes to B3-10 Oshigoto Drama.

label: School Romance (gakuen ren'ai)
secs: 1=High-School Romances | 2=Campus & Young-Adult Romances | 3=Teacher-Student Romances
defn: A Japanese romance among students, mostly live-action adaptations of shōjo manga, set in high school or college (Hana Yori Dango, Itazura na Kiss, Good Morning Call, Ao Haru Ride). A school drama about teachers, delinquents or clubs goes to B3-8.

label: School Drama (gakuen dorama)
secs: 1=Teacher Dramas | 2=Delinquent (Yankii) Dramas | 3=Bullying & Dark Classroom Dramas | 4=School-Club & Sports Dramas (bukatsu) | 5=School Comedies & Coming-of-Age
defn: A Japanese series set in a school whose subject is the institution itself: the crusading teacher, the delinquent class, bullying, or the school club (GTO, Gokusen, The Queen's Classroom, Rookies). A love story between students goes to B3-7.

label: Home Drama (hōmu dorama)
secs: 1=Family Ensemble & Sibling Dramas | 2=Parenting & Single-Parent Dramas | 3=Illness, Disability & Hardship Dramas
defn: A Japanese series about a household: siblings, parents and children, single fathers, a family's illness or hardship (Hitotsu Yane no Shita, Tonbi, One Liter of Tears, Mother). A comedy of everyday eccentricity goes to B3-12.

label: Oshigoto Drama (workplace drama)
secs: 1=Corporate & Finance Dramas | 2=Office Comedies & Temp Dramas | 3=Trades & Service Professions | 4=Media, Publishing & Entertainment | 5=Medical, Legal, Care & Rescue
defn: A Japanese series about a job: the company, the trade, the profession or the industry is the subject (Naoki Hanzawa, Shomuni, The Pride of the Temp, Downtown Rocket). A romance at work goes to B3-6; a cooking or restaurant drama goes to B3-11.

label: Gourmet Drama (gurume dorama)
defn: A Japanese series in which food, cooking and eating are the subject, often episodic around one dish per episode (Solitary Gourmet, Midnight Diner, The Makanai: Cooking for the Maiko House). A romance between cooks goes to B3-5 or B3-6.

label: Slice-of-Life Drama (nichijō)
secs: 1=Healing (Iyashi) Slice of Life | 2=Eccentric-Ensemble Comedy-Drama
defn: A Japanese series of everyday life with no strong romantic or professional engine: healing (iyashi) rhythms or eccentric small-group comedy (Yuru Camp, Barakamon, Kisarazu Cat's Eye, Tiger and Dragon). A food-centred series goes to B3-11.

label: Suspense Drama (sasupensu)
defn: A Japanese series driven by a secret, crime or threat, often a domestic or romantic mystery (I Am Mita, Your Housekeeper, Quartet, Perfect Crime). A detective or police procedural belongs in B7.

label: Fantasy & Supernatural Drama
secs: 1=Fantasy-Premise Romances | 2=Supernatural & Science-Fiction Dramas
defn: A Japanese series whose premise is supernatural or science-fictional, usually framing a romance: a robot or alien lover, a ghost, a time slip, a body swap (Zettai Kareshi, Ima, Ai ni Yukimasu, Q10). Tokusatsu hero shows belong in B9.

label: Historical Epic Drama
defn: A serial that dramatises recorded dynastic history or a classic of Chinese literature at epic scale, statecraft and great events foremost and invented romance secondary (Romance of the Three Kingdoms, The Qin Empire, Ming Dynasty in 1566, A Dream of Red Mansions). A fictional court with romantic leads goes to B4-5; schemers in a fictional court go to B4-3.

label: Palace Drama
defn: A costume serial whose engine is the rivalry of consorts, empresses and palace women in the imperial harem, rising through scheming and survival (Empresses in the Palace, Story of Yanxi Palace, Ruyi's Royal Love in the Palace, Legend of Mi Yue). Male ministers and princes plotting for the throne go to B4-3.

label: Court Intrigue Drama
defn: A costume serial driven by political scheming for power, succession or revenge at court, with a strategist hero at its centre (Nirvana in Fire, The Advisors Alliance, Joy of Life, The Longest Day in Chang'an). Harem rivalry among women goes to B4-2; romance first goes to B4-5.

label: Gong'an & Costume Detective Drama
defn: A costume serial built on cases solved by a magistrate, coroner or detective in imperial China, one or several cases per arc (Justice Bao, The Imperial Coroner, Strange Tales of Tang Dynasty, Luoyang). A jianghu swordsman solving mysteries goes to B4-7.

label: Costume Romance
secs: 1=Royal & Court Romance | 2=House-Fighting Drama (Zhaidou) | 3=Rebirth & Revenge Romance | 4=General & Frontier Romance | 5=Heroine's Enterprise & Farming Drama (Zhongtian) | 6=Costume Romantic Comedy
defn: A guzhuang serial set in imperial or invented dynastic China whose engine is the central love story, intrigue and history serving it (Love Like the Galaxy: Part 1, The Story of Ming Lan, Blossoms in Adversity, Dawn Is Breaking). Immortals and cultivation go to B4-8; a modern heroine thrown into the past goes to B4-6.

label: Time-Travel Drama
secs: 1=Transmigration into Fiction (Chuanshu) | 2=Costume Time-Slip & Palace Time Travel | 3=Modern Time-Slip & Rebirth Romance
defn: A serial whose premise is a protagonist displaced in time or into a fictional world, the gap between eras or texts being the engine (Scarlet Heart, Go Princess, Go!, Romance of a Twin Flower, Back to Seventeen). Supernatural lovers without displacement go to B4-20.

label: Wuxia Drama
secs: 1=Jin Yong Adaptations | 2=Gu Long & Classic Wuxia Authors | 3=Jianghu Romance | 4=Original Wuxia Adventure
defn: A serial of martial heroes in the jianghu, the world of sects, swordsmen and codes of honour, with martial skill realistic rather than magical (The Legend of the Condor Heroes, Laughing in the Wind, Legend of Fei, Mysterious Lotus Casebook). Immortals and cultivation go to B4-8.

label: Xianxia Drama
secs: 1=Immortal & Three-Lives Romance | 2=Cultivation & Sect Adventure | 3=Demon & Spirit Romance | 4=Xianxia Comedy
defn: A serial of immortals, gods, demons and cultivators in a Daoist-mythic cosmos, often across several lifetimes (Eternal Love, Ashes of Love, Love between Fairy and Devil, Till the End of the Moon). Secondary-world empires without Daoist cosmology go to B4-9; the Journey-to-the-West mythology goes to B4-10.

label: Xuanhuan Drama
defn: A serial set in an invented secondary world of magic, races and empires, high fantasy not bound to Daoist cosmology (Novoland: Eagle Flag, Ice Fantasy, Ever Night, Douluo Continent). Immortals and heavens go to B4-8.

label: Shenmo Drama
defn: A serial adapting the gods-and-demons classics and folk legends of China (Journey to the West, Feng Shen Bang, The Legend of White Snake, Butterfly Lovers). Original immortal romances go to B4-8.

label: Republican-Era Drama
secs: 1=Literary & Family Saga | 2=Republican Romance | 3=Republican Mystery & Adventure
defn: A serial set in the Republic of China (1912–1949) whose engine is the period itself: warlords, Shanghai glamour, opera troupes and adventure (Winter Begonia, The Mystic Nine, Siege in Fog, White Deer Plain). Spies of the period go to B4-12.

label: Spy Drama
defn: A serial of undercover agents in the Republican and anti-Japanese war years, the double life and its unmasking the engine (Lurk, Rookie Agent Rouge, All Quiet in Peking, Silent Honor). A war-front epic goes to B4-13.

label: Main-Melody Drama
secs: 1=Revolutionary History & Leaders | 2=War History | 3=PLA Military Drama | 4=Reform, Poverty Alleviation & National Achievement
defn: A state-endorsed serial celebrating the Party, the revolution, the army or a national achievement (Awakening Age, Minning Town, Across the Yalu River, Ace Troops). Spies go to B4-12; Republican romance goes to B4-11.

label: Qiong Yao Drama
defn: A serial adapted from or produced by the novelist Qiong Yao, the canon of tearful romance and its comic costume offshoots (Princess Pearl, Romance in the Rain, Love in the Rain). Later Taiwanese idol drama goes to B4-15.

label: Taiwanese Idol Drama
secs: 1=Manga & Remake Idol Drama | 2=Idol Romantic Comedy | 3=Idol Melodrama | 4=Idol Fantasy | 5=Post-Idol Taiwanese Romance
defn: A Taiwanese romance serial of the idol-drama tradition, young pop-star leads in a glossy love story often adapted from manga (Meteor Garden, It Started with a Kiss, Hana Kimi, In Time with You). Taiwanese BL goes to B5-9.

label: Idol Drama
secs: 1=Sweet Romance (Tianchong) | 2=CEO & Rich-Heir Romance (Bazong) | 3=Contract & Hidden-Identity Romance | 4=Entertainment-Industry Romance
defn: A mainland romance serial of the idol-drama mode, young leads in a sweet, low-conflict love story (Well-Intended Love, Boss & Me, Hello Mr. Right). Adult workplace and marriage dramas go to B4-17; school settings go to B4-18.

label: Urban Romance Drama
secs: 1=Workplace Romance | 2=Professional Romance | 3=Marriage & Family Drama
defn: A mainland serial of adult lives in the city, love bound up with career, profession, marriage or family (The Rational Life, You Are My Hero, Best Choice Ever, Love in the Edge of Divorce). Young sweet romance goes to B4-16.

label: Youth Drama
secs: 1=High-School Youth Drama | 2=College Youth Drama
defn: A mainland coming-of-age serial of school or university years, first love and friendship before adulthood (A Love So Beautiful, With You, When I Fly Towards You, Hidden Love). Sports-team stories go to B4-19.

label: Sports & Esports Drama
secs: 1=Athletic Sports Drama | 2=Esports & Gaming Drama
defn: A serial whose engine is competition in a sport or a video game, romance and rivalry riding on training and tournaments (The Whirlwind Girl, Skate Into Love, Gank Your Heart, Love O2O). Campus life without competition goes to B4-18.

label: Romantic Fantasy Drama
defn: A modern-day mainland romance with one supernatural element, a spirit, alien, mermaid or curse, at its centre (My Girlfriend Is an Alien, I Cannot Hug You, The Fox's Summer, Love Me in Three Days). Displacement in time goes to B4-6; immortals in mythic worlds go to B4-8.

label: TVB Drama
secs: 1=Police & Crime Drama | 2=Professional Drama | 3=Family & Business Saga | 4=Costume Drama | 5=Supernatural & Comedy Drama
defn: A Hong Kong serial in the house tradition of Television Broadcasts Limited, the 20-to-30-episode Cantonese drama of cops, professionals and family empires (Line Walker, Forensic Heroes, Moonlight Resonance, War and Beauty). TVB wuxia goes to B4-7.

label: Thai Campus BL
secs: 1=University BL | 2=High-School BL | 3=Campus Sports & Band BL
defn: A Thai BL (Y series) love story set among students, the faculty, the hazing senior and the dorm its stage (SOTUS, 2gether, Bad Buddy, I Told Sunset about You). Thai BL among working adults goes to B5-2.

label: Thai Workplace & Adult BL
secs: 1=Office & Boss BL | 2=Professional BL | 3=Showbiz & Creative-World BL | 4=Food, Shop & Small-Town BL | 5=Fake-Boyfriend & Contract BL | 6=Adult Romance BL
defn: A Thai BL series about working adults, love tied to the office, a profession, showbiz, a shop or a contract (Lovely Writer, Step by Step, Moonlight Chicken, Last Twilight). Students go to B5-1; gangsters go to B5-3.

label: Mafia & Action BL
defn: A Thai BL series built on gangs, bodyguards, mafia families or fighters, violence and loyalty driving the romance (KinnPorsche, Never Let Me Go, The Heart Killers, Not Me). Murder mysteries go to B5-4.

label: BL Thriller & Horror
defn: A Thai BL series whose engine is a murder case, a killer or a horror, the romance inside a suspense plot (Manner of Death, Dead Friend Forever - DFF, Khemjira, The Effect). Ghost romance without dread goes to B5-5.

label: Fantasy & Period BL
secs: 1=Ghost & Supernatural BL | 2=Time-Slip & Reincarnation BL | 3=Period & Royal BL | 4=Vampire, Creature & Omegaverse BL
defn: A Thai BL series with a supernatural, time-crossing or historical premise (Until We Meet Again, Be My Favorite, Love in the Moonlight, OMG! Vampire). Horror goes to B5-4.

label: Japanese BL Drama
secs: 1=Office & Adult Romance | 2=School & Youth BL | 3=Fantasy & Supernatural BL | 4=BL Parody & Meta-Comedy | 5=Yakuza & Crime BL
defn: A Japanese boys' love television drama, usually a late-night adaptation of BL manga (Ossan's Love, Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?!, My Beautiful Man, What Did You Eat Yesterday?). Japanese GL goes to B5-11.

label: Korean BL Drama
secs: 1=School & Campus BL | 2=Office & Adult BL | 3=Fantasy & Supernatural BL | 4=Sageuk BL
defn: A Korean boys' love series, mostly short web-born drama adapted from webtoons and web novels (Semantic Error, To My Star, Light on Me, Painter of the Night). Korean GL goes to B5-11.

label: Taiwanese & Hong Kong BL
secs: 1=Taiwanese Campus BL | 2=Taiwanese Adult BL | 3=Queer Family & Literary Drama | 4=Hong Kong BL | 5=Singapore BL
defn: A boys' love series from Taiwan, Hong Kong or Singapore, the HIStory anthologies and their successors (HIStory, We Best Love: No. 1 For You, Kiseki: Dear to Me, I'm a Fool for You). Mainland danmei goes to B5-10.

label: Filipino BL
secs: 1=Lockdown-Wave Pinoy BL | 2=Post-Pandemic Pinoy BL
defn: A Philippine boys' love series, the Pinoy BL wave that began with the lockdown productions of 2020 (Gameboys, Hello Stranger, Gameboys 2, Love at First Spike). Filipino GL goes to B5-11.

label: Danmei Drama
secs: 1=Uncensored Web BL (2014–2017) | 2=Censored Danmei Adaptation | 3=Modern-Day Danmei & BL Drama
defn: A mainland Chinese drama from the danmei tradition, uncensored early web BL or censored 'bromance' adaptations of danmei novels (Addicted, The Untamed, Word of Honor, Guardian). Taiwanese BL goes to B5-8.

label: GL Series
secs: 1=Thai GL | 2=Japanese GL | 3=Korean, Filipino & Chinese-Language GL
defn: A girls' love series, a romance between women in the GL/yuri tradition (GAP, Blank, Ayaka Is in Love with Hiroko!, Lulu). Mixed BL and GL anthologies stay with their BL tradition.

label: Nam Nao Lakorn
defn: A prime-time Thai melodrama of passion, rivalry and revenge, often with the forced 'slap-kiss' romance (Sawan Biang, Leh Ratree, Game Sanaeha, So Wayree). Comic romance goes to B6-2.

label: Romantic Comedy Lakorn
defn: A Thai romance serial played for comedy, bickering couples and contrived arrangements (Love at First Hate, Boy for Rent, My Husband in Law, My Secret Bride). Melodrama goes to B6-1.

label: Period & Fantasy Lakorn
defn: A lakorn with a period setting or a supernatural premise, ghosts, time-slip or magic (Love Destiny, Happy Birthday, My Cherie Amour, 55:15 Never Too Late). Thai BL with such premises goes to B5-5.

label: Thai Remake Drama
defn: A Thai serial remaking a Korean, Taiwanese, Chinese or Japanese drama (Full House, F4 Thailand: Boys over Flowers, Princess Hours, Kiss Me). Original lakorn go to B6-1 to B6-3.

label: Thai Teen Drama
defn: A Thai series of teenagers and students, school, sport and first love, mostly from GMMTV and GTH (Hormones, U-Prince: Brian, Project S: Skate Our Souls, Kiss). Teen BL goes to B5-1.

label: Police Procedural
secs: 1=Detective Squad Procedurals | 2=Federal & Specialist Units | 3=Profiling & Behavioural Units | 4=Cold-Case Units | 5=Fantastic-Premise Procedurals
defn: A series whose engine is the investigation itself: detectives, agents or a specialist unit work cases through interviews, evidence and chain of command, usually one case per episode (Law & Order, NCIS, Criminal Minds, Cold Case). A series about the lives of uniformed cops or of bent and undercover officers goes to B7-2; a two-hander built on the partnership to B7-3; a lab-led show to B7-4; a single literary detective to B7-9; a serialised single murder to B7-8.

label: Police Drama
secs: 1=Patrol & Precinct Ensembles | 2=Undercover & Police-Corruption Dramas
defn: A series about the working lives of police officers themselves, the shift, the station, the street and the temptations of the badge, rather than about solving a case (Hill Street Blues, The Bill, The Shield, Line of Duty). A case-driven investigation series goes to B7-1.

label: Buddy Cop Series
secs: 1=Cop Duos | 2=Cop-and-Civilian Partnerships | 3=Comic Buddy Cops
defn: A police or law-enforcement series whose engine is a mismatched pair of partners whose friction drives the cases (Starsky & Hutch, Miami Vice, Castle, Rizzoli & Isles). An ensemble squad goes to B7-1; a sitcom about cops goes to B8.

label: Forensic Procedural
secs: 1=Crime-Scene Lab Procedurals | 2=Pathologist & Coroner Series
defn: A crime series in which the lab, autopsy table or crime scene is the investigative engine and the leads are scientists, pathologists or coroners (CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, Quincy, M.E., Silent Witness, Unnatural). A squad drama that merely uses forensics stays in B7-1.

label: Country Noir
secs: 1=American Backcountry & Frontier | 2=Outback & Antipodean Noir | 3=British, Irish & European Countryside
defn: A crime series set in a rural, small-town, frontier or outback community where the land, isolation and local kinship shape the crime and the lawman (Justified, Longmire, Mystery Road, Happy Valley). A Scandinavian series goes to B7-6; a Scottish one to B7-7.

label: Nordic Noir
secs: 1=Serialised Single-Case Investigations | 2=Recurring-Detective Series
defn: Scandinavian and Nordic crime drama in the bleak, socially critical register named for the cycle that followed The Killing and The Bridge: slow serialised investigations, damaged detectives, wintry landscapes (Wallander, Trapped, Deadwind). Remakes and imitations set elsewhere stay with B7-1 or B7-8.

label: Tartan Noir
defn: Scottish crime drama in the Tartan noir tradition of Ian Rankin and Val McDermid: hard-edged detectives in Edinburgh, Glasgow or the islands (Rebus, Shetland, Karen Pirie). An English village mystery goes to B7-11.

label: Whodunit
secs: 1=Police-Led Serialised Whodunits | 2=Closed-Circle & Golden Age Adaptations | 3=Ensemble & Anthology Whodunits
defn: A serialised mystery in which a single murder or disappearance, and the circle of suspects around it, sustains a whole season and the question who did it is the engine (Broadchurch, Mare of Easttown, And Then There Were None, Magpie Murders). A recurring detective solving a new case each story goes to B7-9.

label: Detective Drama
secs: 1=Sherlock Holmes & Holmesian Geniuses | 2=Golden Age Sleuths | 3=Star Police Inspectors | 4=Puzzle Mysteries (Honkaku)
defn: A series built around a single named star detective, police or private and often of literary pedigree, who solves a self-contained case each story through deduction and character (Agatha Christie's Poirot, Inspector Morse, Sherlock, Kindaichi Shonen no Jikenbo). A squad procedural goes to B7-1; a cosy village mystery to B7-11; a period-set detective to B7-12.

label: Inverted Detective Story
defn: A mystery series in which the audience sees the crime and culprit first and the pleasure is watching the detective work it out (Columbo, Poker Face, Elsbeth).

label: Cozy Mystery
secs: 1=Village & Island Police Mysteries | 2=Amateur & Clerical Sleuths
defn: A gentle murder mystery set in a village, resort or closed community where violence happens offstage and charm, humour and a returning cast matter as much as the puzzle (Midsomer Murders, Murder, She Wrote, Death in Paradise, Father Brown). A period setting first goes to B7-12.

label: Historical Mystery
secs: 1=Medieval to Victorian | 2=Edwardian & Interwar | 3=Wartime & Postwar
defn: A detective or police series whose cases are set in a past era that shapes method and motive (Cadfael, Murdoch Mysteries, Foyle's War, Babylon Berlin). Period gangland sagas go to B7-16.

label: Amateur Sleuth
secs: 1=Consultants to the Police | 2=Hobbyist & Accidental Sleuths | 3=Comic Sleuthing
defn: A series in which a non-police investigator, a consultant, academic, doctor, writer or hobbyist, solves crimes through a special gift, usually alongside the police (Monk, Psych, The Mentalist, Only Murders in the Building). Licensed private investigators go to B7-14.

label: Private Eye
secs: 1=Hardboiled & Lone Investigators | 2=Glamour & Action Agencies
defn: A series following a licensed private investigator or agency taking clients' cases, from hardboiled loners to glamorous agency teams (The Rockford Files, Magnum, P.I., Strike, Jack Irish).

label: Legal Thriller
secs: 1=Defence Lawyers | 2=The Accused | 3=Judges & Prosecutors
defn: A series in which a criminal trial, defence or prosecution is the suspense engine: lawyers, defendants and judges racing to the verdict (Perry Mason, The Night Of, How to Get Away with Murder, Presumed Innocent). Workplace legal dramas without the crime engine go to B1.

label: Gangster Drama
secs: 1=Mafia & Mob Families | 2=Period Gangland Sagas | 3=City Syndicates & Street Crews | 4=Outlaw Biker Clubs | 5=Yakuza, Triad & Asian Syndicates
defn: A saga told from inside a criminal organisation, mob family or gang, its loyalties, succession and turf wars (The Sopranos, Peaky Blinders, Gomorrah, Sons of Anarchy). A series about the drug trade itself goes to B7-17.

label: Narco Series
secs: 1=Cartels & Trafficking Routes | 2=Street Dealing & Urban Drug Wars | 3=Outsiders Who Turn Dealer
defn: A series about the drug trade as an economy: cooks, dealers, cartels, smugglers and the agents chasing them (Breaking Bad, Snowfall, Queen of the South, ZeroZeroZero). A mob saga where drugs are one racket goes to B7-16; a dramatised real kingpin to B7-21.

label: Heist & Caper
secs: 1=Robbery Heists | 2=Cons & Grifters | 3=Gentleman Thieves | 4=Gamblers & Card Sharps
defn: A series whose engine is the plan: a crew assembled for a robbery, a con or a theft, with the pleasure in the scheme and the double-cross (Money Heist, Hustle, Leverage, Lupin).

label: Neo-Noir
secs: 1=Ordinary People Turned Criminal | 2=Fixers, Lawyers & Middlemen | 3=Hitmen & Assassins | 4=Social-Realist & Anthology Noir
defn: A crime series told from the side of the morally compromised: fixers, hitmen, small-time crooks and ordinary people who slide into crime, in the fatalistic noir register (Better Call Saul, Ray Donovan, Good Girls, Mr Inbetween). An organised family saga goes to B7-16; a drug saga to B7-17.

label: Prison Drama
defn: A series set inside a prison, where incarceration, inmate hierarchies and escape are the engine (Oz, Wentworth, El marginal, Locked Up).

label: True Crime Drama
secs: 1=Murder & Serial-Killer Cases | 2=Fraud, Cons & Scandals | 3=Real Heists & Robberies | 4=Real Gangsters & Drug Lords | 5=Terror, Assassination & State Crime | 6=Wrongful Accusation & Justice Campaigns
defn: A scripted dramatisation of a real crime, case or criminal, told with named real people (American Crime Story, Des, Narcos, Scam 1992). Documentary series go to B11.

label: Serial-Killer Thriller
secs: 1=The Killer's Point of View | 2=The Hunt for the Killer
defn: A series organised around a serial killer, whether hunted across a season or followed from the inside (Dexter, The Following, You, The Fall). Episodic profiler units go to B7-1; real killers to B7-21.

label: Psychological Thriller
secs: 1=Missing Persons & Abductions | 2=Obsession, Stalking & Manipulation | 3=Identity, Memory & Double Lives | 4=Buried Secrets & Small-Town Mysteries | 5=Time-Slip & Uncanny Thrillers
defn: A thriller whose suspense lies in the mind: obsession, manipulation, unreliable memory, a missing person or a community's hidden secret, rather than in action (Fool Me Once, Behind Her Eyes, The Missing, Sharp Objects). A thriller of marriage and household goes to B7-24.

label: Domestic Noir
secs: 1=Marital Betrayal & Revenge | 2=Family Secrets & Inheritance | 3=Elite Cliques & School-Gate Rivalries | 4=Neighbours & Intruders
defn: A thriller set in marriage, family and the home, where the danger is a spouse, a lover, a neighbour or one's own household (Big Little Lies, The Undoing, Doctor Foster, Mine). An affair thriller led by sex goes to B7-25.

label: Erotic Thriller
defn: A thriller in which sexual obsession or seduction drives the danger (Fatal Attraction, Dark Desire, Toy Boy). A marriage thriller without the erotic engine goes to B7-24.

label: Revenge & Vigilante Thriller
secs: 1=Vigilantes & Avengers-for-Hire | 2=Personal Revenge
defn: A thriller whose engine is justice taken outside the law: a wronged person's long revenge or a vigilante crew punishing those the system lets go (The Glory, Taxi Driver, Revenge of Others, Vigilante).

label: Action Thriller
secs: 1=Counter-Terror & Ticking-Clock | 2=Lone Heroes & Ex-Soldiers | 3=Bodyguards & Protectors | 4=Hijacks, Hostages & Sieges | 5=Fugitives & Manhunts
defn: A thriller driven by pursuit, combat and the ticking clock: counter-terror agents, lone ex-soldiers, bodyguards, hijacks and fugitives (24, Reacher, Bodyguard, The Fugitive). A spy story goes to B7-28.

label: Espionage
secs: 1=Cold War Tradecraft | 2=Period & Wartime Espionage | 3=Present-Day Agencies & Counter-Terror | 4=Spy-Fi & Gadget Adventures | 5=Action Spies & Assassins | 6=Spy Comedy & Secret Double Lives
defn: A series about spies, intelligence agencies, double agents and covert operations (Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, The Americans, Homeland, Slow Horses). Counter-terror action without tradecraft goes to B7-27.

label: Political Thriller
defn: A thriller set in the machinery of state: governments, coups, diplomats, scandals and the press that exposes them (A Very British Coup, State of Play, Occupied, The Diplomat). A plot by hidden powers outside the state goes to B7-30.

label: Conspiracy Thriller
secs: 1=Corporate & Financial Conspiracies | 2=State & Security-Service Conspiracies | 3=Cults & Secret Societies | 4=Scientific & Biomedical Conspiracies
defn: A thriller in which an ordinary person or a small group uncovers a hidden plot by corporations, cults or shadow powers (Rubicon, Utopia, Edge of Darkness, Hunters).

label: Techno-Thriller
defn: A thriller in which hacking, surveillance, AI or advanced technology is the engine of threat and solution (Mr. Robot, Person of Interest, Hackerville, Zero Day).

label: Death Game
defn: A thriller in which participants are forced into a deadly or ruinous game with prizes and eliminations (Squid Game, Alice in Borderland, Liar Game, Kakegurui).

label: Teen Noir
secs: 1=High-School Secrets & Murders | 2=Classroom & Teacher Thrillers | 3=Boarding School & Campus Mysteries
defn: A mystery or thriller centred on teenagers, schools and campuses, where adolescent secrets, cliques and a death drive the plot (Pretty Little Liars, Veronica Mars, Riverdale, Girl from Nowhere).

label: Survival Thriller
defn: A thriller in which characters are stranded, trapped or hunted in a hostile place and must survive while a mystery unfolds (The Wilds, The Stranded, Persons Unknown, Jirisan).

label: Family Sitcom
secs: 1=US early network sitcom (1947–1959) | 2=US classic network era (1960s) | 3=US relevancy era (1970s): Lear & MTM | 4=US 1980s network era | 5=US Must See TV era (1990s) | 6=US 2000s network era | 7=US streaming era (2010s–) | 8=British family sitcoms | 9=Other national family sitcoms (to 1999) | 10=Other national family sitcoms (2000s–)
defn: A studio (multi-camera, audience or laugh-track) sitcom whose comic engine is the family household: parents, children and relatives colliding at home (Father Knows Best, All in the Family, The Cosby Show, Everybody Loves Raymond). A single-camera family comedy goes to B8-2; a family comedy-drama goes to B8-24.

label: Single-Camera Family Comedy
secs: 1=Nuclear & Suburban Families | 2=Working-Class Families | 3=Single-Parent, Blended & Surrogate Families | 4=Married Couples & New Parents | 5=Immigrant & Ethnic Families | 6=Joint-Family & Multigenerational Comedies | 7=Period Nostalgia Family Comedies
defn: A family sitcom shot single-camera without audience or laugh track, playing family life with filmic cutaways, narration or deadpan (Malcolm in the Middle, The Middle, Friday Night Dinner, Fresh Off the Boat). A studio family sitcom goes to B8-1; a family mockumentary such as Modern Family goes to B8-11.

label: Workplace Comedy
secs: 1=US early network and classic eras (1947–1969) | 2=US relevancy era (1970s): Lear & MTM | 3=US 1980s network era | 4=US Must See TV era (1990s) | 5=US 2000s single-camera turn | 6=US streaming era (2010s–) | 7=British golden age (1960s–1970s) | 8=British sitcom 1980s–1990s | 9=British sitcom 2000s (post-Office mockumentary turn) | 10=British sitcom since 2010 | 11=Other national workplace comedies (to 1999) | 12=Other national workplace comedies (2000s–)
defn: A comedy series whose comic engine is a workplace and its colleagues, the job supplying the situation and the hierarchy the conflict (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Cheers, The IT Crowd, Superstore). A workplace mockumentary goes to B8-11; a military unit to B8-4; a political office to B8-15.

label: Military Comedy
defn: A comedy series set in an army unit, camp or wartime posting, its humour drawn from rank, drill and the absurdities of war (Dad's Army, Hogan's Heroes, M*A*S*H, Bluestone 42). A satire of the military establishment as policy goes to B8-15.

label: Hangout Sitcom
secs: 1=US network era (1960s–1980s) | 2=US Must See TV era (1990s) | 3=US 2000s network era | 4=US streaming era (2010s–) | 5=British sitcoms (1970s–1980s) | 6=British post-alternative sitcoms (1990s–2000s) | 7=British sitcoms since 2010 | 8=Other national sitcoms (to 1999) | 9=Other national sitcoms (2000s–)
defn: A comedy series whose engine is a group of friends, flatmates or neighbours simply spending time together, plot subordinate to banter (Seinfeld, Friends, How I Met Your Mother, The Golden Girls). A group defined by a job goes to B8-3; one built around a romance to B8-6.

label: Romantic Comedy Series
secs: 1=Couple Comedies | 2=Dating & Singles Comedies | 3=Romantic Comedy Anthologies
defn: A comedy series whose engine is a couple or the search for love: courtship, cohabitation, dating and break-ups (Mad About You, Catastrophe, The Mindy Project, Nobody Wants This). A marriage played as family life goes to B8-1/B8-2; a romance-led drama to B1.

label: Teen Comedy
secs: 1=High-School Comedies | 2=College & University Comedies
defn: A comedy series about adolescents or students made for a general or adult audience, built on school, sex and growing up (The Inbetweeners, Derry Girls, PEN15, Community). A teen sitcom made for children's networks goes to B10-4.

label: Rural Comedy
defn: A comedy series whose engine is country or small-town life, often with the rube-versus-city contrast (The Andy Griffith Show, Green Acres, Corner Gas, Letterkenny). A small-town comedy-drama goes to B8-24.

label: Character Comedy
secs: 1=British golden age (1960s–1970s) | 2=British sitcom 1980s–1990s | 3=British sitcom 2000s (post-Office turn) | 4=British sitcom since 2010 | 5=Other national character comedies (to 1999) | 6=Other national character comedies (2000s–)
defn: A comedy series built on one grotesque, deluded or hapless central character whose flaw drives every plot (Fawlty Towers, Keeping Up Appearances, Mr. Bean, One Foot in the Grave). Where the comedy is the audience's embarrassment rather than the character, see B8-10.

label: Cringe Comedy
defn: A comedy series whose engine is social embarrassment, the awkward pause and the faux pas, often with the star playing a version of himself (Curb Your Enthusiasm, Peep Show, Extras, I'm Alan Partridge). A documentary-style cringe comedy goes to B8-11.

label: Mockumentary
secs: 1=Workplace Mockumentaries | 2=Character & Celebrity Mockumentaries | 3=Documentary & Reality-TV Pastiches | 4=Family & Community Mockumentaries
defn: A scripted comedy series shot as if it were a documentary or reality show, with talking heads and camera awareness (The Office, Parks and Recreation, Summer Heights High, What We Do in the Shadows).

label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
secs: 1=Alternative Comedy | 2=Absurdist Narrative Comedies | 3=Anti-Comedy
defn: A narrative comedy series whose engine is the illogical, dreamlike or anti-comic, breaking realism rather than embarrassing anyone (The Young Ones, The Mighty Boosh, Get a Life, Joe Pera Talks With You). A surreal sketch show goes to B8-13.

label: Sketch Comedy
secs: 1=Variety-Sketch Shows | 2=Live Ensemble Sketch Shows | 3=Troupe & Alternative Sketch Shows | 4=Character Sketch Shows | 5=Star-Vehicle Sketch Shows | 6=Topical & Satirical Sketch Shows | 7=Prank, Puppet & Riffing Shows
defn: A comedy series made of short unrelated sketches, with recurring characters but no running plot (Monty Python's Flying Circus, Saturday Night Live, The Fast Show, Key & Peele). A sketch series for children goes to B10-3.

label: Ramadan Comedy
defn: An Arabic-language comedy series made for the Ramadan prime-time season, typically thirty episodes, often social satire (Maraya, Tash ma Tash, Choufli Hal, El Kebeer Awi). Ramadan drama goes to B12.

label: Political Satire
secs: 1=Government & Politics Satires | 2=News Satire & Satirical Journalism | 3=Bureaucratic & Corporate Satire | 4=Royal & Period Satire | 5=Social Satire
defn: A comedy series that ridicules power: governments, politicians, news media, bureaucracy, monarchy or the rich (Yes Minister, The Thick of It, Veep, Brass Eye).

label: Parody Series
secs: 1=Cop-Show & Crime Parodies | 2=Spy, Action & Superhero Parodies | 3=Fantasy, Horror & Science Fiction Parodies | 4=Soap, Telenovela & Melodrama Parodies | 5=Film, TV & Media Spoofs
defn: A comedy series that imitates and mocks a specific genre or programme (Police Squad!, Sledge Hammer!, Childrens Hospital, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace). A documentary-form parody goes to B8-11.

label: Musical Comedy Series
defn: A comedy series in which characters perform songs as part of the story (Flight of the Conchords, Glee, Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, Schmigadoon!).

label: Sports Comedy
defn: A comedy series set around a team, athlete or sport, built on competition and locker-room egos (Coach, Eastbound & Down, Ted Lasso, Shoresy).

label: Fantasy Sitcom
secs: 1=Magic & Supernatural Beings | 2=Aliens, Robots & Creatures | 3=Afterlife & High-Concept Premises | 4=Body-Swap & Time-Slip Comedies
defn: A comedy series whose premise is a magical, supernatural or impossible element placed in everyday life (Bewitched, ALF, 3rd Rock from the Sun, The Good Place). Spaceships and future worlds go to B8-20; ghosts and monsters played for scares to B8-21.

label: Science Fiction Comedy
defn: A comedy series set in space, the future or a technological world (Hyperdrive, Avenue 5, Upload, The Last Man on Earth).

label: Horror Comedy
defn: A comedy series built on horror premises (ghosts, vampires, zombies, slashers) played for laughs (Santa Clarita Diet, Ghosts, Scream Queens, Stan Against Evil).

label: Crime Comedy
secs: 1=Criminal, Con & Heist Comedies | 2=Comic Detectives & Police | 3=Comic Murder Mysteries
defn: A comedy series whose engine is crime: criminals, cons, heists, comic cops or murder mysteries played for laughs (Porridge, Weeds, Los simuladores, The Afterparty). A parody of cop shows goes to B8-16; a crime drama to B7.

label: Black Comedy
defn: A comedy series that finds humour in death, cruelty, despair or taboo, inviting laughter at the dreadful (Nighty Night, Inside No. 9, Barry, Dead to Me).

label: Comedy-Drama
secs: 1=Family Dramedies | 2=Small-Town & Community Dramedies | 3=Medical, Legal & Teaching Dramedies | 4=Workplace, Showbiz & Arts Dramedies | 5=Women's Ensemble & Single-Life Dramedies | 6=Semi-Autobiographical Comedian Series | 7=Anthology & Vignette Dramedies
defn: A series that balances comedy with dramatic stakes and serialized character arcs, usually single-camera and hour or half-hour (Northern Exposure, Gilmore Girls, Sex and the City, Atlanta). Comedy built on illness, grief or crisis goes to B8-25; a drama with light touches to B1.

label: Tragicomedy
secs: 1=Illness & Dying | 2=Grief & Bereavement | 3=Addiction & Recovery | 4=Mental Health | 5=Divorce & Midlife Crisis
defn: A comedy-drama whose comedy is wrung from a wound: terminal illness, bereavement, addiction, mental illness or midlife collapse (The Big C, After Life, Kidding, Mom).

label: Space Opera
secs: 1=Star Trek | 2=Star Wars | 3=Stargate | 4=Battlestar Galactica & Military Space Opera | 5=Space Westerns & Adventure Operas | 6=Space Exploration & Colony Dramas
defn: A series whose drama plays out among starships, space stations and interplanetary polities (Star Trek, Babylon 5, The Expanse, The Mandalorian). Earth-bound alien drama goes to B9-2; a comic space series to B9-11.

label: Alien Invasion
secs: 1=Invasion & Occupation | 2=Hidden Aliens & Government Conspiracy | 3=First Contact | 4=Aliens Among Us
defn: A series whose engine is extraterrestrials arriving on Earth — as conquerors, hidden infiltrators, first contacts or neighbours (V, Falling Skies, 3 Body Problem, Roswell). Star-faring drama goes to B9-1.

label: Time Travel
secs: 1=Time-Travel Adventure | 2=Changing-the-Past Thrillers | 3=Time Slip | 4=Time Loop
defn: A series whose premise is movement through time — travellers, slips, rewrites or loops (Doctor Who, Quantum Leap, 12 Monkeys, JIN). Time-slip romance with rebirth goes to B9-19.

label: Mystery Box
defn: A serial built on a withheld central enigma that the audience decodes over seasons — an island, a vanished flight, a town no one can leave (Lost, Dark, Manifest, The OA). If the enigma is solved weekly by investigators, B9-22.

label: Techno-thriller
secs: 1=Genetic Engineering & Clones | 2=Enhanced Humans & Human Experiments | 3=Fringe Science & Corporate Conspiracy
defn: A science-fiction thriller whose threat is a near-present technology or experiment — clones, enhancements, fringe science (Orphan Black, Fringe, Limitless, Kyle XY). Machines that think go to B9-6; costumed powers to B9-12.

label: Artificial Intelligence in Fiction
secs: 1=Androids & Robots | 2=Virtual Reality & Simulation | 3=Cyberpunk
defn: A series whose premise is a thinking machine or a simulated world — androids, AI, virtual reality, cyberpunk cities (Westworld, Humans, Altered Carbon, Memories of the Alhambra).

label: Dystopian Fiction
secs: 1=Totalitarian Dystopia | 2=Technological & Corporate Dystopia | 3=Survival Games & Selection Dystopia
defn: A series set in an oppressive engineered society, or a contest that society stages for survival (The Handmaid's Tale, 3%, Severance, Alice in Borderland). A world after a catastrophe goes to B9-9.

label: Alternate History
defn: A series set in a history that diverged at a known point (The Man in the High Castle, For All Mankind, SS-GB). A traveller who changes history goes to B9-3.

label: Apocalyptic and Post-Apocalyptic Fiction
secs: 1=Pandemic & Extinction | 2=Wasteland & Collapse | 3=Impending Catastrophe
defn: A series about the end of civilisation — the plague, collapse or impact, or the world that survives it (Station Eleven, Jericho, The 100, Fallout). Zombie apocalypses go to B9-28.

label: Anthology Series
defn: A science-fiction or fantasy series telling a self-contained story with new characters each episode (The Twilight Zone, Black Mirror, The Outer Limits, Amazing Stories). Horror anthologies go to B9-26.

label: Comic Science Fiction & Comic Fantasy
secs: 1=Comic Science Fiction | 2=Comic Fantasy
defn: A series that plays a science-fiction or fantasy premise chiefly for laughs (Red Dwarf, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Good Omens, The Watch). A sitcom with a light fantastic touch stays in B8.

label: Superhero Fiction
secs: 1=DC Comics | 2=Marvel Comics | 3=Creator-Owned & Original Superheroes | 4=Superpowered-People Dramas | 5=Asian Superhero & Martial-Arts Power Series
defn: A series about costumed or superpowered heroes and their villains (Smallville, Daredevil, The Boys, Moving). Japanese henshin heroes go to B9-13.

label: Tokusatsu
secs: 1=Super Sentai | 2=Kamen Rider | 3=Ultra Series | 4=Metal Heroes & Other Henshin Heroes | 5=Power Rangers
defn: A Japanese special-effects hero series built on transformation (henshin), suit actors and miniature monsters, and its adaptations (Kamen Rider, Himitsu Sentai Goranger, Ultraman, Power Rangers).

label: High Fantasy
secs: 1=Epic Invented-World Fantasy | 2=East Asian Invented-World Fantasy | 3=Sword-and-Sorcery & Adventure Fantasy
defn: A series set wholly in an invented secondary world of magic, kingdoms and quests (Game of Thrones, The Wheel of Time, The Witcher, Alchemy of Souls). Myth and legend retold go to B9-15.

label: Mythic Fiction
secs: 1=Greco-Roman Sword-and-Sandal | 2=Arthurian & European Legend | 3=Arabian Nights & Asian Epics | 4=Gods in the Modern World
defn: A series that retells myth, legend or epic, or brings old gods into the modern world (Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, Merlin, Alif Laila, American Gods).

label: Fairy Tale & Portal Fantasy
secs: 1=Fairy-Tale Retellings | 2=Portal & Parallel-World Fantasy | 3=Children's Literary Fantasy
defn: A series that retells fairy tales or sends its characters through a door into a magical land (Once Upon a Time, The 10th Kingdom, His Dark Materials, A Series of Unfortunate Events).

label: Historical Fantasy
secs: 1=Steampunk & Gaslamp Fantasy
defn: A period series in which magic or the uncanny is woven into recognisable history (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, The Nevers, Carnival Row).

label: Urban Fantasy
secs: 1=Witches & Covens | 2=Werewolves, Shapeshifters & Fae | 3=Hidden Magical Worlds | 4=Angels, Demons & Immortals
defn: A series in which witches, shapeshifters, fae, angels or demons live hidden in the present-day world (Charmed, Lost Girl, The Magicians, Preacher). Teen-centred versions go to B9-21; investigators of the uncanny to B9-22.

label: Magic Realism
secs: 1=Body Swap & Possession | 2=Rebirth & Second Life | 3=Afterlife, Grim Reapers & Fate | 4=Magic-Realist Dramas & Thrillers
defn: A realist drama with one impossible premise taken matter-of-factly — a body swap, a second life, a grim reaper at work (Reborn Rich, Dead Like Me, Mystic Pop-up Bar, Wonderfalls). Fully supernatural worlds go to B9-18.

label: Paranormal Romance
secs: 1=Korean Fantasy Romance | 2=Chinese & Japanese Supernatural Romance | 3=Western Paranormal Romance
defn: A romance whose lover is supernatural — a gumiho, ghost, angel or beast (Tale of the Nine-Tailed, Bring It On, Ghost, A Discovery of Witches). Vampire romance goes to B9-23.

label: Supernatural Teen Drama
secs: 1=Slayers & Monster-Fighting Teens | 2=Teen Witches & Magic | 3=Teen Vampires & Werewolves | 4=Teen Horror Mysteries
defn: A teen drama in which adolescents fight, love or become monsters (Buffy the Vampire Slayer, The Vampire Diaries, Teen Wolf, Stranger Things).

label: Occult Detective Fiction
secs: 1=Paranormal Investigators | 2=Psychics & Mediums | 3=Monster Hunters & Exorcists | 4=Supernatural Cops & Consultants
defn: A series of cases solved by investigators of the paranormal — agents, psychics, hunters (The X-Files, Supernatural, Medium, Grimm). A serial enigma with no case-of-the-week goes to B9-4.

label: Vampire Fiction
secs: 1=Gothic Vampires & Dracula | 2=Vampire Plague & Apocalypse | 3=Vampire Romance & Society | 4=Vampire Detectives & Heroes
defn: A series centred on vampires (Dracula, True Blood, The Strain, Angel). Teen vampire romance goes to B9-21.

label: Ghost Story
secs: 1=Haunted Houses & Gothic Ghost Stories | 2=Asian Ghost Horror | 3=Cursed Media & Analog Horror
defn: A horror series driven by the dead returning to haunt a place, a family or an object (The Haunting of Hill House, Ju-On: Origins, Rose Red, Archive 81).

label: Supernatural Horror
secs: 1=Demonic Possession & Religious Horror | 2=Cults, Witches & Folk Horror | 3=Cosmic & Lovecraftian Horror | 4=Gothic & Literary Horror
defn: A horror series whose threat is demonic, occult or cosmic (The Exorcist, Midnight Mass, Lovecraft Country, Penny Dreadful). Ghosts go to B9-24; vampires to B9-23.

label: Horror Anthology
secs: 1=Hosted Classic Anthologies | 2=Season-Long Anthologies | 3=Episodic Modern Anthologies
defn: A horror series with new stories by episode or by season (Tales from the Crypt, American Horror Story, Masters of Horror).

label: Slasher
defn: A horror series in which a killer stalks and picks off a group one by one (Scream: The TV Series, Harper's Island, Chucky).

label: Zombie Apocalypse
secs: 1=The Walking Dead Franchise | 2=Zombie Survival | 3=East Asian Zombie Series
defn: A series about survival among the risen or infected dead (The Walking Dead, All of Us Are Dead, The Last of Us). Non-zombie collapse goes to B9-9.

label: Creature Feature
secs: 1=Dinosaurs & Lost Worlds | 2=Giant Monsters & Sea Creatures | 3=Monster-Siege Survival | 4=Body Horror & Parasites
defn: A series whose threat or wonder is a monster or prehistoric beast (Primeval, Tremors, Sweet Home, Parasyte: The Grey).

label: Psychological Horror
defn: A horror series whose terror is in minds and violence rather than the supernatural (Hannibal, Servant, Yellowjackets).

label: Comedy Horror
defn: A horror series played for laughs (Ash vs Evil Dead, The Baby, Post Mortem: No One Dies in Skarnes).

label: Preschool Television
defn: A live-action or puppet series made for children under about six, teaching through song, repetition and play (Sesame Street, Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Teletubbies, Blue's Clues). Animated preschool series go to C13.

label: Educational Children's Series
defn: A school-age children's series whose purpose is teaching reading, science or history, often with a presenter (The Electric Company, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy, Blue Peter).

label: Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy
defn: A comedy series for children made of sketches, puppet routines or variety segments rather than a single story (You Can't Do That on Television, All That, Pee-wee's Playhouse, 31 Minutes).

label: Teen Sitcom
secs: 1=School & Everyday-Life Sitcoms | 2=Family & Sibling Sitcoms | 3=Showbiz & Double-Life Sitcoms | 4=Magic & Superpower Sitcoms | 5=Hotel, Camp & Boarding Sitcoms
defn: A sitcom made for children's networks about tweens and teens at school, at home or in showbusiness (Saved by the Bell, Lizzie McGuire, Hannah Montana, iCarly). A teen comedy for adults goes to B8-7.

label: Teen Drama
defn: A serialized live-action drama or dramedy made for children's networks about teens: sport, dance, friendship and growing up (Andi Mack, The Next Step, Free Rein, Geek Girl). Teen drama for adults goes to B1.

label: Children's Adventure Series
secs: 1=Animal Companion Series | 2=Children's Literature Adaptations | 3=Kid-Gang & Detective Adventures
defn: A live-action children's series of realistic adventure: animal companions, literary classics and kid-gang mysteries (Lassie, Pippi Longstocking, Emil of Lönneberga, De Zevensprong). Magic and science fiction go to B10-7.

label: Children's Fantasy Series
secs: 1=Fairy-Tale & Everyday-Magic Series | 2=Magic School, Mermaid & Supernatural-Teen Series | 3=Science Fiction, Time-Travel & Superhero Series | 4=Children's Horror Anthologies
defn: A live-action children's series built on magic, the supernatural, science fiction or horror (Arabela, Round the Twist, The Worst Witch, Goosebumps).

label: Christmas Calendar
defn: A Nordic television serial of 24 episodes broadcast daily from 1 to 24 December (Jul i Skomakergata, Nissebanden, Sunes jul); adult parodies of the form (The Julekalender) stay here.

label: Nature Documentary Series
secs: 1=Landmark Natural-History Series | 2=The Attenborough "Life" Surveys | 3=Regional Natural-History Series | 4=Presenter-Led Wildlife Series | 5=Prehistoric Life Reconstructions
defn: A documentary series about animals, plants and ecosystems, including reconstructions of prehistoric life (Life on Earth, Planet Earth, Blue Planet II, Walking with Dinosaurs).

label: Science Documentary Series
secs: 1=Cosmos & Space | 2=General-Science Strands | 3=Explainer & Pop-Science Series
defn: A documentary series explaining science, space, the body or how things work (Cosmos: A Personal Voyage, NOVA, How the Universe Works, Explained).

label: History Documentary Series
secs: 1=Narrative National Histories | 2=Social & Cultural History | 3=Docudrama Hybrids | 4=Essay & Polemical History | 5=Disaster & Event Retrospectives
defn: A documentary series narrating past events, eras or peoples (other than war), from archive narration to docudrama (American Experience, Prohibition, The Century of the Self, Mayday). War history goes to B11-4.

label: War Documentary Series
defn: A documentary series about a war or the military history of an era (The World at War, The Civil War, The Vietnam War, Apocalypse: The Second World War).

label: Biographical Documentary Series
secs: 1=Entertainers & Celebrities | 2=Politicians, Royals & Business Figures | 3=Artists & Writers
defn: A documentary series portraying the life of a person (other than athletes and musicians) through archive and interview (Biography, The Roosevelts, Arnold, Harry & Meghan). Athletes go to B11-7; musicians to B11-6.

label: Music Documentary Series
defn: A documentary series about musicians, genres or music scenes (The Beatles Anthology, Jazz, Hip Hop Evolution, The Beatles: Get Back).

label: Sports Documentary Series
secs: 1=All-Access Season Docuseries | 2=Retrospectives & Athlete Portraits
defn: A documentary series about athletes, teams or sporting events (30 for 30, The Last Dance, Formula 1: Drive to Survive, Last Chance U). Live sport goes to B16.

label: Arts & Pop-Culture Documentary Series
defn: A documentary series about art, design, film, television, toys or pop culture, including making-of series (Civilisation, The Story of Film: An Odyssey, The Toys That Made Us, LIGHT & MAGIC).

label: Travel & Food Documentary Series
secs: 1=Travelogues | 2=Comic & Celebrity Travelogues | 3=Food & Culinary Documentary
defn: A non-competitive documentary series following a presenter through places or cuisines (Michael Palin: Around the World in 80 Days, An Idiot Abroad, Chef's Table, Street Food: Asia). Cooking competitions go to B13.

label: Investigative & Observational Documentary Series
secs: 1=Investigative Exposés | 2=Observational Docuseries | 3=Documentary Strands & Anthologies
defn: A documentary series exposing wrongdoing or observing an institution or community from inside, and the anthology strands that carry such films (Dirty Money, Rotten, Hopkins, POV). Criminal cases go to B11-11.

label: True Crime Docuseries
secs: 1=Single-Case Murder & Disappearance | 2=Serial-Killer Docuseries | 3=Wrongful Conviction & Trial Docuseries | 4=Cults, Abuse & Celebrity Scandal | 5=Fraud, Scams & Heists | 6=Organised Crime, Terror & Manhunts | 7=Case-of-the-Week & Reenactment Strands
defn: A documentary series reconstructing a real crime, investigation or trial (Making a Murderer, The Jinx, Tiger King, Forensic Files). A dramatized true-crime series goes to B7.

label: Paranormal & Pseudo-Documentary Series
defn: A series in documentary form about hauntings, aliens or lost civilisations, presenting fringe claims as investigation (Ancient Aliens, Paranormal Witness, Ancient Apocalypse).

label: News & Current Affairs Programmes
secs: 1=Newsmagazines & Investigative Current Affairs | 2=Political Interview & Debate Programmes | 3=Breakfast & Morning Television | 4=Evening Newscasts | 5=Cable News & Opinion Shows | 6=Tabloid & Entertainment News
defn: Regularly scheduled journalism programmes: investigative newsmagazines and current-affairs strands, political interview and debate programmes, breakfast television, evening newscasts, cable news and opinion shows, and tabloid and entertainment news magazines (60 Minutes, Panorama, Meet the Press, Today, PBS NewsHour, Entertainment Tonight).

label: Telenovela
secs: 1=Mexican Telenovelas | 2=Venezuelan & South American Telenovelas | 3=Colombian & US Hispanic Telenovelas | 4=Youth Telenovelas | 5=Telenovelas Outside Latin America
defn: A closed-ended Latin American (or Latin-modelled) melodrama serial of one central love story told over months of daily episodes (Los ricos también lloran, María la del Barrio, Yo soy Betty, la fea, Rebelde). Brazilian novelas go to B12-2; narco serials go to B12-3.

label: Brazilian Telenovela
defn: A Brazilian novela, typically a Globo prime-time serial with large ensembles and social themes alongside the central romance (Roque Santeiro, Vale Tudo, The Clone). Spanish-language telenovelas go to B12-1.

label: Narconovela
defn: A telenovela-format serial built around drug traffickers, cartels and the women around them (The Cartel, Pablo Escobar: The Drug Lord, La Reina del Sur). A narco crime series made in a non-telenovela format goes to B7.

label: Soap Opera
secs: 1=American Daytime Soaps | 2=British & Irish Continuing Dramas | 3=Australian & New Zealand Soaps | 4=European Daily Soaps
defn: An open-ended continuing drama broadcast daily or several times a week, with interwoven storylines in a fixed community that can run for decades (Coronation Street, Days of Our Lives, Neighbours, Gute Zeiten, schlechte Zeiten). A weekly prime-time serial of glamour and wealth goes to B12-5.

label: Prime-Time Soap Opera
defn: A weekly evening serial of wealth, glamour, family feuds and revenge, with cliffhangers in place of closure (Dallas, Dynasty, Melrose Place, Desperate Housewives). A daily continuing soap goes to B12-4.

label: Dizi
secs: 1=Melodrama Dizi | 2=Romantic-Comedy Dizi | 3=Crime, Revenge & Action Dizi | 4=Family Dizi | 5=Teen Dizi | 6=Ottoman Historical Dizi
defn: A Turkish television serial, typically of long weekly episodes, from the romance melodrama to Ottoman epics (What is Fatmagul's Fault?, Ezel, Erkenci Kuş, The Magnificent Century). A Turkish streaming miniseries outside the broadcast form goes to its genre leaf in B1.

label: Indian Television Soap Opera
defn: A Hindi (or other Indian-language) daily serial of joint-family conflict, marriage and the saas-bahu (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) axis (Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai, Anupamaa). Mythological serials go to B12-8.

label: Mythological Serial
defn: An Indian television serial retelling Hindu epics and Puranic stories of gods and heroes (Ramayan, Mahabharat, Devon Ke Dev...Mahadev). Biblical and Islamic epics go to B1-19.

label: Pakistani Drama
defn: A Pakistani Urdu drama serial, typically a closed 20–30 episode story of love, marriage and family duty (Humsafar, Zindagi Gulzar Hai, Meray Paas Tum Ho). Indian daily soaps go to B12-7.

label: Sri Lankan Teledrama
defn: A Sinhala-language teledrama, the daily or weekly serial of Sri Lankan television (Deweni Inima, Koombiyo). Kept small as the attested national tradition.

label: Musalsal
secs: 1=Historical Musalsal | 2=Social & Family Musalsal | 3=Crime, Spy & Thriller Musalsal
defn: An Arabic television serial, classically a 30-episode drama made for the Ramadan season (Bab Al-Hara, Omar, Al Hayba, Raafat Al Haggan). Turkish serials go to B12-6.

label: Teleserye
defn: A Philippine prime-time television serial in the telenovela mould, from romance to fantasy (Marimar, The Promise (Pangako Sa 'Yo), On the Wings of Love). Latin American telenovelas go to B12-1.

label: Sinetron
defn: The Indonesian television serial (sinema elektronik): long-running daily or weekly family, romance, religious and comedy serials of the private networks RCTI, SCTV and Indosiar (Si Doel Anak Sekolahan, Para Pencari Tuhan, Ikatan Cinta).

label: Talent Show
secs: 1=Variety Talent Shows | 2=Dance Competitions | 3=Celebrity Performance Contests | 4=Comedy, Magic & Novelty Talent
defn: A competition in which acts perform before judges or the public (Got Talent, Strictly Come Dancing, RuPaul's Drag Race). Singing-only contests go to B13-2.

label: Singing Competition
defn: A competition among singers decided by judges or votes (The Voice, Pop Idol, The X Factor, Star Academy). Idol-group debut shows go to B13-3.

label: Idol Survival Show
defn: A competition in which trainees vie for places in a debuting pop group, or groups battle for rank (Produce 101, Girls Planet 999, Queendom, I-LAND).

label: Reality Competition
secs: 1=Live-In Social Elimination | 2=Races & Expeditions | 3=Physical & Stunt Challenges | 4=Strategy Game Reality | 5=Skill, Lifestyle & Business Contests | 6=Comedy Endurance
defn: An unscripted contest in which players live, travel or endure under rules and are eliminated until one wins (Survivor, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, Physical: 100).

label: Cooking Competition
defn: A contest among cooks or bakers (MasterChef, The Great British Bake Off, Iron Chef, Culinary Class Wars). How-to cookery goes to B14-8.

label: Game Show
secs: 1=Quiz Shows | 2=Word & Puzzle Games | 3=Panel & Guessing Games | 4=Chance & Pricing Games | 5=Physical & Obstacle Games | 6=Music Game Shows | 7=Comedy Game Shows
defn: A studio programme in which contestants play a game for prizes (Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, The Price Is Right, Family Feud, Taskmaster). Comedy panel shows go to B15-4.

label: Dating Show
secs: 1=Dating Game Shows | 2=Dating Reality | 3=Same-Sex Dating Reality
defn: A programme that sets up real people to date, pair or marry (The Bachelor, Love Is Blind, Single's Inferno, Taken Out).

label: Docusoap
secs: 1=Celebrity & Family Docusoaps | 2=Ensemble Docusoaps & Structured Reality | 3=Occupational Reality
defn: An observational series following real people's lives as ongoing serial drama (The Osbournes, Jersey Shore, Terrace House, Cops).

label: Social Experiment
defn: A factual format that places people in a contrived situation to see how they cope (Wife Swap, Undercover Boss, 60 Days In, The Rehearsal).

label: Makeover Show
secs: 1=Personal & Style Makeovers | 2=Home & Property Makeovers | 3=Intervention & Rescue
defn: A format that transforms a person, home or business before the camera (Queer Eye, Extreme Makeover: Home Edition, Supernanny, Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares).

label: Hidden Camera
defn: A programme that films unwitting people reacting to staged pranks, or stunts staged for the camera (Candid Camera, Punk'd, Impractical Jokers, Jackass).

label: Paranormal Television
secs: 1=Ghost-Hunting Investigations | 2=Mediums & Psychics | 3=Cryptid & Monster Hunts
defn: A factual series investigating hauntings and the unexplained (Ghost Hunters, Paranormal State). Scripted ghost hunters go to B9-22.

label: Travel Documentary
secs: 1=Motoring & Road-Trip Shows | 2=Comic & Celebrity Travel Shows | 3=Survival & Wilderness Shows
defn: A presenter-led entertainment series built on a journey or road trip (Top Gear, The Grand Tour, Running Wild with Bear Grylls, Conan O'Brien Must Go).

label: Instructional Television
secs: 1=Cooking Shows | 2=Art, Craft & Hobby Instruction | 3=Know-How, Science & Collecting
defn: A how-to or explainer programme that teaches a skill or tests ideas (The Joy of Painting, Good Eats, MythBusters, Antiques Roadshow).

label: Court Show
defn: A programme in which a television judge arbitrates real small-claims disputes (Judge Judy, Judy Justice).

label: Business Reality Television
secs: 1=Pitch & Investment Shows | 2=Business Rescue & Turnaround Shows | 3=Undercover Boss Shows | 4=Pawn, Picking & Auction Shows
defn: Factual entertainment built around running or financing a business: entrepreneurs pitching to investors, experts rescuing failing restaurants, bars and hotels, bosses going undercover, and dealers trading, pawning and buying at auction (Dragons' Den, Kitchen Nightmares, Bar Rescue, Undercover Boss, Pawn Stars).

label: Property & Home Improvement Television
secs: 1=House-Hunting & Relocation | 2=Renovation, Flipping & DIY | 3=Self-Build & Design | 4=Real-Estate Agents & Luxury Listings
defn: Lifestyle television about buying, selling, building and renovating homes: house-hunting and relocation shows, renovation and flipping shows, self-build and design series, and luxury real-estate docusoaps (Location, Location, Location, House Hunters, Grand Designs, Fixer Upper, Selling Sunset). One-off makeovers of a home as a gift stay in B14-4 Makeover Show.

label: Crime & Law-Enforcement Reality
secs: 1=Ride-Along & Patrol Reality | 2=Border, Custody & Prison Reality | 3=Investigation & Sting Reality | 4=Bounty Hunting & Manhunts
defn: Reality television that follows police, border, custody and prison officers, bounty hunters and investigators at work, filmed on ride-alongs, in custody suites and in stings (Cops, Live PD, Border Security, 24 Hours in Police Custody, Dog the Bounty Hunter). Documentary investigations of past cases go to B11-11 True Crime Docuseries.

label: Variety Show
secs: 1=Golden Age Variety (1948–1960) | 2=Network Variety Hours (1961–1979) | 3=Post-Network & International Variety (1980–)
defn: A hosted revue of comedy, music and novelty acts (The Ed Sullivan Show, The Red Skelton Show, The Flip Wilson Show, Wetten, dass..?). Korean cast-based variety goes to B15-2.

label: Real Variety
secs: 1=Challenge & Game Variety | 2=Observational Variety | 3=Travel & Hospitality Variety | 4=Idol Reality & Variety
defn: A Korean-style variety programme in which a fixed celebrity cast plays missions, travels, runs a business or is observed living (Running Man, New Journey to the West, I Live Alone, Run BTS!).

label: Talk Show
secs: 1=Late-Night Talk Shows | 2=Satirical News Shows | 3=Daytime & Tabloid Talk | 4=Celebrity Chat & Comedy Talk
defn: A host-led programme of conversation with guests or audience (The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, The Daily Show, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Graham Norton Show).

label: Panel Show
secs: 1=Topical News Quizzes | 2=Comedy Panel Games | 3=Improvisational Comedy Formats
defn: A comedy programme in which a panel of comedians plays a loose quiz or improvisation game (Have I Got News for You, QI, Whose Line Is It Anyway?). Prize-driven games go to B13-6.

label: Clip Show
defn: A hosted programme built from home videos or viral clips (America's Funniest Home Videos, Ridiculousness, Tosh.0).

label: Association Football Broadcasts
secs: 1=International Tournaments | 2=Continental Club Competitions | 3=Domestic League & Cup Coverage | 4=Football Highlights & Magazine Programmes
defn: A broadcast of competitive association football played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (FIFA World Cup, UEFA Champions League, Match of the Day, Sportschau). A multi-sport Saturday programme that merely carries football goes to B16-17.

label: American Football Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive American (gridiron) or Canadian football played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Super Bowl, Monday Night Football, The NFL Today, Grey Cup). The Super Bowl halftime show as a concert goes to B16-25.

label: Basketball Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive basketball played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (NBA Finals, Inside the NBA, NCAA March Madness).

label: Baseball Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive baseball played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (World Series, Sunday Night Baseball, Japan Series, Little League World Series).

label: Ice Hockey Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive ice hockey played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Hockey Night in Canada, Stanley Cup Final, Summit Series). Olympic hockey games famous in their own right stay here with see_also B16-16.

label: Cricket Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive cricket played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Cricket World Cup, The Ashes, Indian Premier League, World Series Cricket).

label: Rugby Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive rugby union or rugby league played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Rugby World Cup, Six Nations Championship, State of Origin series, Rugby Special).

label: Tennis Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive tennis played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Wimbledon, Breakfast at Wimbledon, Battle of the Sexes).

label: Golf Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive golf played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Masters Tournament, The Open Championship, Ryder Cup, Shell's Wonderful World of Golf).

label: Motorsport Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive motor racing on cars or motorcycles played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Formula One World Championship, Indianapolis 500, Daytona 500, 24 Hours of Le Mans). A motoring magazine such as Top Gear is factual entertainment (B14).

label: Cycling Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive road or track cycling played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Tour de France, Giro d'Italia, Paris–Roubaix).

label: Athletics Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive track-and-field athletics or road running played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (World Athletics Championships, London Marathon, Diamond League). Athletics inside the Olympics goes to B16-16.

label: Snooker & Darts Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive snooker, pool or darts played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport, the indoor sports that became mass television in Britain (Pot Black, World Snooker Championship, PDC World Darts Championship). A darts game show such as Bullseye is a competition format (B13).

label: Combat Sports Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive boxing, mixed martial arts, kickboxing or sumo played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport, including named landmark bouts sold as pay-per-view events (Rumble in the Jungle, HBO World Championship Boxing, UFC 1, NHK Ōzumō). Professional wrestling, whose outcomes are scripted, goes to B16-18.

label: Horse Racing Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of competitive horse racing played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Kentucky Derby, Grand National, Melbourne Cup, Channel 4 Racing).

label: Multi-Sport Event Coverage
defn: The broadcast of a multi-sport games as one event, including its opening and closing ceremonies as landmark broadcasts (Olympic Games, 2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, Commonwealth Games, X Games). A single-sport championship goes to its sport leaf.

label: Sports Anthology & Magazine Shows
defn: A recurring studio-based programme that covers many sports, by live inserts, highlights, results, features or debate, rather than one sport (ABC's Wide World of Sports, Grandstand, SportsCenter, Das aktuelle Sportstudio). A highlights show for one sport goes to that sport's leaf; a sports quiz is a competition format (B13).

label: Professional Wrestling Television
secs: 1=Weekly Wrestling Programmes | 2=Pay-Per-View & Premium Live Events | 3=Puroresu & Lucha Libre Programmes
defn: A programme or event of professional wrestling: athletic performance with scripted outcomes and serial storylines, broadcast as live or live-to-tape matches (WWE Raw, WCW Monday Nitro, WrestleMania, Wrestle Kingdom). Unscripted combat sports go to B16-14.

label: Award Ceremonies
secs: 1=Film Award Ceremonies | 2=Television Award Ceremonies | 3=Music Award Ceremonies | 4=Theatre, Sports & Multi-Field Award Ceremonies
defn: The televised ceremony at which an academy, industry body or publication presents its annual awards, hosted and staged as a show (Academy Awards, Primetime Emmy Awards, Grammy Awards, Tony Awards). A song contest whose prize is decided on the night goes to B16-20.

label: Song Contests & Music Festival Broadcasts
defn: The broadcast of a song contest, in which new songs or national entries compete live for a prize, or of a named music festival as a televised event (Eurovision Song Contest, NHK Kōhaku Uta Gassen, Sanremo Music Festival, Melodifestivalen). A talent-search series with weekly eliminations (The X Factor) is a competition format (B13).

label: Beauty Pageants
defn: The televised final of a beauty pageant, in which contestants are judged on stage for a title (Miss Universe, Miss World, Miss America). A reality series about pageant children (Toddlers & Tiaras) is factual entertainment (B14).

label: Parades & New Year's Eve Broadcasts
defn: Annual live coverage of a civic parade, carnival or calendar festivity, above all New Year's Eve countdown shows (Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve, CCTV New Year's Gala, Jools' Annual Hootenanny). Military and state parades go to B16-23.

label: State & Royal Occasions
defn: Live coverage of a ceremony of state: coronations, royal weddings, state funerals, inaugurations, national-day and military parades (Coronation of Elizabeth II, Wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer, Trooping the Colour). Political news coverage is out of scope.

label: Telethons & Benefit Concerts
defn: A broadcast staged to raise money for a cause, either a long-form appeal telethon or a benefit concert broadcast live (Live Aid, Jerry Lewis MDA Labor Day Telethon, Comic Relief, 24-Hour Television). A concert without a fund-raising purpose goes to B16-25.

label: Concert Broadcasts & Specials
defn: A musical performance before an audience broadcast as a programme, as a one-off concert special or a recurring concert strand (Elvis: Aloha from Hawaii, Vienna New Year's Concert, MTV Unplugged, Austin City Limits). Studio chart and music-variety shows go to B15; benefit concerts to B16-24; opera and ballet to B16-26.

label: Theatre, Opera & Ballet Broadcasts
defn: A staged theatrical work (play, musical, opera, ballet) broadcast live or relayed from the stage, including the live television musical (Great Performances, Live from Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Opera: Live in HD, The Sound of Music Live!). A drama written for television (anthology drama) goes to B1.

label: Circus & Spectacle Broadcasts
defn: A broadcast of a circus show or of a live stunt or feat staged as a television event outside organized sport (Circus of the Stars, International Circus Festival of Monte-Carlo, Evel Knievel's Snake River Canyon jump, Skywire).

label: Stand-Up Comedy Specials
secs: 1=Premium Cable & Broadcast Specials | 2=Streaming-Era Specials | 3=Stand-Up Showcase Series | 4=Musical & Improvised Comedy Specials
defn: A recorded stand-up (or live improvised) comedy performance before an audience broadcast or streamed as a special, or a showcase series of such sets (Eddie Murphy: Delirious, Chris Rock: Bring the Pain, Nanette, Live at the Apollo). A theatrically released concert film goes to A12; sketch shows go to B8 or B15.

label: Battle Shōnen
secs: 1=Pirate, Hunter & Quest Adventures | 2=Fantasy-Kingdom & Alchemy Battles | 3=Modern-World Ability Squads | 4=Proxy-Battle Contests
defn: A long-running shōnen serial whose engine is an escalating ladder of fights inside a power system, with a hero who grows through rivals, training arcs and tournaments (One Piece, Hunter x Hunter, Fairy Tail, Fullmetal Alchemist). If the powers are ki-based martial arts it goes to C1-9; if the foes are demons, yōkai or curses, to C1-2.

label: Supernatural Battle Shōnen
secs: 1=Shinigami & Afterlife Battles | 2=Yōkai & Demon-Hunter Battles | 3=Exorcist & Curse-User Battles
defn: A battle shōnen whose fighters hunt or channel the supernatural, shinigami, yōkai, demons, curses, as an organised calling (Bleach, Kimetsu no Yaiba, Jujutsu Kaisen, InuYasha). Vampire hunting goes to C1-7; adult splatter to C1-8.

label: Superpower Anime (chōnōryoku)
secs: 1=Stand & Ability Duels | 2=Esper Cities & Institutes | 3=Ability Detectives & Syndicates | 4=Fugitive Espers & Test Subjects
defn: Action whose combatants are espers or ability users with one personal power each, and whose drama is the rules of those powers (JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken, Toaru Kagaku no Railgun, Bungou Stray Dogs, Darker than Black). Costumed hero work goes to C1-13.

label: Battle Royale & Death Game Anime
secs: 1=Holy Grail Wars (Fate) | 2=Death-Game Survival
defn: Action built on an enclosed, rule-bound contest in which participants must kill or be eliminated until one survives (Fate/Zero, Gantz, Darwin's Game, Juuni Taisen). An open tournament without killing goes to C1-9.

label: Battle School Anime
secs: 1=Magic-School Hierarchies | 2=Duel & Harem Academies
defn: A school or academy series, usually from a light novel, in which students rank, duel and graduate by combat magic or weapons (Mahouka Koukou no Rettousei, Rakudai Kishi no Cavalry, Gakusen Toshi Asterisk, Kill la Kill). A school setting in a Jump battle serial stays in C1-1.

label: Urban Fantasy Action
secs: 1=Hidden-World Magic Battles | 2=Dungeon-Gate Hunters | 3=Demon & Otherworld Incursions
defn: Action in which a hidden magical or otherworldly order breaks into the contemporary city and ordinary teens fight it, chiefly from light novels and games (Shakugan no Shana, Persona 4 the Animation, Ore dake Level Up na Ken, X). Shōnen-magazine demon hunting goes to C1-2.

label: Vampire Anime
defn: Action whose fighters are vampires or vampire hunters and whose conflict is the war between the undead and the living (Hellsing Ultimate, Strike the Blood, Owari no Seraph, Blade).

label: Seinen Action Anime
secs: 1=OVA-Boom Seinen Action (1985–1995) | 2=Television & Streaming-Era Seinen Action (2000–)
defn: Adult-demographic action whose fights are graphic, its heroes monstrous or compromised, and its tone nihilist (Tokyo Ghoul, Ajin, Terra Formars, Akame ga Kill!). Horror without a fighting engine goes to C9.

label: Martial Arts Anime
secs: 1=Ki & Power-Escalation Fighters | 2=Armoured Constellation Warriors | 3=Fighting Tournaments & Underground Bouts | 4=Fighting-Game Adaptations | 5=School-Brawl Fighters | 6=Post-Apocalyptic Fist
defn: Anime whose fights are bodily martial technique, ki, styles and lineages, contested in duels and tournaments (Dragon Ball Z, Grappler Baki, Hokuto no Ken, Saint Seiya). Weapon-based Japanese swordsmanship goes to C1-11; Chinese martial worlds to C1-12.

label: Ninja Anime
secs: 1=Naruto & Boruto | 2=Historical Ninpō Battles | 3=Modern Ninja
defn: Anime whose fighters are shinobi using ninjutsu or ninpō, historical or modern (Naruto, Basilisk: Kouga Ninpou Chou, Juubee Ninpuuchou, Nabari no Ou).

label: Samurai & Chanbara Anime
secs: 1=Wandering Swordsmen & Rōnin | 2=Bakumatsu & Shinsengumi | 3=Sengoku Warlords | 4=Supernatural & Demon-Hunting Jidaigeki | 5=Battle-Shōnen Jidaigeki
defn: A jidaigeki in animation: swordsmen of feudal or Bakumatsu Japan whose engine is the blade duel (Rurouni Kenshin, Samurai Champloo, Shigurui, Hakuouki). Ninja go to C1-10.

label: Wuxia & Xianxia Animation
secs: 1=Jianghu Wuxia | 2=Xianxia Cultivation Epics | 3=Modern-City Cultivation
defn: Chinese animation (donghua) of the martial world (wuxia) or of Daoist cultivation toward immortality (xianxia), including modern-city cultivation (Mo Dao Zu Shi, Doupo Cangqiong, Scissor Seven, Yi Ren Zhi Xia).

label: Superhero Anime
secs: 1=Hero Society (My Hero Academia) | 2=Henshin & Cyborg Hero Teams | 3=Superhero Parody & Deconstruction | 4=American Comics in Anime
defn: Anime about costumed or transforming heroes who protect the public, including hero societies, henshin teams, deconstructions and American comics made in Japan (Boku no Hero Academia, One Punch Man, Tiger & Bunny, Kagaku Ninja-tai Gatchaman). Tokusatsu-derived giant heroes go to C2-5.

label: Delinquent Anime (yankī)
defn: Anime about high-school delinquents and bōsōzoku gangs whose engine is the street brawl and gang loyalty (Tokyo Revengers, Wind Breaker, Beelzebub).

label: Gun Action Anime
secs: 1=Hitmen, Sweepers & Assassins | 2=Girls with Guns | 3=Mercenaries, Arms Dealers & Mafia
defn: Action whose engine is gunplay by hitmen, sweepers, mercenaries or armed heroines (Black Lagoon, City Hunter, Noir, Lycoris Recoil). Military units go to C1-17; cyborg police to C2-8.

label: Spy Anime
defn: Action whose heroes are secret agents running covert missions (Princess Principal, Spy Kyoushitsu, R.O.D: Read or Die, Yozakura-san Chi no Daisakusen).

label: Military Action Anime
defn: Action about soldiers, pilots and units in present-day or alternate-history warfare, without mecha or space settings (Area 88, Pumpkin Scissors, Kouya no Kotobuki Hikoutai). Future warfare goes to C2-7.

label: Super Robot
secs: 1=Classic Super Robots | 2=Combining & Hot-Blooded Revivals | 3=Mecha Deconstructions | 4=Occult & Mystic Giants | 5=Surreal & Parody Robots
