defn: Mecha anime in which a unique, near-mythic giant robot piloted by a hot-blooded hero fights monsters or invaders, with named attacks and combinations (Mazinger Z, Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann, Shinseiki Evangelion, Yuusha-Ou GaoGaiGar). Mass-produced machines in a realistic war go to C2-2.

label: Real Robot
secs: 1=Military Mecha Wars | 2=Rebellion & Political Mecha (Code Geass) | 3=Transforming Fighters & Idol Wars (Macross) | 4=Alien-War & Survival Mecha | 5=Police & Labor Mecha | 6=Fantasy-World Mecha | 7=Teen & Comedy Mecha
defn: Mecha anime in which robots are mass-produced weapons or tools in a plausible war or society, with logistics, politics and attrition (Soukou Kihei Votoms, Macross, Code Geass, Kidou Keisatsu Patlabor). The Gundam franchise is C2-3.

label: Gundam
secs: 1=Universal Century | 2=Alternate Universes | 3=Gunpla Battle
defn: Any entry of Sunrise's Gundam franchise, the founding real-robot saga (Kidou Senshi Gundam, Kidou Senshi Zeta Gundam, Gundam Wing, Kidou Senshi Gundam: Suisei no Majo).

label: Mecha Musume
defn: Anime whose fighters are girls fused with machine parts, warships or aircraft, or girl-shaped machines (Strike Witches, Kantai Collection: KanColle, Aoki Hagane no Arpeggio, Frame Arms Girl).

label: Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
defn: Animation of the tokusatsu tradition, giant monsters (kaiju), Ultra-type giant heroes and Kamen Rider-type henshin armour (SSSS.Gridman, Ultraman, Godzilla: Kaijuu Wakusei, Kaijuu 8-gou).

label: Space Opera Anime
secs: 1=Galactic War Epics | 2=Space Pirates & Wanderers | 3=Space Westerns & Bounty Hunters | 4=Space Adventure, Survival & Spaceflight
defn: Science fiction set among starships and planets, whose scale is interstellar war, piracy or roaming adventure (Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu, Uchuu Senkan Yamato, Cowboy Bebop, Uchuu Kaizoku Captain Herlock). Space mecha go to C2-1/C2-2. Grounded spaceflight drama (Planetes, Ouritsu Uchuugun: Honneamise no Tsubasa) sits in the last section.

label: Military Science Fiction Anime
defn: Science fiction about future or alternate-world soldiers, fleets and wars, without giant robots as the core (Last Exile, Blue Gender, Gyakusatsu Kikan, All You Need Is Kill).

label: Cyberpunk Anime
secs: 1=Ghost in the Shell | 2=Cyber-Police & Hardsuits | 3=Cyborg & Android Noir | 4=Megacity Underworlds
defn: Science fiction of high tech and low life: cyborgs, networks and megacities policed by corporations and states (Akira, Koukaku Kidoutai, Psycho-Pass, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners).

label: Virtual Reality Anime
defn: Science fiction whose stakes play out inside virtual worlds, games or augmented reality (Accel World, Summer Wars, Dennou Coil, Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online). Trapped-in-another-world fantasy goes to C3.

label: Android & Artificial Intelligence Anime
defn: Science fiction whose subject is robots, androids and AIs as persons (Tetsuwan Atom, Pluto, Eve no Jikan, Vivy: Fluorite Eye's Song). Giant piloted robots go to C2-1/C2-2.

label: Dystopian Anime
defn: Science fiction of a controlled, unjust future society that its heroes expose or resist (Shinsekai yori, No.6, Harmony, Guilty Crown). Tech-noir megacities go to C2-8.

label: Post-Apocalyptic Anime
secs: 1=Survival & Rebuilding | 2=Wasteland Action | 3=Eco-Apocalypse | 4=Quiet End-of-the-World
defn: Science fiction set after the collapse of civilisation, about surviving, wandering or rebuilding (Kaze no Tani no Nausicaä, Dr. Stone, Shoujo Shuumatsu Ryokou, Casshern Sins). Hokuto no Ken stays in C1-9.

label: Time Travel Anime
defn: Science fiction whose plot engine is time travel, time loops or crossing between parallel worlds (Steins;Gate, Toki wo Kakeru Shoujo, Noein, Gnosia).

label: Alien Invasion & First Contact Anime
defn: Science fiction about aliens arriving on Earth, invading, infiltrating, or simply moving in (Kiseijuu: Sei no Kakuritsu, Seikaisuru Kado, Dead Dead Demons Dededede Destruction, Ansatsu Kyoushitsu).

label: Steampunk Anime
defn: Science fiction of an alternate steam-age technology, airships and clockwork (Steamboy, Fushigi no Umi no Nadia, Sakura Taisen, Clockwork Planet).

label: Science Fiction Anthology Film
defn: An omnibus of short SF films by several directors under one title (Memories, Robot Carnival, Manie-Manie: Meikyuu Monogatari, Genius Party).

label: Isekai (Transported to Another World)
secs: 1=Portal Fantasy | 2=Summoned Hero | 3=Transported Adventurer (Cheat Skill) | 4=Modern Know-How in Another World | 5=Isekai Comedy & Parody | 6=Reverse Isekai
defn: A series or film whose protagonist is physically carried, summoned or dropped from our world into another, and whose story turns on being an outsider there (Fushigi Yuugi, Re:Zero, Tate no Yuusha no Nariagari, Gate). Rebirth into the other world goes to C3-2; being trapped inside a game goes to C3-4.

label: Isekai Tensei (Reincarnation)
secs: 1=Reborn into a New Life | 2=Reborn as a Non-Human | 3=Slow-Life Isekai
defn: A story whose protagonist dies in our world and is reborn, with memories intact, into a fantasy world, as a person or as something else (Mushoku Tensei, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken, Kumo desu ga, Nani ka?, Isekai Nonbiri Nouka). Reborn into an otome game goes to C3-3.

label: Otome Isekai (Villainess)
defn: A story whose heroine (rarely a hero) is reborn or transported into the world of an otome game or romance novel, typically as its doomed villainess, and must rewrite the plot (Otome Game no Hametsu Flag shika Nai Akuyaku Reijou ni Tensei shiteshimatta, Akuyaku Reijou Level 99, Seijo no Maryoku wa Bannou desu). A villainess romance with no crossing goes to C5-9.

label: Game-World Isekai (VRMMO & LitRPG)
secs: 1=Trapped in a VRMMO | 2=Transported into a Game World | 3=Virtual-Reality Gaming
defn: A story set inside an online or video game, or a world run on its rules, where the hero is a player, trapped player or transported avatar (Sword Art Online, .hack//Sign, Log Horizon, Overlord, Shangri-La Frontier). A fantasy world with mere status screens stays in C3-1.

label: High Fantasy
secs: 1=Fantasy War Epic | 2=Court & Kingdom Intrigue | 3=Travelogue Fantasy | 4=Witch & Wizard Fantasy | 5=Storybook & Fable Fantasy
defn: A story set wholly in an invented secondary world with its own history, kingdoms and magic, built around wars, courts, journeys or the craft of magic rather than a questing party (Arslan Senki, Kemono no Souja Erin, Kino no Tabi, Little Witch Academia). Party adventure goes to C3-6; grim violence to C3-8.

label: Sword and Sorcery
secs: 1=Questing Heroes & Parties | 2=Dungeon & Adventurers' Guild | 3=Party Exile & Hidden-Power Adventurers | 4=Video-Game Franchise Fantasy
defn: A fantasy-world adventure whose engine is a hero or party of swordsmen, mages and thieves questing, fighting monsters and delving dungeons (Lodoss-tou Senki, Sousou no Frieren, Dungeon ni Deai wo Motomeru no wa Machigatteiru Darou ka, Tales of Zestiria the X). Comic sword and sorcery goes to C3-7; grimdark to C3-8.

label: Comic Fantasy
defn: A secondary-world fantasy whose primary engine is comedy and genre parody (Slayers, Dragon Half, Mairimashita! Iruma-kun). Isekai parody goes to C3-1 section 5.

label: Dark Fantasy
secs: 1=Grimdark Swords & Monsters | 2=Demonic Transformation | 3=Titans & Siege Survival | 4=Gothic & Fairy-Tale Darkness
defn: A fantasy whose world is defined by horror, cruelty and despair, with demons, monsters and graphic violence (Berserk, Claymore, Shingeki no Kyojin, Devilman: Crybaby, Made in Abyss). Pure horror without a fantasy world goes to C9.

label: Science Fantasy
defn: A fantasy whose world mixes magic with lost technology, steampunk machines or a post-apocalyptic future (Tenkuu no Shiro Laputa, Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children, Utawarerumono, Houseki no Kuni). Hard science fiction goes to C2.

label: Mythic Fiction
secs: 1=Japanese Gods & Kami | 2=Gods & Demons of World Myth | 3=Afterlife & Limbo
defn: A story built from myth and religion: gods, kami, demons and the afterlife acting in a world or limbo of their own (Mononoke Hime, Haibane Renmei, Angel Beats!, Campione!). Chinese gods-and-demons stories go to C3-11; yōkai to C3-13.

label: Shenmo & Xianxia
defn: A Chinese-tradition fantasy of gods, demons, immortals and spirit beasts, from the shenmo classics to cultivation (xianxia) and fox-spirit tales (Hakujaden, Nezha Zhi Mo Tong Jiang Shi, Huyao Xiao Hongniang, Fanren Xiu Xian Zhuan). Martial-arts combat-first wuxia goes to C1.

label: Urban Fantasy
secs: 1=Hidden Magic & Mage Societies | 2=Supernatural Beings in the City | 3=Everyday Magic & Contemporary Fantasy Films | 4=Monogatari Oddities
defn: A story set in the contemporary everyday world where magic, monsters or a hidden supernatural society exist alongside ordinary life (Durarara!!, Kara no Kyoukai, Kyoukai no Kanata, Bakemonogatari). Japanese folklore spirits go to C3-13; ghost hunters to C3-14; vampires to C3-15.

label: Yōkai Fiction
secs: 1=Spirit-Seer Tales | 2=Yōkai Comedy & Everyday Life | 3=Yōkai Battle & Guardians | 4=Spirit-World & Kamikakushi Journeys
defn: A story whose supernatural beings are the yōkai, kami and spirits of Japanese folklore, met by seers, children or guardians (Natsume Yuujinchou, Mushishi, Gegege no Kitarou, Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi). Yōkai romances go to C5-8.

label: Occult Detective Fiction
defn: A story whose protagonists investigate and exorcise ghosts, curses and demons as a profession or calling (Tokyo Babylon, Ga-Rei: Zero, Koukyuu no Karasu, Muhyo to Rouji). Battle-first exorcist shōnen goes to C1.

label: Vampire Fiction
defn: A story whose central figures are vampires, as hunters, monsters or anti-heroes (Vampire Hunter D, Trinity Blood, Vanitas no Karte, Kizumonogatari). A vampire love story goes to C5-8.

label: Majokko (Classic Magical Girl)
defn: A magical-girl series whose heroine uses magic, often with a transforming item and mascot, in everyday life rather than in battle (Mahoutsukai Sally, Mahou no Tenshi Creamy Mami, Cardcaptor Sakura, Ojamajo Doremi). Teams fighting monsters go to C4-2.

label: Magical Girl Warrior
secs: 1=Shōjo Warrior Teams | 2=Otaku-Oriented Battle Magical Girls | 3=Magical Boys & Parodies
defn: A magical-girl series whose transformed heroines, usually a team, fight monsters or villains (Bishoujo Senshi Sailor Moon, Futari wa Precure, Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha, Senki Zesshou Symphogear). Grim deconstructions go to C4-3.

label: Dark Magical Girl
defn: A magical-girl series that deconstructs the form, making the contract, battles and transformation sources of trauma, death or despair (Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, Yuuki Yuuna wa Yuusha de Aru, Mahou Shoujo Ikusei Keikaku, Mahou Shoujo Site).

label: Shōjo Romance
secs: 1=School First Love | 2=Comic & Boy-Centred Shōjo Romance | 3=Period & Adult Shōjo Romance
defn: A love story told from a girl's point of view in the shōjo-manga tradition, about first love, confession and the couple's bond (Kimi ni Todoke, Ao Haru Ride, Marmalade Boy, Fruits Basket). Comedy-first school romance goes to C5-4; one heroine wooed by many to C5-3.

label: Josei Romance
secs: 1=Adult Romantic Drama | 2=Workplace & Otaku Romantic Comedy
defn: A love story about adult women's work, friendship and relationships, from the josei-manga tradition (Nana, Hachimitsu to Clover, Paradise Kiss, Wotaku ni Koi wa Muzukashii).

label: Reverse Harem
secs: 1=Shōjo Reverse Harem | 2=Otome-Game Adaptations
defn: A romance in which one heroine is surrounded and courted by several young men (Ouran Koukou Host Club, Hana yori Dango, Uta no Prince-sama-type otome adaptations such as Kiniro no Corda, Diabolik Lovers).

label: Romantic Comedy
secs: 1=School Love Comedy | 2=Teasing Romantic Comedy | 3=Otaku & Gamer Romantic Comedy | 4=Marriage & Cohabitation Comedy | 5=Workplace Romantic Comedy
defn: A romance whose engine is comic: misunderstandings, pride, teasing and slow-burning confessions between one central couple (Toradora!, Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai, Karakai Jouzu no Takagi-san, Tonikaku Kawaii). A boy courted by many girls goes to C5-5; a girl's first-love story to C5-1.

label: Harem
secs: 1=Domestic & School Harem | 2=Dating-Sim & Visual-Novel Harem | 3=Science-Fiction & Fantasy Harem (Oshikake)
defn: A romance in which one ordinary male lead is surrounded by several girls who desire him (Love Hina, Tenchi Muyou!, Nisekoi, 5-toubun no Hanayome). One girl courted by many men goes to C5-3.

label: Romantic Drama
secs: 1=Visual-Novel Romantic Drama | 2=School-Age Romantic Drama | 3=Adult Romantic Drama | 4=Romance Feature Films
defn: A love story whose engine is longing, loss, illness, love triangles or separation rather than comedy (Clannad, White Album 2, Byousoku 5 Centimeter, Koi wa Ameagari no You ni).

label: Sekai-kei
defn: A love story in which a teenage couple's relationship is tied directly to the fate of the world, with society in between left out (Saishuu Heiki Kanojo, Kimi no Na wa., Tenki no Ko, Seishun Buta Yarou).

label: Paranormal Romance
secs: 1=Goddess, Android & Alien Lovers | 2=Yōkai & Monster Lovers | 3=Vampire Romance | 4=Ghost & Spirit Romance
defn: A love story between a human and a supernatural or artificial being: goddess, android, alien, yōkai, vampire or ghost (Aa! Megami-sama!, Chobits, Kamisama Hajimemashita, Vampire Knight). Supernatural stories without a romance engine go to C3.

label: Romantic Fantasy
secs: 1=Fairy-Tale & Court Romance | 2=Villainess & Broken-Engagement Romance
defn: A love story set in a fantasy or fairy-tale kingdom whose engine is the courtship (Akagami no Shirayuki-hime, Akatsuki no Yona, Unnamed Memory, Loop 7-kaime no Akuyaku Reijou). Rebirth into an otome game goes to C3-3.

label: Boys' Love
secs: 1=School & Youth BL | 2=Adult & Workplace BL | 3=Fantasy, Sci-Fi & OVA BL
defn: A romance between male characters in the boys' love (yaoi) tradition (Junjou Romantica, Given, Sasaki to Miyano, Loveless).

label: Yuri
secs: 1=School & Everyday Yuri | 2=Fantasy & Comic Yuri
defn: A romance or intense bond between female characters in the yuri tradition (Maria-sama ga Miteru, Yagate Kimi ni Naru, Adachi to Shimamura, Citrus).

label: Iyashikei
secs: 1=Countryside & Seaside Iyashikei | 2=Fantastical & Twilight-World Iyashikei | 3=Pet & Animal Iyashikei | 4=Travel, Camping & Outdoor Iyashikei
defn: A series or film whose purpose is to soothe: unhurried days, gentle landscapes and an absence of real conflict carry it (Aria the Animation, Non Non Biyori, Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou, Yuru Camp). If the healing comes mainly from a cast of cute girls bantering, it goes to C6-2; if from food, C6-7.

label: Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
secs: 1=Four-Panel School Ensembles | 2=Hobby & Club Ensembles | 3=Café & Workplace Ensembles | 4=Supernatural & Fantasy Ensembles | 5=Moe Military & Mecha Ensembles | 6=Kemonomimi & Fanservice Moe
defn: An ensemble of (usually) teenage girls whose small daily pleasures and banter are the whole story, usually adapted from a four-panel manga (Azumanga Daiou, K-On!, Kiniro Mosaic, Gochuumon wa Usagi desu ka?). A healing landscape series goes to C6-1; a band or idol arc that drives the plot goes to C6-4 or C6-5.

label: Club Activity Anime (Bukatsu)
defn: A series built around an after-school or university club (bukatsu) whose activity is a hobby rather than a sport or a band: otaku circles, film-making, diving, odd societies (Genshiken, Eizouken ni wa Te wo Dasu na!, Grand Blue). A sports club goes to C7; a girls' hobby ensemble with no arc goes to C6-2.

label: Idol Anime
secs: 1=Girl Idol Units | 2=Boy Idol Units | 3=Idol Hybrids & Parodies
defn: A series whose protagonists train, debut and perform as Japanese-style pop idols (Love Live!, The iDOLM@STER, Uta no Prince-sama, Zombieland Saga). A rock band goes to C6-5; a thriller set in the idol industry goes to C8-2.

label: Music Anime
secs: 1=Rock & Pop Band Anime | 2=Concert Band & Orchestra Anime | 3=Classical Soloist Anime | 4=Jazz, Rap & Traditional-Music Anime
defn: A series or film about making music as players, where rehearsal and performance are the dramatic spine (Beck, Hibike! Euphonium, Shigatsu wa Kimi no Uso, Bocchi the Rock!). Idol units go to C6-4; staged theatre and rakugo go to C6-6; a cute-girls band ensemble without a performance arc (K-On!) stays in C6-2.

label: Performing Arts Anime
defn: A series about stage performers outside pop music: actors, revue and theatre troupes, rakugo storytellers, voice actors and dancers (Shouwa Genroku Rakugo Shinjuu, Kageki Shoujo!!, Glass no Kamen, Shoujo Kageki Revue Starlight). Idols go to C6-4; competitive ballroom goes to C7-11.

label: Cooking & Gourmet Anime
defn: A series in which preparing, serving or eating food is the engine of each episode: cooking battles, home cooking, gourmet drinking and fantasy restaurants (Shokugeki no Souma, Amaama to Inazuma, Isekai Shokudou, Wakako-zake). A café used only as a backdrop for cute girls goes to C6-2.

label: Workplace Anime (Oshigoto)
secs: 1=Creative-Industry Anime | 2=Service & Retail Comedies | 3=Office & Salaryman Anime | 4=Professions & Trades
defn: A series about doing a job, in which the profession's routines, deadlines and colleagues drive the story (Shirobako, Working!!, Aggressive Retsuko, Bakuman.). A café that only frames a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2; a restaurant whose dishes drive it goes to C6-7.

label: Family Slice of Life (Home Drama)
secs: 1=Parents & Found Families | 2=Siblings & Household Comedies | 3=Supernatural & Fantasy Households
defn: An episodic series about a household — a single parent, a found family, siblings or a new marriage — whose daily care and quarrels are the story (Usagi Drop, Kakushigoto, Gakuen Babysitters, Ani ni Tsukeru Kusuri wa Nai!). Arc-driven family films go to C8-7; family comedy for small children goes to C11-1.

label: Monster Girl Anime
defn: A slice-of-life or comedy series in which a dragon, demi-human, mermaid, vampire or other non-human girl lives in the human everyday (Kobayashi-san Chi no Maid Dragon, Demi-chan wa Kataritai, Shinryaku! Ika Musume). A fanservice harem of monster girls goes to C10-9; a demon lord working a day job goes to C10-6.

label: Baseball Anime
defn: A sports series or film whose contests are baseball games, typically high-school Koushien drives (Major, Touch, Diamond no Ace, Ookiku Furikabutte). A baseball con-game thriller such as One Outs stays here with see-also C8-3.

label: Football Anime
secs: 1=Association Football | 2=Rugby, Gridiron & Kabaddi
defn: A sports series whose contests are association football or another football code — rugby, American football — or a kindred contact team game (Captain Tsubasa, Inazuma Eleven, Blue Lock, Eyeshield 21).

label: Basketball Anime
defn: A sports series or film whose contests are basketball games (Slam Dunk, Kuroko no Basket, Ahiru no Sora). Franchise omake and NG reels stay with their series.

label: Volleyball Anime
defn: A sports series whose contests are volleyball, indoor or beach (Haikyuu!!, Attack No.1, Harukana Receive). The Attack No.1 shoujo spokon is the canonical ancestor; franchise specials stay with their series.

label: Racket Sports Anime
defn: A sports series whose contests are played with a racket or paddle: tennis, badminton, table tennis (Tennis no Oujisama, Baby Steps, Ping Pong the Animation, Hanebado!). Gag shorts such as Teekyuu go to C10-1.

label: Combat Sports Anime
defn: A sports series about a ring or mat contest — boxing, pro wrestling, judo, sumo, kendo (Ashita no Joe, Hajime no Ippo, Megalo Box, Yawara!). Fantasy fighting tournaments go to C1.

label: Racing Anime
secs: 1=Street & Touge Racing | 2=Circuit & Formula Racing | 3=Road Cycling
defn: A sports series or film whose contests are races on wheels — street and touge racing, circuit and formula racing, road cycling (Initial D, Mach GoGoGo, Redline, Yowamushi Pedal).

label: Swimming & Water Sports Anime
defn: A sports series about swimming, diving, surfing or racing on water (Free!, Dive!!, Wave!! Surfing Yappe!!). A fanservice swim-club series goes to C10-10; a diving-club comedy to C6-3.

label: Winter & Ice Sports Anime
defn: A sports series about figure skating, ice hockey or other sports on ice (Yuri!!! on Ice, Medalist, Skate-Leading Stars). Idol series that only use skating go to C6-4.

label: Horse Racing Anime
defn: A sports series about thoroughbred racing, literal or through horse-girls (Uma Musume: Pretty Derby, Gunjou no Fanfare). Small, but a recognised franchise canon.

label: Individual Sports Anime
secs: 1=Track & Running | 2=Gymnastics, Cheer & Dance Sport | 3=Archery, Golf & Precision Sports | 4=Climbing, Skating & Extreme Sports | 5=Shooting, Airsoft & Tankery
defn: A sports series about a sport scored person by person rather than by a ball team: track and running, gymnastics and cheer, archery and golf, climbing and skating, shooting and airsoft (Kaze ga Tsuyoku Fuiteiru, Tsurune, Birdie Wing, SK8 the Infinity). Ball team sports go to C7-1 to C7-4.

label: Board Game & Mind Sport Anime
secs: 1=Go & Shogi | 2=Karuta | 3=Mahjong | 4=Other Tabletop & Quiz Games
defn: A series about competitive play at a traditional table game — go, shogi, karuta, mahjong — or a quiz (Hikaru no Go, Chihayafuru, Saki, 3-gatsu no Lion). Gambling for ruinous stakes goes to C8-3.

label: Card Game Anime
defn: A series whose battles are trading-card-game duels, usually a tie-in to the card game itself (Yu-Gi-Oh!, Cardfight!! Vanguard, Selector Infected WIXOSS). Spinning-top and figure battles go to C11-3.

label: Esports & Video Game Anime
defn: A series about competitive video-gaming or puzzle contests played as a sport (Quanzhi Gaoshou, Bokura no Ame-iro Protocol, Phi Brain). Isekai trapped in a game world go to C3.

label: Spokon (Sports-Guts Anime)
defn: The Shōwa-era supōtsu konjō ('sports guts') cycle launched by Ikki Kajiwara's Kyojin no Hoshi: a sports series of brutal training, self-sacrifice and fighting spirit, chiefly 1968–1980s (Kyojin no Hoshi, Attack No.1, Ashita no Joe, Ace wo Nerae!, Tiger Mask). Later sports anime go to their sport (C7).

label: Detective & Mystery Anime
secs: 1=Meitantei Conan | 2=Teen & School Detectives | 3=Everyday Mysteries (Nichijou no Nazo) | 4=Occult & Supernatural Detectives | 5=Period & Historical Mysteries | 6=Procedural & Science-Fiction Investigations
defn: A series or film built on cases to solve: a detective, sleuthing student or investigator reasons from clues to a solution (Meitantei Conan, Hyouka, Kusuriya no Hitorigoto, Gosick). A thriller where the mind duel matters more than the solution goes to C8-2.

label: Psychological Thriller Anime
secs: 1=Duels of Wits & Manipulation | 2=Fractured Identity & Perception | 3=Conspiracy & Science-Fiction Paranoia | 4=Dark Adolescence
defn: A series or film whose suspense comes from minds under pressure — duels of wits, unstable identity, manipulation and paranoia (Death Note, Perfect Blue, Monster, Zankyou no Terror). A deadly game with rules goes to C8-3; supernatural dread goes to C9.

label: Death Game Anime
secs: 1=Gambling & Mind-Game Contests | 2=Death Games & Battle Royales
defn: A series in which characters are forced into a game whose losers die, are ruined or enslaved — battle royales, survival games and high-stakes gambling (Kaiji, Mirai Nikki, Danganronpa, Kakegurui). An open-ended mind duel without a game goes to C8-2.

label: Crime & Gangster Anime
secs: 1=Gentleman Thieves & Con Artists | 2=Mafia, Gangsters & Assassins | 3=Cops & Period Lawmen
defn: A series or film whose protagonists are criminals, thieves, gangsters or the cops who chase them (Lupin III, 91 Days, Baccano!, Banana Fish). A case-solving detective goes to C8-1.

label: War Anime
secs: 1=Home Front & Civilians | 2=Battlefield & Campaign Epics | 3=Espionage & Alternate-History War
defn: A series or film about a real or alternate-history war, its soldiers or its civilians (Hotaru no Haka, Hadashi no Gen, Kono Sekai no Katasumi ni, Kingdom). Space and mecha wars go to C2.

label: Historical Drama Anime
secs: 1=Japanese Period Drama (Jidaigeki) | 2=Chinese Historical Drama | 3=European & Other Historical Drama
defn: A series or film set in a recreated historical period, whose drama comes from that period's people and politics (Vinland Saga, Versailles no Bara, Heike Monogatari, Golden Kamuy). A war-centred story goes to C8-5.

label: Coming-of-Age Drama Anime
secs: 1=School-Youth Drama | 2=Grief & Healing | 3=Vocation & Adult Lives | 4=Family & Growing-Up Films | 5=Disaster & Survival Drama
defn: A drama, series or film whose subject is growing up — first loss, friendship, vocation, identity — resolved through an emotional arc (Ano Hi Mita Hana no Namae, Koe no Katachi, Sora yori mo Tooi Basho, Blue Period). Episodic daily life goes to C6; a romance-led story goes to C5.

label: Melodrama Anime
defn: A drama built to make the audience cry — terminal illness, lost memory, doomed love, shoujo hardship — often from nakige visual novels (Violet Evergarden, Little Busters!, Candy Candy, Kokoro Connect). A quieter coming-of-age arc goes to C8-7.

label: Medical Drama Anime
defn: A series about doctors, rescuers or the body as a hospital whose cases drive each episode (Black Jack, Young Black Jack, Megumi no Daigo).

label: Art Anime
secs: 1=Mushi Production Experiments & Animerama (1962–1973) | 2=Independent & Festival Shorts | 3=Auteur Features & Series
defn: An auteur or independent work valued for form over story — wordless, painterly or allegorical (Tenshi no Tamago, Kanashimi no Belladonna, Tsumiki no Ie, Mind Game).

label: Ghost Story Anime (Kaidan)
secs: 1=Anthology & Urban-Legend Shorts | 2=Haunted-School Horror | 3=Curse & Vengeance Horror | 4=Occult Investigators & Exorcists
defn: A horror series or film whose terror is a ghost, curse or urban legend in the tradition of the Japanese kaidan (Yami Shibai, Jigoku Shoujo, Another, Gakkou no Kaidan). A village cult or rural curse goes to C9-2.

label: Folk Horror Anime
defn: A horror series set in an isolated village or community whose customs, gods or rites are the danger (Higurashi no Naku Koro ni, Hikaru ga Shinda Natsu, Ookamikakushi).

label: Vampire Anime
defn: A horror series or film whose monster is the vampire (Blood+, Shiki, Kyuuketsuhime Miyu). Vampire romcoms go to C10-6.

label: Zombie Anime
defn: A horror series or film about the walking dead and the outbreak they cause (Highschool of the Dead, Biohazard: Degeneration, Gakkougurashi!).

label: Body Horror & Cosmic Horror Anime
defn: A horror series or film whose dread is the mutated body, the grotesque (ero guro) or an incomprehensible cosmic order (Uzumaki, Itou Junji: Collection, Elfen Lied, Pupa).

label: Comedy Horror Anime
defn: A series whose ghosts, curses or zombies are played for laughs as much as frights (Mieruko-chan, Zom 100, Jigoku Sensei Nube). Pure gag series with a monster mascot go to C10.

label: Gag Anime
secs: 1=Surreal & Absurdist Gag | 2=Slapstick & Manzai Gag | 3=Satirical Gag | 4=Short-Form & Flash Gag
defn: A comedy whose engine is the gag itself — non sequitur, slapstick, manzai timing, satire — with little or no plot (Nichijou, Poputepipikku, Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, Sayonara Zetsubou Sensei). Parody of a named work goes to C10-2; a spin-off of a non-comedy series goes to C10-3.

label: Parody Anime
secs: 1=Jidaigeki & Shounen Parody (Gintama) | 2=Genre & Media Parody | 3=Magical-Girl & Tokusatsu Parody | 4=National & Historical Parody
defn: A comedy whose jokes depend on the audience knowing the genre, franchise or history it mocks (Gintama, Hayate no Gotoku!, Haiyore! Nyaruko-san, Hetalia). A chibi spin-off of one specific series goes to C10-3.

label: Chibi Spin-off Anime
secs: 1=Chibi Theatres & Four-Panel Shorts | 2=Multi-Franchise Crossovers | 3=Omake, Specials & Picture Dramas
defn: A short comedy spin-off of a (usually non-comedy) series, often drawn super-deformed: theatre shorts, crossovers of several franchises, omake and picture dramas (Isekai Quartet, Carnival Phantasm, Sword Art Offline, Shingeki! Kyojin Chuugakkou). An original parody goes to C10-2.

label: School Comedy Anime
secs: 1=Student Council & Club Comedies | 2=Classroom & Deskmate Comedies | 3=Delinquent & Teacher Comedies | 4=Superpowered-Student Comedies | 5=Elementary-School Comedies
defn: A comedy whose jokes come from school life — classmates, the student council, a club, a teacher — rather than from a romance (Baka to Test to Shoukanjuu, Seitokai Yakuindomo, Tonari no Seki-kun, Saiki Kusuo no Psi-nan). A school romcom goes to C5; a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2.

label: Otaku Comedy Anime
defn: A comedy about otaku life — fandom, games, doujinshi, cosplay, shut-ins and their embarrassments (Himouto! Umaru-chan, Watashi ga Motenai no wa Dou Kangaetemo Omaera ga Warui!, Otaku no Video). An otaku club arc goes to C6-3.

label: Fantasy Comedy Anime
secs: 1=Demons & Gods Next Door | 2=Vampires, Youkai & Spirits | 3=Isekai & RPG-World Comedy | 4=Witches & Magic
defn: A comedy whose premise is a fantasy being or world — demons, gods, vampires, youkai, isekai heroes — dropped into absurd situations (Hataraku Maou-sama!, Hoozuki no Reitetsu, Saint Oniisan, Kono Healer, Mendokusai). A monster girl's quiet daily life goes to C6-10.

label: Science Fiction Comedy Anime
secs: 1=Alien Visitors & Invaders | 2=Robots, Androids & the Body | 3=Space Crews & Space-Opera Comedy | 4=Time Travel & Other Premises
defn: A comedy whose premise is science fiction — aliens, robots, time travel, space crews (Urusei Yatsura, Keroro Gunsou, Space Dandy, Hinamatsuri).

label: Action Comedy Anime
secs: 1=Martial-Arts Comedy | 2=Spy, Assassin & Ninja Comedy | 3=Delinquent (Yankii) & Yakuza Comedy | 4=Cop & Prison Comedy
defn: A comedy built on fights, missions or chases — martial artists, spies, ninja, cops, delinquents (Ranma 1/2, Spy x Family, Kyou kara Ore wa!!, Taiho Shichau zo).

label: Harem Comedy
secs: 1=Supernatural & Demon Harems | 2=Alien & Science-Fiction Harems | 3=Fantasy-World & Battle Harems | 4=Domestic & School Harems
defn: A comedy in which one protagonist is surrounded by several romantic candidates, usually with fanservice (To LOVE-Ru, High School DxD, Rosario to Vampire, Sekirei). Without the harem structure, fanservice comedy goes to C10-10; a romance-led story goes to C5.

label: Ecchi Anime
secs: 1=Fanservice Battle Anime | 2=Ecchi Comedies | 3=Fetish & Pin-up Shorts | 4=Sports Fanservice | 5=Mature & Taboo Ecchi
defn: A comedy or action series whose main appeal is sexual fanservice short of explicit sex (Prison School, Queen's Blade, Getsuyoubi no Tawawa, Keijo!!!!!!!!). With a harem structure it goes to C10-9; explicit erotica is out of scope.

label: Gender-Bender Anime
secs: 1=Sex-Change & Transformation Comedies | 2=Crossdressing (Josō) Comedies
defn: A comedy or romance whose engine is a character's change or concealment of sex: magical sex change and body transformation, or crossdressing (josō) passing (Ranma ½, Stop!! Hibari-kun!, Kämpfer, Princess Princess, Oniichan wa Oshimai!). Serious drama of gender identity goes to C8-7; body-swap romance to C5.

label: Kodomo Anime
secs: 1=Everyday Family Comedy | 2=Animal Tales & Fables | 3=Fantasy & Adventure for Children
defn: Anime made for young children and the family audience: household comedies, animal tales and gentle fantasy (Doraemon, Crayon Shin-chan, Sazae-san, Gamba no Bouken). Monster-collecting franchises go to C11-2.

label: Monster-Collecting Anime
secs: 1=Pokemon | 2=Digimon | 3=Other Monster-Partner Franchises
defn: A children's franchise in which kids befriend, collect and battle with monster partners, tied to games (Pokemon, Digimon Adventure, Youkai Watch).

label: Toy & Game Tie-in Anime
defn: A children's series made to sell a toy line or video game, whose battles are fought with the product (Bakuten Shoot Beyblade, Bakugan Battle Brawlers, Medarot, Rockman.EXE). Trading-card duels go to C7-13.

label: World Masterpiece Theater
defn: Nippon Animation's Sekai Meisaku Gekijou adaptations of Western children's classics and the kindred literary adaptations of the period (Akage no Anne, Flanders no Inu, Haha wo Tazunete Sanzenri, Muumin).

label: Early Japanese Animation
secs: 1=Meiji–Taishō Pioneers (1907–1926) | 2=Early Shōwa & Wartime Animation (1927–1945) | 3=Postwar to Early Tōei Dōga (1946–1963)
defn: Japanese animation from the silent era to the early 1960s, before television anime: folk-tale shorts, wartime propaganda, post-war shorts (Namakura Gatana, Momotarou: Umi no Shinpei, Kobutori).

label: Disney Animated Canon
secs: 1=Golden Age (1937–1942) | 2=Wartime Package Films (1942–1949) | 3=Silver Age (1950–1967) | 4=Bronze Age (1970–1988) | 5=Disney Renaissance (1989–1999) | 6=Post-Renaissance Era (2000–2009) | 7=Revival Era (2010– )
defn: A theatrical feature produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and counted in its official canon, hand-drawn or computer-animated (Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, The Lion King, Frozen). Disney direct-to-video sequels go to C12-10; Pixar to C12-3.

label: Traditional Animated Feature
secs: 1=American Features of the 1960s–1980s | 2=British Hand-Drawn Features | 3=Don Bluth Films | 4=Studio Rivals of the Disney Renaissance and After | 5=Fleischer Studios Features (1939–1941)
defn: A hand-drawn (cel) theatrical feature from an English-language studio other than Disney (The Secret of NIMH, Watership Down, The Iron Giant). European and other auteur hand-drawn features go to C12-18.

label: Pixar Films
defn: A feature produced by Pixar Animation Studios (Toy Story, WALL·E, Inside Out, Coco). Pixar short films go to C14-2.

label: DreamWorks Animation
secs: 1=Hand-Drawn Epics | 2=Shrek & Fairy-Tale Parody | 3=Talking-Animal Comedies | 4=Fantasy & Adventure Franchises | 5=High-Concept Comedies & Musicals
defn: A feature produced by DreamWorks Animation, from its hand-drawn epics to its computer-animated franchises (The Prince of Egypt, Shrek, Kung Fu Panda, How to Train Your Dragon). DreamWorks shorts and specials go to C14.

label: Computer-Animated Family Film
secs: 1=Illumination | 2=Blue Sky Studios | 3=Sony Pictures Animation | 4=Warner Bros. CG Features & Lego Films | 5=Paramount, Nickelodeon & Other Major-Studio Features | 6=Independent & Low-Budget American CG | 7=Streaming-Era Originals
defn: A computer-animated family feature from a Hollywood or American studio other than Disney, Pixar and DreamWorks (Despicable Me, Ice Age, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs, The Lego Movie). European, Latin American and Asian mainstream features go to C12-7; motion-capture films to C12-6.

label: Performance-Capture Animation
defn: A feature animated from motion- or performance-captured actors rather than keyframed (The Polar Express, Beowulf, The Adventures of Tintin). Rotoscoped films go to C12-17.

label: International Family Animated Feature
secs: 1=French, Belgian & British | 2=Nordic, Central & Southern European | 3=Russian & Ukrainian | 4=Latin American | 5=African & Asian
defn: A mainstream family feature (mostly computer-animated) from a European, Latin American, African or Asian studio outside the auteur circuit (Arthur and the Invisibles, Planet 51, Mavka: The Forest Song, BoBoiBoy: The Movie). Festival auteur features go to C12-18; Chinese features to C12-14.

label: Live-Action/Animated Film
defn: A feature combining live-action footage with animated characters, including photoreal 'live-action' remakes made wholly in CG (Who Framed Roger Rabbit, Space Jam, Cool World, The Lion King (2019)).

label: Television Spin-off Feature
secs: 1=Nicktoons Features | 2=Disney Television Features | 3=Cartoon Network Features | 4=Prime-Time & Adult Series Features | 5=Action & Fantasy Series Features
defn: A feature (theatrical, streaming or TV movie) continuing the cast and world of a specific animated series (The Simpsons Movie, The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, Futurama: Bender's Big Score). Scooby-Doo films go to C12-10; DC and Marvel films to C12-12.

label: Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
secs: 1=Disney Direct-to-Video Sequels | 2=Disney Fairies & Planes | 3=Scooby-Doo Films | 4=Other Franchise Sequels & TV Films
defn: A feature made for home video (later streaming) as a sequel to a theatrical film or as an entry of a long-running franchise (The Return of Jafar, Tinker Bell, Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island, The Land Before Time II).

label: Toy-Based Film
secs: 1=Barbie Fairy-Tale & Princess Films | 2=Barbie Fairy & Mermaid Films | 3=Barbie Contemporary Adventures | 4=Monster High & Ever After High | 5=Other Toy-Line Films
defn: A feature produced to extend a toy or doll line (Barbie in the Nutcracker, Monster High: Ghouls Rule!, Bionicle: Mask of Light, My Little Pony: Equestria Girls). Theatrical Lego films go to C12-5.

label: Superhero Animated Feature
secs: 1=DC Animated Universe Films | 2=Batman Films | 3=Superman, Wonder Woman & Green Lantern Films | 4=Justice League & Team Films | 5=Marvel & Spider-Verse Features
defn: An animated feature whose protagonists are comic-book superheroes, chiefly DC and Marvel (Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, Batman: Under the Red Hood, Justice League: The Flashpoint Paradox, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). Superhero comedies of a studio canon (The Incredibles) stay with C12-3.

label: Franco-Belgian Comics Adaptation
defn: An animated feature adapting a bande dessinée or Spanish historieta series (Asterix the Gaul, The Twelve Tasks of Asterix, Seven Crystal Balls and the Prisoners of the Sun). Sony's Smurfs films stay in C12-5.

label: Chinese Animation
secs: 1=Shanghai Animation Film Studio Classics (1941–1999) | 2=Contemporary Chinese Animation (2015–)
defn: A feature from the Chinese animation tradition (donghua), from the Shanghai Animation Film Studio classics to the 2010s revival (Havoc in Heaven, Big Fish & Begonia, Ne Zha).

label: Faith-Based Animated Film
defn: An animated feature made to retell scripture or religious narrative for devotional audiences (The Star, The King of Kings, Mahavatar Narsimha). DreamWorks' The Prince of Egypt stays in C12-4.

label: Stop-Motion Feature
secs: 1=Puppet & Silhouette Pioneers | 2=Aardman Features | 3=Selick & Burton Gothic | 4=Laika | 5=American & Australian Auteur Stop-Motion | 6=European & Latin American Auteur Stop-Motion
defn: A feature animated frame by frame with puppets, clay, cut-outs or objects (The Nightmare Before Christmas, Chicken Run, Coraline, My Life as a Zucchini).

label: Rotoscoped Feature
defn: A feature animated by tracing or painting over live-action footage (Waking Life, A Scanner Darkly, Loving Vincent, Bakshi's The Lord of the Rings).

label: Arthouse Animation
secs: 1=French & Belgian Auteur Animation | 2=Cartoon Saloon & British Arthouse | 3=Central & Eastern European | 4=Iberian & Latin American | 5=North American, Israeli & South Asian Independent | 6=Italian Auteur Animation | 7=East Asian Independent Animation
defn: An auteur-driven animated feature made for the festival and art-cinema circuit, usually outside the US studio system (The Triplets of Belleville, The Secret of Kells, Persepolis, Flow). Stop-motion auteur features go to C12-16; mainstream European family films to C12-7.

label: Adult Animation
secs: 1=Underground & Countercultural Features | 2=Adult Animated Comedy | 3=Adult Fantasy, Horror & Action
defn: An animated feature made for adults through explicit sex, violence or transgressive comedy (Fritz the Cat, Heavy Metal, Sausage Party, The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf). Adult auteur features go to C12-18; adult series features to C12-9.

label: Animated Documentary
defn: A non-fiction film told wholly or chiefly through animation: reconstructed memory, testimony or reportage drawn, painted or modelled instead of filmed (Waltz with Bashir, Flee, Ryan, The Sinking of the Lusitania). Live-action documentaries with animated inserts stay in A19.

label: Animated Sitcom
secs: 1=Prime-Time Family Sitcom | 2=Workplace & Ensemble Sitcom | 3=Teen & Coming-of-Age Sitcom | 4=Science-Fiction & Fantasy Sitcom | 5=Anthropomorphic Tragicomedy | 6=Children's & Teen Sitcom
defn: A situation comedy in animated form built on a fixed household, workplace or ensemble (The Simpsons, King of the Hill, Futurama, Daria). Adult Swim-style absurdist or shock comedy goes to C13-2; network-canon children's comedies to C13-7–C13-9.

label: Adult Animated Comedy
secs: 1=Parody & Repurposed-Cartoon Comedy | 2=Surreal & Absurdist Comedy | 3=Satire & Shock Comedy | 4=Genre & Action Spoof
defn: An animated comedy series for adults whose engine is parody, absurdism or shock rather than the sitcom household (Aqua Teen Hunger Force, Robot Chicken, South Park, Archer).

label: Adult Animated Action & Drama
secs: 1=Anthology Series | 2=Video-Game & Tabletop Adaptations | 3=Superhero & Comics Adaptations | 4=Myth & Historical Epics | 5=Science Fiction & Psychological Drama
defn: A non-comic animated series for adults: violent action, horror, epic or psychological drama (Æon Flux, Castlevania, Arcane, Invincible).

label: Saturday-Morning Cartoon
secs: 1=Theatrical-Cartoon Characters on Television | 2=Hanna-Barbera & Made-for-TV Comedies | 3=Scooby-Doo Series | 4=Licensed Comedies of the 1980s | 5=1990s Warner & Syndicated Comedies
defn: A comedy cartoon series made for US network or syndicated children's slots from the 1960s to the 1990s, including television packages and revivals of theatrical cartoon stars (The Bugs Bunny Show, The Yogi Bear Show, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!, Animaniacs). Action cartoons of the same slots go to C13-11–C13-13.

label: The Disney Afternoon
defn: A series of the Disney Afternoon syndicated block and its revivals (DuckTales, Chip 'n' Dale Rescue Rangers, Darkwing Duck, Gargoyles).

label: Nicktoons
defn: An original animated series of Nickelodeon's Nicktoons brand (Rugrats, The Ren & Stimpy Show, SpongeBob SquarePants, The Loud House). Nickelodeon's action series (Avatar) go to C13-13.

label: Cartoon Cartoons
secs: 1=Cartoon Cartoons (1995–2008) | 2=Later Cartoon Network Studios Originals
defn: An original series of Cartoon Network Studios, from the Cartoon Cartoons brand to its later creator-driven shows (Dexter's Laboratory, The Powerpuff Girls, Adventure Time, Steven Universe). Samurai Jack and DC series go to C13-13 and C13-11.

label: Disney Television Animation
defn: An original series of Disney Television Animation for Disney Channel, Disney XD or ABC, not based on a feature film (Recess, Phineas and Ferb, Gravity Falls, The Owl House). Feature spin-offs go to C13-10; Disney Junior series to C13-15.

label: Film Spin-off Series
secs: 1=Disney Feature Spin-offs | 2=Pixar & Disney+ Shorts Series | 3=DreamWorks Spin-offs | 4=Live-Action Film Spin-offs
defn: A series continuing the characters of a specific feature film (Lilo & Stitch: The Series, The Penguins of Madagascar, The Real Ghostbusters, Dug Days). Star Wars and superhero series go to their genre leaves.

label: Superhero Animated Series
secs: 1=DC Animated Universe | 2=Other DC Series | 3=Marvel Series | 4=Original Superheroes
defn: A series whose protagonists are costumed superheroes (Batman: The Animated Series, X-Men, Teen Titans, The Spectacular Spider-Man). Adult superhero series go to C13-3.

label: Toy-Based Animated Series
secs: 1=1980s Toy-Line Cartoons | 2=Toy-Line Revivals & Reboots | 3=Construction-Toy & Doll Lines
defn: A series created with or to sell a toy line, the 'program-length commercial' of 1980s syndication and its reboots (He-Man and the Masters of the Universe, The Transformers, G.I. Joe, My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic).

label: Action-Adventure Animated Series
secs: 1=Classic Adventure Serials | 2=Science-Fiction Franchise Series | 3=Martial-Arts & Ninja Series | 4=Teen Spy & Paranormal Series | 5=Gadget, Game & Sports Heroes | 6=Fantasy Quest Series
defn: A children's or family series built on adventure, quests and combat rather than gags (Jonny Quest, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, Avatar: The Last Airbender, Code Lyoko). Superhero and toy-line series go to C13-11 and C13-12.

label: European Children's Animated Series
secs: 1=Soviet & Russian | 2=Central European | 3=Western European
defn: A children's series from a European tradition, from Soyuzmultfilm and the Czech, Polish and Hungarian studios to British and French television (Well, Just You Wait!, The Adventures of the Mole, Bolek and Lolek, Oggy and the Cockroaches). European preschool series go to C13-15.

label: Preschool Animated Series
secs: 1=Storybook & Family-Life Series | 2=Curriculum & Mission Series | 3=Model & Stop-Motion Series
defn: A series made for children under six, built on gentle storytelling, curriculum or play (Little Bear, Dora the Explorer, Thomas & Friends, Bluey).

label: Educational Animated Series
defn: A series whose stated purpose is teaching a subject, from history to science and literacy (Schoolhouse Rock!, Once Upon a Time… Man, The Magic School Bus).

label: Theatrical Cartoon
secs: 1=Silent-Era Pioneers (1892–1927) | 2=Walt Disney Studio & Silly Symphonies | 3=Fleischer Studios | 4=Warner Bros. (Looney Tunes & Merrie Melodies) | 5=MGM Cartoon Studio (Avery, Hanna & Barbera) | 6=UPA & Postwar Modernism | 7=Independent & Late Theatrical Shorts
defn: A short made for cinema programmes by a studio or pioneer from the silent era to the end of the studio system (Gertie the Dinosaur, Steamboat Willie, Duck Amuck, What's Opera, Doc?).

label: Pixar Short Films
secs: 1=Graphics Group & Early Pixar | 2=Theatrical Pixar Shorts | 3=Franchise Shorts & SparkShorts
defn: A short produced by Pixar or its Lucasfilm Graphics Group precursor (Luxo Jr., Geri's Game, Bao, Jack-Jack Attack).

label: Studio Short Film
secs: 1=Walt Disney Animation Studios Shorts | 2=DreamWorks Animation Shorts | 3=Franchise Shorts from Television & Other Studios
defn: A post-studio-era short from a major animation studio or franchise, released theatrically, on home video or streaming (Paperman, Feast, Far Far Away Idol, The Longest Daycare).

label: Abstract Animation
defn: A short of non-figurative form, colour and rhythm, often drawn on film or set to music (Begone Dull Care, Motion Painting No. 1, Free Radicals). Figurative auteur shorts go to C14-5.

label: Auteur Animated Short
secs: 1=National Film Board of Canada | 2=Zagreb School & Central European | 3=Soviet, Russian & Estonian | 4=American Independent | 5=Western European Festival Shorts | 6=Latin American, African & Asian Auteurs
defn: An independent or state-studio art short driven by its maker's vision, the festival short (Neighbours, Hedgehog in the Fog, Rejected, The Windshield Wiper). Stop-motion art shorts go to C14-6.

label: Stop-Motion & Puppet Short
secs: 1=Stop-Motion Pioneers | 2=Czech Puppet & Object Animation | 3=Aardman & British Clay | 4=Contemporary Stop-Motion Auteurs | 5=Puppet Horror-Comedy | 6=Japanese Puppet Animation (Kawamoto Kihachirō)
defn: A short animated with puppets, clay or objects (The Cameraman's Revenge, Dimensions of Dialogue, The Wrong Trousers, Harvie Krumpet).

label: Animated Television Special
secs: 1=Classic Network Holiday Specials (1964–1979) | 2=Franchise & Storybook Specials
defn: A one-off animated programme made for television, typically a holiday special (A Charlie Brown Christmas, How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, The Gruffalo).

label: Soviet Animation
secs: 1=Socialist-Realist Fairy Tales (1936–1960) | 2=The Aesthetic Switch (1961–1968) | 3=Golden Collection Classics (1969–1991)
defn: The state-studio animation of the USSR, above all Soyuzmultfilm (Moscow) with Kievnauchfilm, Uzbekfilm and Ekran: fairy-tale features and shorts, satirical and modernist art shorts and the children's classics of its 'Golden Collection' (The Snow Queen, Film, Film, Film, Winnie-the-Pooh, Hedgehog in the Fog, Three from Prostokvashino). Soviet TV serials go to C13-14; Estonian and post-Soviet auteur shorts to C14-5.
